# Management-Governance Module — NU (Synthesis)

**Ticker:** NU (Nu Holdings Ltd.) · **Date:** 2026-09-06 · **Line read:** NYSE:NU Class A ordinary shares, USD · **Reporting:** IFRS, fiscal year ends 31 December · **Jurisdiction:** Cayman Islands incorporation, SEC foreign private issuer (Form 20-F is the proxy-equivalent), operating banks in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia · **Data pool:** `data/NU/` (citation label; all reads resolved inside the frozen extraction generation `f9081efa…09f2be`).

**Mode:** FULL run. All thirteen specialists (`00`–`12`) completed; zero agents failed; no declared-gap agent. The nine-component composite formula applies with **no substituted components** — every one of `07`–`12` produced a score. `balance-sheet-survival` did not run in this chain, so `10` and `11` proceeded on their own read of the pool and said so.

## Abstract

Nu Holdings is run by the founder who built it, and he is both heavily invested and unaccountable: he owns 18.6% of the economics and 74.4% of the votes through twenty-vote shares. Capital has created per-share value rather than size — book value per share rose 72.8% in eighteen months and retained profit earned roughly 29% incremental returns. Pay is small at 3.18% of net income, yet no performance metric or weight is disclosed for any award. The sharpest flag is structural, not criminal: chair and chief executive are one person, the founder picks five of nine directors, and minority holders cannot call a meeting. Competent, economically aligned stewards inside a rights architecture giving outsiders almost nothing.

---

## 1. Stewardship Verdict

- **Verdict:** **Aligned & competent** — and read the qualifier, because it does not travel without it. *Alignment* here is **economic** (an 18.6% founder stake worth ~US$13.0bn, zero pledging, related-party dealing at 0.58% of revenue) and *competence* is **delivered** (net income to parent −US$364.6m in FY2022 → US$3,607.1m TTM to Jun-2026; the Mexican banking licence obtained). The flags are **not minor**: they are structural minority-rights flags, and they are what caps the rating at Watchlist. This verdict must never be restated as "good governance" or "shareholder-friendly" — the board and the audit file are clean; the *rights architecture* is not.
- **NON-NEGOTIABLE GATE: PASS.** All four conditions tested on evidence rows: (1) `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` triggered no hard disqualifier; (2) zero Critical red flags fired in this module; (3) no controller, CEO, CFO or board chair is graded Disqualifying (25 persons swept: 22 Clean, 3 Minor concerns, 0 Material, 0 Disqualifying); (4) no material undisclosed legal or regulatory matter — A9-10 Green, with the one undisclosed item (a BCB fine of R$12,500 ≈ US$2,300, 0.00002% of net worth) failing the materiality threshold by four orders of magnitude. **Gate PASS is reported with 160 of 179 checklist items answered.**
- **Hard disqualifier flagged (business-model/01)?** **N.** Verbatim from that scan: *"No disqualifier triggered."* · *"Any disqualifier triggered: **N**"* · *"**No lock is applied here.** This scan clears NU on all eight hard tests only."*

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** the rights architecture is not a discount, it is a lock. A 20:1 dual class whose sunset needs Class B voting power below 10% against 84.2% today, a founder who designates and removes five of nine directors, a standing veto over dividends, share issues, mergers and officer pay, no shareholder right to nominate or to requisition a meeting, and a dormant staggered board that arms the moment founder control drops below 50% [`FY25 20-F, Item 10.B, pp.209, 214, 217–218`; `Item 6.A — Shareholder's Agreement, p.193`]. Shareholder friendliness scores 2 of 15 on voting rights for exactly this.
- **Strongest bull point (the steelman):** the conduct inside that architecture has been better than the architecture required. Independence is 77.8% when the controlled-company exemption required none; the audit committee is 100% independent and chaired by a designated financial expert who is a former PwC audit partner; the related-party balance is **US$265 thousand** at 30-Jun-2026 (0.0015% of total liabilities); there is **no royalty, no promoter loan, no ICD, no pledge and no related-party M&A across a ten-year sweep**; and the founder handed back a **US$422.6m** contingent share award and up to 2% of dilution for no consideration in 2022 [`05` §1, §4; `09` A5-02/03/04/09; `FY24 20-F, Item 6.E, p.288`].
- **Single killer risk:** the founder's veto meets a credit cycle. Non-performing loans have risen every year (6.7% → 7.8% → 7.9% → 8.6% of loans) while the Tier 1 ratio fell 16.2% → 14.4% → 13.4%, and the company began repurchasing stock inside that trend with US$28.8bn of undrawn card limits off balance sheet [`02` §3]. If capital has to be conserved against minority interests, no outside holder has a mechanism.
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** three items cut against the bear case and are recorded, not buried — the buyback was executed at an average of about **US$12.31**, below the contemporaneous price, and reduced the share count 0.51%; the CFO succession was pre-announced six weeks ahead with a named successor and a transition to 2026-08-31; and both 2026 AGM resolutions passed with **96.23%** of votes cast, with no proxy-advisor campaign found [`02`; `01` §2; `SEC Form 6-K, AGM results Ex-99.1, filed 2026-08-07`].
- **What would flip the verdict down:** a second unannounced senior departure, or the Q3'26 print showing the non-performing ratio and the Tier 1 ratio diverging further while repurchases continue.

## 3. Reconciliation

Five items were routed to this synthesis for adjudication rather than inheritance, plus two disagreements found in the fidelity pass.

**A. `07`'s RF-NET-003 cap on People & network integrity — is the linkage "live"? Adjudicated: YES, the cap stands at 50.** `07` capped itself at 50 and asked me to decide. The band-(b) trigger names *"an admitted insolvency or liquidation proceeding … live enforcement, or a credible fraud allegation."* Grupo Casas Bahia's *recuperação judicial* is Brazil's judicial reorganisation — the local equivalent of an admitted insolvency proceeding — filed by the debtor itself on/around **2026-08-16**, quantified at **R$17.3bn** across ten group companies, **three weeks before this report's as-of date and unresolved**. The reported departure of Calderón from that board *after* the filing does not extinguish a linkage that was live at the filing date and is live now, and treating a same-week exit as severance would reward exactly the timing the "smart rat" test exists to catch (`07` correctly found that test does **not** fire here, because he left *after* the event, not ahead of it, and there is no second company). The cap binds: **People & network integrity 50, Governance risk floor 55, no rating above "Watchlist."** ⚠ **Carry the basis at every layer (§3):** *no adverse record was found against this person on any swept axis* — he is a former PwC audit partner, a Brazilian registered accountant, and Nu's designated audit-committee financial expert; the grade reflects the linkage, never a record against him. I also affirm `07`'s adjudication that the flag fires **once**, on Calderón, and **not** on Douglas Leone: Sequoia's FTX exposure is a **pleading-stage private civil claim against an investor that lost US$210m to someone else's fraud**, with no regulator, no admission and no adverse ruling — a Minor exposure floor, not a band-(b) fact.

**B. The CFO attribution conflict — `06` is right; `01` and `earnings/04` are corrected.** `01` and `earnings/04_guidance-consensus` both attribute the Q1'26 effective-tax-rate and risk-adjusted-NIM guides to **CFO Rob Livingston**. The **verbatim Q1 2026 transcript (2026-05-14) names Guilherme Marques do Lago as CFO** and records zero occurrences of "Livingston" — Livingston's appointment was effective **2026-07-13**, two months after that call. **The guides were given by the outgoing CFO, Lago.** The substance of both promise tests is unchanged (the numbers, the dates and the outcomes are the same), so `01`'s 65 and `06`'s 69 stand. The candor point sharpens rather than softens: **the outgoing CFO set the guide, and the incoming CFO ran the call on which it was missed and left unmentioned** — a handover boundary is exactly where a quietly-dropped guide is easiest to lose. Every downstream reference must name Lago.

**C. `04`'s RF-OWN-004 instruction — accepted in full.** §24 Filter 6 was tested and is **negative**: state-owned shares 0.03%, one reported segment = 100% of revenue, and Nu is the top holding company, not a listed subsidiary of a value-maximising parent. **RF-OWN-004 is NOT emitted; the Filter-6 Shareholder-friendliness cap of 55 and Governance-risk floor of 55 are NOT applied, and no value-trap note goes to the valuation module.** Shareholder friendliness scores 50 on its own evidence, below the cap that does not apply — so the number is earned, not imposed. Findings **04-015 (20:1 dual class) and 04-016 (55.8pp wedge) are one fact and are priced once**, in the Governance-risk read; they appear as two checklist rows (A3-04, A3-03) because the registry tests them separately, not because the penalty is taken twice. A founder-controller who built the business and holds 18.6% of the economics is not the structurally unaligned owner §24 Filter 6 describes — but he *is* an entrenchment problem, and that is priced under Shareholder friendliness and Governance risk instead.

**D. The unannounced-departure cluster — `01` and `05` are the same finding, and together they are worse than either alone.** `01` found the **President & COO (Lahrech)** and the **CTO (Olivier)** vanished between the FY24 and FY25 20-F with no announcement. `05` independently found two more: **David Marcus lost his independence designation** between the same two filings while staying on the Compensation and People Committee (dropping it to 3-of-4 independent), and **Daniel Krepel Goldberg** — an independent director from April 2021 who became a permanent observer of the Audit and Risk Committee in December 2023 — **vanished between the FY23 and FY24 20-F**. That is **four unannounced senior status changes across three filing years: two executives gone, one director gone, one director's independence silently dropped.** No single one is Red. The pattern is a **disclosure-completeness habit**, not four coincidences, and it is why Disclosure candor is held at 69 rather than higher and A1-09 is Amber rather than Green. Reconciled view: the more conservative reading is adopted — this is a repeated practice, and the follow-up is whether the FY2026 20-F names a President/COO or confirms the role is eliminated.

**E. The two RF-DISC-001 / RF-DISC-002 uses — reconciled; three distinct fires, no double count.** They are different facts, correctly tagged, and I record them separately: (i) **`06` fired RF-DISC-002** on recurring "one-off" add-backs — share-based compensation, a cost present in every period on record (US$212.6m / US$272.4m / US$271.8m / US$216.8m H1'26), added back to Adjusted Net Income every year, plus a CSLL tax remeasurement management called *"a nonrecurring one-off event"* (+US$58.5m FY2025) that recurred the next period (+US$28.4m H1'26); **`06` explicitly tested RF-DISC-001 and did NOT fire it** — the defect is omission of the tax line, not an assertion the numbers contradict. (ii) **`10` fired RF-DISC-001** on a different fact entirely: a **14.0× gap** between the Note 25(d) figure of US$92,738k and the related narrative, i.e. commentary that does not reconcile to the note it points at — compounded by the FY2025 20-F signposting readers to "note 23" when the contingency note is note 25. (iii) **`10` also fired RF-CL-001** on the GMF placement defect. Reconciled: **RF-DISC-002 (from `06`) and RF-DISC-001 (from `10`) both stand as separate rows in the Red-Flag Register**; neither is inherited into the other agent's score, and `06`'s not-fired RF-DISC-001 is recorded as tested-and-not-fired so a downstream reader does not read `10`'s fire as `06`'s.

**F. Triage's anticipated sweep cap vs what the sweeps actually did — the specialists win.** `00` recorded that every network host was denied in this runtime and pre-declared **People & network integrity max 65, Legal & regulatory risk floor 40, Confidence max 70**. `07` ran and logged 68-subject discovery plus per-person sweeps with dated web citations; `12` ran and logged twelve company-level sweeps; `05` obtained the **AGM 6-K (filed 2026-08-07)** that triage named its single highest-value missing document. Reconciled on the evidence rows, not on the anticipation: **that cap does not bind.** A narrower, real coverage limit is priced instead — no primary Cayman registry pull (the register is non-public), no paid Brazilian court-docket terminal, no certified consolidated-sanctions query, no partner-level PCAOB sweep, and ~65 named subjects in `07`'s declared breadth overflow. Those are what hold Confidence at 76 rather than higher.

**G. The one number where two agents could have disagreed and do not.** `10`'s ~22.1%-of-net-worth GMF figure and `12`'s A9-10 Green look opposed. They are not: `10` says the claim is **disclosed but in the wrong place** (Item 8.A, not Note 25(c)); `12` says it **is disclosed somewhere in the filing**, which is what A9-10 tests. Both are right, and the conservative composite is the one adopted: **no undisclosed material litigation (gate condition 4 not tripped), but a real placement-and-completeness defect (RF-CL-001, High).**

No other material disagreements between specialists.

## 5. Stewardship Summary

**(a) Have they delivered on promises and created per-share value?** Mostly, on a sample the company itself keeps thin. Six promises were specific and dated enough to test: two kept (the risk-adjusted interest margin after credit losses recovered from 9.5% to 12.4%, past the level promised; the Mexican banking licence obtained roughly three years after application), one missed (the 15–20% effective tax rate, delivered at 14.2% and then dropped from the script), one missed for six quarters then met, one open and currently running better than guided, one not assessable. The delivered record behind that is not thin at all: net income to parent went from −US$364.6m (FY2022) to US$3,607.1m (TTM to Jun-2026), diluted earnings per share from −US$0.08 to US$0.734, and book value per share up 72.8% in eighteen months to US$2.743, with retained profit earning about 29.2% incremental returns. That is per-share value, not size — but it has never been tested through a credit downturn, and non-performing loans have risen every year (6.7% → 8.6%) while the Tier 1 capital ratio fell 16.2% → 13.4%.

**(b) Do incentives and ownership point at per-share value or at size?** Ownership does, emphatically; pay does neither. The founder's 18.6% economic stake (~US$13.0bn) is roughly **142 times the entire annual pay pool** and is unpledged, so his dominant incentive is the share price, not the salary — and in 2022 he surrendered a US$422.6m contingent award and up to 2% of dilution for no consideration. The formal incentive plan, though, attaches **no metric and no weight to any award**: bonuses rest on undisclosed "pre-established business goals" and long-term awards are time-vested RSUs. Nothing in it is size-based either — there is no revenue, EBITDA, headcount or deal metric anywhere — so the plan is best described as *absent*, not perverse. Aggregate pay of US$91.3m is 3.18% of net income and fell 4.9% while profit rose 45.6%.

**(c) Are minority shareholders protected, and is management candid when results are bad?** Protected, no. Candid, mostly yes. The rights architecture is the weakest part of this company's governance by a distance: 20 votes per Class B share with an unreachable sunset, five of nine directors designated by the founder, a standing veto over dividends, share issues, mergers and officer pay, no right to nominate or requisition, an exclusive Cayman forum, and a staggered board that arms the moment founder control drops below 50%. Voting rights score 2 of 15. On candor the evidence runs the other way: management volunteered an 8.2% margin trough with a basis-point decomposition before being asked, talked down its own record-low 17.6% cost ratio as "not a run rate" and was proved right one quarter later, and itemised three one-offs — two of them negatives — in answer to a hard question. What holds candor at 69 is that **the selectivity runs one way**: the guide being beaten was reiterated; the guide missed to the flattering side was never mentioned again, in the quarter the tax line produced 96.7% of the earnings beat. And four senior status changes across three filing years went unannounced.

**(d) The single most important reason to trust — or not trust — this team with capital.** Trust: the *conduct* inside a structure that required none of it. Independence is 77.8% when the controlled-company exemption required zero, the audit committee is 100% independent under a real financial expert, the related-party balance is **US$265 thousand**, there is no royalty, no promoter loan, no pledge, no related-party acquisition in ten years, no restatement in five, and five consecutive unqualified audit opinions. Not-trust: none of that is **enforceable** by an outside holder, and the same person decides whether it continues. Everything good here is a choice the founder is currently making, and a choice is not a protection.

## 7. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- **The stewardship verdict is "Aligned & competent," and the single strongest piece of evidence for it is conduct the structure did not require:** independence at 77.8% when the controlled-company exemption required zero, a 100%-independent audit committee, a related-party balance of **US$265 thousand** at 30-Jun-2026, and a founder who handed back a **US$422.6m** contingent award and up to 2% of dilution for no consideration. **Do not harden that verdict into "good governance" or "shareholder-friendly"** — the flags are not minor, they are structural minority-rights flags, and they are what caps the rating.
- **Non-Negotiable Gate: PASS**, computed from all four conditions with 160/179 items answered. No hard disqualifier, zero Critical red flags, zero Disqualifying grades on any controller/CEO/CFO/chair, and no material undisclosed legal matter (A9-10 Green; the one undisclosed item is a R$12,500 BCB fine, 0.00002% of net worth).
- **Capital allocation created per-share value, not size:** diluted EPS −US$0.08 (FY2022) → US$0.734 (LTM Jun-26), book value per share +72.8% in eighteen months to US$2.743, retained profit earning ~29.2% incremental returns, and a first buyback executed at ~US$12.31 average that cut the share count 0.51%. **Carry the qualifier:** the record is short and the credit book has never been through a downturn — non-performing loans have risen every year (6.7% → 8.6%) while Tier 1 fell 16.2% → 13.4%, and repurchases began inside that trend.
- **Incentives and ownership point in opposite directions.** Ownership aligns him hard: 18.6% of the economics, ~US$13.0bn, **142× the entire annual pay pool**, zero pledged. The formal plan aligns nobody: **zero named metrics and zero weights** on any award. Nothing is size-based either — the plan is absent, not perverse. Pay is 3.18% of net income and fell while profit rose 45.6%.
- **The people read:** 25 persons swept — **22 Clean, 3 Minor concerns, 0 Material, 0 Disqualifying**. The riskiest is **Rogério Calderón, chair of the Audit and Risk Committee — Minor concerns on an exposure floor, with no adverse record against him personally**; the grade reflects his seat at Grupo Casas Bahia S.A., in judicial reorganisation over R$17.3bn since ~2026-08-16. **No open §24 Filter 1 signal exists** — `business-model/01` routed nothing and RF-MGT-005 is not emitted by any agent.
- **The checklist read: 89.4% coverage (160/179), 10 Reds.** They cluster in exactly two places — **board control** (chair=CEO, no independent chair, three IDs with independence concerns, one director on 11 boards) and **ownership structure** (20:1 dual class, 55.8pp wedge) — plus four singletons (KPMG firm discipline, the dropped tax guide, the Colombia claim's placement, the Casas Bahia linkage). **The binding Checklist Risk is Contingent-liability risk at 32** (`10`), the worst of the four; RPT 22, forensics 31, legal 15.
- **Biggest governance risk:** the founder's 74.4%-vs-18.6% wedge plus a veto over dividends, share issues, M&A and officer pay that survives until Class B voting power falls below 10% (84.2% today). Severity: **High, structural, permanent on any realistic horizon.** Everything else in this module is conduct that could change tomorrow at his discretion.
- **Hard disqualifier from `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` — verbatim: *"No disqualifier triggered."* · *"Any disqualifier triggered: N."* · *"No lock is applied here. This scan clears NU on all eight hard tests only."***
- **§24 rejector filters: none tripped.** Filter 1 (integrity) — nothing routed, no cap. Filter 2 (turnaround) — not a turnaround, RF-MGT-004 not emitted, no cap. Filter 4 (serial acquirer) — US$131.9m over five years, RF-CAP-004 not emitted, no cap. **Filter 6 (unaligned owner) — tested and NEGATIVE by `04`: RF-OWN-004 is NOT emitted, so no Shareholder-friendliness cap of 55, no Governance-risk floor of 55 from that source, and NO VALUE-TRAP NOTE goes to valuation.** Shareholder friendliness is 50 on its own evidence, below a cap that does not apply.
- **Partial-data caps: exactly two, both from `07`, both pointing at one score.** RF-NET-003 band (b) cuts People & network integrity from a raw 77 to **50**, floors Governance risk at **55**, and holds the rating at **Watchlist**. The declared breadth overflow (~65 named subjects) caps Confidence at 80 (applied: **76**). Real coverage limits that are priced but not capped: no primary Cayman registry pull (regime fact, not opacity), no paid court-docket or certified sanctions query, no PCAOB partner-level sweep (no partner is named in any filing), 15 E-B entities scoped not swept. **Triage's anticipated "sweep did not run" cap does NOT bind — both sweeps ran and are logged.**
- **Two attribution corrections to carry forward:** (i) the Q1'26 effective-tax-rate and NIM guides were given by **outgoing CFO Guilherme Marques do Lago**, not Rob Livingston — `01` and `earnings/04` have this wrong and the verbatim transcript is decisive; (ii) `10`'s ~22.1%-of-net-worth GMF figure is a **bound on a gross claim against 52 defendants jointly, not Nu's exposure** — every *measured* contingent liability is 0.352% of net worth.
- **Biggest missing data point (one item):** the **2026 AGM poll tallies split between founder and public shareholders**. The 6-K discloses 96.23% for the nine-director slate, but not the public-only split — in a company where one person holds 74.4% of the votes, that split is the only direct measure of minority sentiment, and it would turn A10-03 from an Amber derivation into a real answer.
- **Explicit handoff: this module SUPERSEDES the `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance` quick-read.** Where they overlap, the master synthesizer must treat **this module's governance verdict and scores as the primary governance read** — Governance Score 60, Confidence-Adjusted 46, Rating **Watchlist**, Gate **PASS**, 6 red flags / 0 Critical.
- **Boundary respected:** no fair value, no probabilities, no risk/reward, no rating in the §18 decision set, no sizing. The one number this module hands the valuation module is a **negative**: Filter 6 does not trip, so no value-trap discount is warranted on ownership grounds.

## 8. Simple Summary

- **Promises: mostly kept, on a sample the company keeps deliberately small.** Two of six testable promises were kept, one was missed, one was missed for six quarters then met. Nu publishes no revenue, profit or cost guidance at all, so it cannot miss targets it never sets.
- **Capital has created value per share, not just size.** Earnings per share went from −US$0.08 to US$0.734; book value per share is up 72.8% in eighteen months; retained profit earns about 29 cents on each extra dollar of equity. The first buyback was well priced at about US$12.31.
- **The pay plan rewards nothing in particular.** Not one performance measure or weight is attached to any award — bonuses rest on undisclosed goals and long-term awards are just time-vested shares. It is not an empire-building plan either; it is an absent one. Total pay is small: 3.18% of profit, and it fell while profit rose 45.6%.
- **Skin in the game is exceptional; buying is not.** Insiders own 22% of the company, the founder alone 18.6% (~US$13.0bn) with **nothing pledged**. But in the observed window there were **zero open-market purchases and four sales** (net ~US$9.0m) — every sale after results, never before.
- **Minority shareholders are not protected.** The founder has 74.4% of the votes on 18.6% of the money, picks five of nine directors, and can veto dividends, share issues, takeovers and executive pay. Outside holders cannot call a meeting or nominate anyone.
- **Management is mostly candid when results are bad — with one repeatable exception.** It volunteered its worst margin before being asked and talked down its own best cost number. But the tax-rate promise it *missed* in a flattering direction was never mentioned again, in the very quarter the tax line produced almost the entire profit beat. Four senior people changed status across three years with no announcement.
- **No hard disqualifier was flagged.** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` cleared all eight tests: *"No disqualifier triggered."* Six red flags fired in this module, **none Critical**, and the governance gate **passes**.
- **This module is useful for the master synthesizer:** 89% checklist coverage on primary filings with zero extraction failures, and it supersedes the earlier one-page governance read.

**LEAD for `07` (recorded here, not concluded here).** The **claimed founding year (2013) predates the incorporation date of the listed entity (26 February 2016) by about three years**, and the filings disclose no predecessor by name. On its face the gap is explained by the Brazilian operating company having started in 2013 and a Cayman holding company being interposed in 2016 — but that is a hypothesis, not a finding. `07` runs the **D-2 lineage test (A17-02)** to confirm or reconcile it: identify which entity actually began in 2013 (Nu Pagamentos S.A. is the obvious candidate, CIQ 280438260), establish its own incorporation date and any former names, and check whether that lineage is disclosed anywhere in the filings. **Do not treat this as evidence that an undisclosed predecessor exists** — a truthfully-cited group history is not a finding. A second, smaller lead: the **registered office is a corporate-services provider's address (Campbells)**, which is standard for a Cayman exempted company and will produce a very large co-address cluster — `07` should expect it and must not treat that cluster as an A17-05 signal without a corroborated second link.

## 6. Sufficiency Verdict

- **Verdict:** **Sufficient**
- **Reason:** The foreign-private-issuer proxy-equivalent (FY25 Form 20-F Items 6, 7 and 16A–16K), a current beneficial-ownership table with Form 4 insider transactions to 2026-08-26, board composition with committee membership and a quantified related-party note, and five consecutive audited years plus M&A, offering and capitalisation histories are all present with zero extraction failures — so all twelve specialists have primary material to work from.
- **Specialists that can run:** all twelve — management track record (01), capital allocation (02), incentives (03), ownership (04), board and shareholder rights (05), candor (06), people dossiers (07 — filings-graded and coverage-limited), audit quality (08), RPT and group forensics (09), contingent liabilities (10), accounting forensics (11), regulatory/legal (12 — coverage-limited).
- **Hard disqualifier already flagged by `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`?** **N.** All eight hard tests cleared; "No disqualifier triggered" and no verdict lock applied. Two items were explicitly routed to THIS module and must be picked up rather than re-adjudicated: (a) the **CFO succession effective 2026-07-13** — pre-announced, outgoing CFO retained as advisor to the audit and risk committee, no restatement, no auditor change, no qualified opinion; (b) **open-market insider selling** — `ciq_facts.json` net −592,707 shares (0 buys / 4 sells) TTM to 2026-08-18 against all-types net +4,015,012. Neither is a disqualifier; both are this module's to read.
- **Active caps (these bind even though the verdict is Sufficient — the synthesis must apply them):**
  - **Web / legal-database sweep did not run.** Every network host is denied in this runtime (`deniedHosts: ["*"]`), so no registry, court, regulator, insolvency, disqualification, sanctions, trademark or dated-adverse-media source was reachable. `07` and `12` are **coverage-limited: graded on filings alone and never presented as swept-and-clean**. **People & network integrity max 65; Legal & regulatory risk floor 40; Confidence Score max 70.**
  - **Discovery loop may be unrunnable (conditional on `07`'s own reachability test).** D-1 (company website) is unreachable from here, as are D-2 through D-5. If `07` also reaches nothing, it records **A17-01 Insufficient Data naming exactly what failed** and applies **People & network integrity max 60; Confidence Score max 75**, sweeping the §5E seed roster anyway and reporting the result as a statement about the filings, not about the company. If `07` CAN reach sources, this cap does not bind.
  - **Individual compensation and pay metrics not disclosed.** `03` answers **A6-02, A6-03 and A6-05 as Not Available**, giving the reason (Cayman law does not require individual disclosure; FPI exemption), and scores incentive alignment on structure alone with stated reduced confidence. The blanket "no compensation disclosure" cap does not bind, because a disclosure exists.
  - **No AGM vote tallies.** `05` answers **A10-03 Not Available** and must not read the absence of a reported dispute as support.
  - **RPT counterparty unnamed.** `09` quantifies the amount from Note 28 and records the counterparty as Not Available; the non-naming is itself a disclosure observation for `09` and `06`.
  - **Recently listed (IPO Dec-2021).** Every checklist item needing 3–5 years of listed history is **Not Applicable (insufficient listed history)** — never a Red, never a silent Green.
- **Critical missing items:** none that block a specialist. The four real gaps, in order of what they cost: (1) reachable legal, regulatory and registry databases; (2) AGM voting results; (3) per-individual compensation with metrics and weights; (4) the name of the related-party counterparty in Note 28(a)(i).
- **Single highest-value missing document:** **the 6-K reporting the results of the 2026-08-06 AGM** — the poll tallies on the reelection of all nine directors and on the ratification of the FY2025 accounts. In a company where one person controls 74.4% of the votes, how the *public* shareholders voted is the only direct measure of minority sentiment available, and it is the single input that would turn A10-03 from Not Available into a real answer.

**Founder / owner-operator status.** Yes, and to an unusual degree. David Vélez Osorno founded the business in 2013, still runs it, and also controls it: he beneficially owns **88.3% of the Class B ordinary shares**, and Class B carries **20 votes per share**, giving him **74.3–74.4% of total voting power**, largely through Rua California Ltd., a company he owns 100% of (`FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A (Major Shareholders) and fn.2/fn.4`; `Item 10.B`). Co-founder Cristina Junqueira is still an executive and holds Class A and Class B shares carrying about 9.9% of votes (`FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A, fn.3`). This is an owner-operated company in the literal sense — the CEO cannot be removed by the public shareholders. The alignment and minority-rights consequences of that structure are owned by `04_ownership-and-insider-behavior` and `05_board-and-shareholder-rights`; it appears here only because it is what makes CEO succession a governance question rather than a board decision.

He is in the management-team table of the FY24 20-F (filed 2025-04-16), speaks on the **Q1 2025 call (2025-05-13)**, and then **disappears**: he is absent from every call from **Q2 2025 (2025-08-14)** onward and absent from the FY25 20-F management table (filed 2026-04-08). **No announcement, no stated reason, and no successor appear anywhere in the pool**, and the President/COO role has not been refilled. **Flagging the warning plainly.** The CFO change is orderly and well handled and does not trip the sudden-CFO-resignation flag. What does deserve a flag is different and easy to miss: **the President & Chief Operating Officer — the company's number two, who had personally presented asset quality on the earnings calls for years — left with no announcement, no stated reason and no replacement, and the same is true of the CTO.** A departure the company simply does not mention is a disclosure gap in its own right. It is graded Amber, not Red, because nothing in the pool ties either exit to a financial, legal or accounting event, and because the roster changes coincide with genuine expansion (a US build-out, a new product tier, a Mexican bank licence) rather than with distress.

## 3. Stated Strategy & Targets

Management's stated plan is to keep compounding a single business — a low-cost digital bank — along three lines: grow the customer base and deepen it (the "Nu Ecosystem"), extend the same model across Brazil, Mexico and Colombia, and lay the foundation for a US launch (`FY25 Form 20-F, Item 4, "Our Growth Strategies"`; `Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, Aug-13-2026, prepared remarks`). The economics they say drive it are an average revenue per active customer that rises with cohort age while cost to serve stays "at or below $1 per customer" (`Q1 2025 earnings-call transcript, May-13-2025, prepared remarks`).

**On explicit, checkable targets, there are almost none, and that is itself the finding.** The 20-F's strategy section contains no numeric multi-year target — no revenue, margin, return, leverage or customer goal. The company issues **no revenue, EPS, EBITDA or capex guidance at all**, and said so on the record when asked for a growth number: *"I won't necessarily give you a specific number of growth"* (`Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, Aug-13-2026, Q&A — David Vélez`; corroborated by `earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md`). The only explicit numbers management has put a period against are three call-derived modelling parameters — a **full-year 2026 efficiency ratio of "approximately 20%"**, an **IFRS effective tax rate of 15–20% for the remainder of 2026**, and a **cap of "less than 100 basis points" of efficiency-ratio drag from US investment in each of 2026 and 2027** — plus a qualitative statement that the current risk-adjusted net interest margin (interest margin after credit losses) is sustainable (`Q1 2026 earnings-call transcript, May-14-2026, prepared remarks`; `Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, Aug-13-2026, prepared remarks and Q&A`). A management team that publishes no targets cannot miss them; it also cannot be held to them. That structurally limits how much of the promise-vs-delivery test below can bite.

**Scoreboard.** Six promises were specific and dated enough to test. **Two kept** (risk-adjusted NIM recovery; Mexican banking licence). **One missed** (the tax-rate range, on the first quarter it was tested, and then dropped from the script). **One missed for six quarters then met** (the 2023 credit-expansion claim). **One still open and currently running better than guided** (the FY26 efficiency ratio). **One not assessable** (the S-2 reclassification). Against that, the delivered record on profit and scale is unambiguous. The honest summary is **mixed-to-good, on a thin sample** — thin because the company deliberately publishes almost nothing that can be scored.

## 5. Management Read

The people running NU are the people who built it: a founder-CEO of thirteen years who controls 74.4% of the votes, a co-founder still in an executive seat, and a risk officer of eight years — sitting alongside a bench that has been rebuilt at speed, with five of the nine officers named in the FY25 20-F (plus the CFO and the product officer appointed since) under about fifteen months in post. The delivered record is real and not in dispute: profit to parent has gone from a US$364.6m loss in FY2022 to US$3,607.1m over the twelve months to June 2026, risk-adjusted NIM has recovered from 8.2% to 12.4%, and the Mexican banking licence that was applied for in 2023 was granted in August 2026. Where explicit promises exist they are few and mostly met — the exception being the tax-rate range, which was missed on its first test and then dropped from the script.

The single biggest management signal is a negative one, and it is about disclosure rather than performance: **the President & Chief Operating Officer, the CEO's number two and the executive who personally presented asset quality on the earnings calls, left between the Q1 2025 and Q2 2025 calls with no announcement, no stated reason and no successor — and the Chief Technology Officer went the same way — while the one seat that functioned as a deputy was quietly eliminated in a company where no shareholder vote can change the CEO.** That is not evidence of wrongdoing; it is evidence that this company does not tell you when its most senior people leave, which is precisely the thing an outside holder cannot check for themselves.

Promise-vs-delivery is therefore built from prepared remarks and Q&A on six dated statements, not from a target framework. # Capital-Allocation Scorecard — NU

**Company:** Nu Holdings Ltd. · **Line read:** NYSE:NU Class A ordinary shares, USD · **Date:** 2026-09-06
**Jurisdiction (CLAUDE.md §27):** Cayman Islands incorporation, US **foreign private issuer**. The annual filing is **Form 20-F**, not a 10-K; there is no DEF 14A and no 8-K. Material events surface in 6-K/press releases (captured here through the `CIQ Key Developments export`) and in the interim condensed financial statements. The absence of a US domestic form is not missing data.
**Reporting standard:** IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB. **Reporting currency: US dollars (USD).** Financial-statement figures are in **thousands of USD** in the filings; this report converts them to **millions (US$m)** and says so in each table. **Fiscal year ends 31 December.**
**Evidence base:** the supervisor-frozen extraction generation only, cited logically as `data/NU/`. No web source was used.
**Upstream inputs read:** `management-governance/01_management-and-track-record.md`; `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` (the quick-read this deepens and supersedes); `earnings/01_historical-financials.md`.

**Two basis warnings that govern every number below (CLAUDE.md §15).**
1. **There are two different operating-cash-flow bases for this company and they differ by roughly US$13bn a year.** The **company-basis (IFRS, as filed)** cash-flow statement puts the increase in customer deposits *inside* operating activities; the **Capital IQ bank-template** export moves that deposit inflow *out* of operating and into financing. Worked reconciliation, FY2025: 3,500.5 (company) − 12,861.3 (deposit inflow) = **−9,360.8**, which is exactly the CIQ figure [S9][S21]. **This report uses the company (filed) basis for every "% of CFO" figure and labels it every time.** The CIQ figure is shown alongside where relevant, never mixed into the same row.
2. **Return on invested capital in the normal `Δ NOPAT / Δ invested capital` form is not computable for this company.** There is no EBITDA, no EBIT and no interest-expense line on the bank template — `ciq_facts.json` records `ltm_ebitda_m` as `unknown` with the note "Income Statement sheet has no 'EBITDA' row" [S18]. The bank-appropriate substitute, **Δ net income to parent ÷ Δ total equity**, is used and is labelled as that substitute wherever it appears. It is not a NOPAT-based ROIC and must not be quoted as one.

## 1. Uses of Capital (3–5 years)

**Window: FY2021 → H1 2026 (five full fiscal years plus one half-year).** The half-year is included because the *entire* buyback record sits in it. **Reporting currency: USD; amounts in US$ millions.**

Denominators, both company-basis (filed) and both cumulative over the same FY2021–H1 2026 window:
- **Cumulative CFO = US$3,755.1m** (FY2021 −2,924.3; FY2022 +755.6; FY2023 +1,266.2; FY2024 +2,399.1; FY2025 +3,500.5; H1 2026 −1,242.0) [S21][S4]
- **Cumulative FCF = US$2,819.0m**, on the doctrine default FCF = CFO − total capex [S21]

| Use | Cumulative Amount | Currency | % of CFO (company basis) | Source |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Acquisitions (net cash) | 131.9 | US$m | 3.5% | `CIQ Financials→Cash Flow export, FY2021–FY2025, "Cash Acquisitions" row — vendor export` [S9]; nil in H1 2026 per `Q2 FY26 Interim Report (14 Aug 2026), statements of cash flows` [S4] |
| Buybacks | 500.4 | US$m | 13.3% | `Q2 FY26 Interim Report (14 Aug 2026), Note 31(e) — Share repurchase program` [S3] |
| Dividends | 0.0 | US$m | 0.0% | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 8.A — Dividend and Dividend Policy` [S1]; `CIQ Financials→Cash Flow export, "Total Dividends Paid" = nil every year — vendor export` [S9] |
| Capex (property & equipment + intangibles) | 936.1 | US$m | 24.9% | FY2023–FY2025 and H1 2026 from the filed cash-flow statements; FY2021–FY2022 from `CIQ Financials→Cash Flow export — vendor export`, per the build in `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` [S21][S4][S9] |
| Debt repayment | 1,936.3 | US$m | 51.6% | `CIQ Financials→Cash Flow export, "Total Debt Repaid" FY2021–FY2025 — vendor export` [S9]; H1 2026 448.8 from `Q2 FY26 Interim Report, statements of cash flows` [S4] |
| *(Memo — sources, not uses)* Debt issued | 5,825.1 | US$m | 155.1% | Same sources [S9][S4] |
| *(Memo)* Equity issued (of which the Dec-2021 IPO is 3,403.1) | 3,676.5 | US$m | 97.9% | `CIQ Financials→Cash Flow export, "Issuance of Common Stock" FY2021–FY2025 — vendor export` [S9] |

**On a cumulative-FCF denominator (US$2,819.0m) the same rows read:** acquisitions 4.7%, buybacks 17.8%, dividends 0.0%, debt repayment 68.7%. Capex is not expressed as a % of FCF because it is already deducted in the FCF numerator.

**The row this table would otherwise hide, and it is the biggest one by an order of magnitude.** For a deposit-funded lender the dominant use of capital is not in the investing section at all — it is the loan book. **Gross loans grew from US$6,605.0m (31 Dec 2021) to US$40,274.6m (30 Jun 2026), an increase of US$33,669.7m — roughly 9.0× cumulative company-basis CFO over the same window** [S10]. It was funded principally by customer deposits, which rose from US$36,716.7m cumulatively over FY2021–FY2025 (`CIQ Financials→Cash Flow export, "Net Incr. in Deposit Accounts" — vendor export`) plus a further US$3,408.7m in H1 2026 (`Q2 FY26 Interim Report, statements of cash flows`) [S9][S4]. Any verdict on this company's capital allocation is 90% a verdict on the return and the credit risk of that loan book, and only 10% a verdict on the five rows in the table above.

**Serial-acquirer + opportunity-cost test (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 4) — result: the filter does NOT trip. RF-CAP-004 is NOT emitted and the M&A score cap (Capital allocation max 50) does NOT apply.** The tests and what the evidence shows:

- **Frequency and size.** Cash spent on acquisitions across the full five-year public history is **US$131.9m** — 3.5% of cumulative company-basis CFO, 1.9% of FY2025 revenue of US$6,991m, and 1.0% of equity of US$13,251.7m at 30 Jun 2026 [S9][S18][S4]. No single deal is material to the balance sheet.
- **Debt-funded deals near or above own value.** None. Total debt issued over the window went to funding the loan book, not deals; borrowings and financing were US$4,398.2m at 31 Dec 2025 and US$4,682.3m at 30 Jun 2026 against equity of US$13,251.7m [S8][S4].
- **Goodwill, the balance-sheet fingerprint of deal-making.** Goodwill is **flat**: US$401.9m (Dec-2021) → US$397.4m → US$397.5m → US$414.3m → US$409.4m (Dec-2025) → US$409.4m (Jun-2026) [S10][S5]. **No impairment has ever been recognised** — the annual test at 31 Dec 2025 concluded every cash-generating unit's recoverable amount exceeded its carrying amount, and management found no interim indicator at 30 Jun 2026 [S5]. **RF-FIN-004 does not fire.**
- **Opportunity cost — divestitures, focus, options foregone.** There is **no divestiture in any year** of the window (`Divestitures` row nil, FY2021–LTM Jun-2026) [S9]. No geese were sold to buy a hen. The one opportunity cost worth naming is not financial but managerial: `01_management-and-track-record.md` records that the **President & COO seat was vacated with no announcement and eliminated**, and roughly half the officer bench is under fifteen months in post [S23] — a bench that thin is the constraint on how much M&A this company could integrate, which is an argument for why the near-zero deal spend is the right answer rather than a missed one.
- **Language test.** The Banco Porto Real rationale is **not** bare "synergies / strategic fit / culture fit" — it names a specific regulation (Joint Resolution No. 17) and a specific consequence (brand-name standardisation for regulated institutions). It clears the §24 evidence bar for a stated rationale even though the price does not clear the disclosure bar.

**What must not be claimed.** **No return on any completed acquisition is disclosed or computable.** The single-segment reporting (Banking = 100% of revenue) makes it structurally impossible to test the Easynvest or Hyperplane deals from filings. Per the partial-data rule, no return is assumed. The correct statement is: *M&A here is too small to have destroyed value, and too opaquely reported to be proven to have created any.*

**Cumulative programme status.** US$1.0bn authorised on 3 June 2026 for twelve months to 3 June 2027; **US$500,393k spent, US$499,607k remaining** at 30 June 2026 [S3].

**Six specific price-discipline and conduct reads, stated plainly.**

1. **Net share count actually fell — RF-CAP-002 does NOT fire.** The count of shares issued and fully paid dropped 0.51% in the half, the first fall since listing after three years of low-single-digit creep (weighted diluted shares rose 4.9% from FY2022 to FY2025, about 1.6% a year) [S3][S12]. The buyback did more than offset compensation dilution; it retired 2.59× the shares that vesting created.
2. **The price paid is at the bottom of the stock's own contemporaneous valuation range.** US$12.31 is 4.49× the 30-Jun-2026 book value per share of US$2.743 (equity attributable to parent US$13,249.67m ÷ 4,830,688,659 shares). Capital IQ's Q2 2026 P/BV range for the stock is 4.48 low / 5.52 average / 6.64 high [S13]. **Basis caveat (§15):** my ratio uses the period-end reported book value, while the vendor's daily range uses whatever book value was the latest reported on each pricing date, so the two are close but not perfectly matched-basis — treat the comparison as indicative of the low end, not as a decimal-precise rank.
3. **On a plain price basis it also looks well timed so far.** The last close in the pool is **US$14.30 as of 2026-08-29** (`ciq_facts.json current_price`, from `CIQ Comps→Financial Data`), which is **16.2% above** the average price paid — an unrealised mark-to-market gain of roughly **US$81m** on the shares bought. *Conflict recorded, not averaged away:* `CIQ Financials→Key Stats export` shows a share price of **US$14.88** on a different pull [S14]. I use the pinned sidecar figure of 14.30 and flag the difference; it does not change the direction of the read. Buying below the later price is a fact about ten weeks, not a verdict about management skill.
4. **Leverage did not rise to pay for it.** Borrowings and financing rose 6.5% (4,398.2 → 4,682.3) while equity rose 17.0% (11,321.6 → 13,251.7) over the same half [S8][S4]. The board's own announcement states the programme "will be funded using cash balances derived from retained and future earnings" [S15]. On the evidence, this buyback was paid for out of profit.
5. **The capital ratio is a real qualifier, and it is not resolved.** The Tier 1 capital ratio fell **16.2% (FY2024) → 14.4% (FY2025) → 13.4% (30 Jun 2026)**, and non-performing loans rose **6.7% (FY2023) → 7.8% → 7.9% → 8.6% of loans** over the same span [S11]. The buyback began inside that trend. Two facts cut the other way and must be given their weight: Tier 1 capital in dollars *rose* through the buyback quarter (US$4,276.4m at 31 Mar 2026 → US$4,785.8m at 30 Jun 2026) and the Tier 1 *ratio* rose from 12.8% to 13.4% in that same quarter [S14]. So the buyback did not draw the cushion down in the period it ran; the multi-year direction of the ratio is still down.
6. **No share has been cancelled.** All 40,659,600 shares sit in treasury, carrying no voting or dividend rights while held [S3]. The equity note already deducts them from shares issued and fully paid, so the per-share arithmetic above is on an ex-treasury basis. Treasury shares can be reissued; cancellation would make the reduction permanent. The announcement says the shares "will either be retained in treasury or canceled" [S15] — the choice has not been made.

Followed for ≥4 years?** | **No documented policy; consistent conduct.** Verbatim: "**Nu has not adopted a dividend policy** with respect to future declarations and payment of dividends… We currently intend to retain any future earnings and do not expect to pay any dividends in the foreseeable future" [S1]. The Articles permit dividends out of distributable reserves or share premium, pro rata across Class A and Class B, with no class preference [S2]. Conduct has been identical for **4.7 years since listing** (zero, every period), so nothing has been cut, nothing is erratic, and no payout has been funded by debt. **Verdict: Amber** — the Green band requires a *documented* policy, which does not exist; the Red band requires erratic cuts or debt-funded payouts, neither of which is present | [S1][S2][S9] |
| **Incremental return on reinvested capital** (bank substitute for `Δ NOPAT / Δ invested capital`; see the basis warning at the top) | **Δ net income to parent ÷ Δ total equity: 29.2%** over FY2024 → LTM Jun-2026 (Δ NI 3,607.1 − 1,972.1 = 1,635.0; Δ equity 13,251.7 − 7,647.1 = 5,604.6). Longer windows: **37.4%** FY2023 → FY2025; **50.3%** FY2022 → FY2025; **42.8%** FY2021 → LTM Jun-2026 | `CIQ Financials→Balance Sheet export, "Total Equity"` and `CIQ Financials→Cash Flow export, "Net Income"` — vendor exports [S9][S10]; net income to parent cross-checked to `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` [S21] |
| Reported return on equity | **18.2% (FY2023) → 28.1% (FY2024) → 30.3% (FY2025) → 31.6% (LTM Jun-2026)** | `CIQ Financials→Ratios export, "Return on Equity %" — vendor export` [S11] |
| Per-share outcome — diluted EPS excluding extraordinary items | **−0.08 (FY2022) → 0.2121 (FY2023) → 0.4034 (FY2024) → 0.5846 (FY2025) → 0.7341 (LTM Jun-2026)** | `CIQ Financials→Income Statement export — vendor export` [S12] |
| Per-share outcome — book value per share (equity attributable to parent ÷ shares issued and fully paid, ex-treasury) | **US$1.587 (31 Dec 2024) → US$2.325 (31 Dec 2025) → US$2.743 (30 Jun 2026)**, i.e. **+72.8% in eighteen months** | Equity from `Q2 FY26 Interim Report, statements of financial position`; share counts from `Note 31 (Equity)` [S3][S4] |

**Reading the reinvestment number honestly.** Three qualifications travel with the ~29–37% incremental return, and none of them is cosmetic:

1. **Almost none of the added equity came from shareholders.** New stock issued after FY2022 is trivial — US$9.1m (FY2023), US$5.5m (FY2024), US$6.2m (FY2025) [S9]. Retained earnings did the work: accumulated gains went from US$329.5m (FY2023) to US$5,151.4m (FY2025) to US$7,083.7m (30 Jun 2026) [S10][S3]. So this genuinely measures the return on **profit the board chose to retain rather than distribute**, which is exactly what the A10-01 test needs.
2. **Part of the equity movement is currency translation, not reinvested profit.** Accumulated other comprehensive income swung from −US$184.3m (31 Dec 2025) to +US$186.4m (30 Jun 2026), a US$370.7m move driven mainly by currency translation on foreign entities [S3]. That flatters the denominator's stability, not the numerator. The effect is under 7% of the equity increase in the half and does not change the band the return sits in.
3. **The metric that argues the other way, named as §3 requires.** Company-basis operating cash flow went from **+US$3,640.0m in H1 2025 to −US$1,242.0m in H1 2026** as credit-card receivables (−US$8,135.7m) and loans (−US$6,604.2m) grew faster than deposits (+US$3,408.7m) [S4][S21]. Reported profit is at a record while reported operating cash is negative. That does **not** overturn the reinvestment verdict — for a lender, growing the loan book *is* the investment, and it is recorded inside the operating line rather than the investing line, so a negative operating figure in a fast-growing year is arithmetic rather than deterioration. But it means the ~29% incremental return is **an accounting return on a book that has not been through a credit downturn**, and the adjudication of whether the accrual/cash gap is an earnings-quality problem belongs to `earnings/06_earnings-quality`, not here.

## 4A. Distribution Conduct (A10-05)

A buyback **did** occur in the period, so this section judges the mechanism, not the dividend alone.

| Test | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Mechanism rationale stated (dividend vs buyback, who benefits)?** | **No.** What exists is a *mechanics* statement, not an economic rationale. The interim note describes size, window, methods (open market or privately negotiated, under Rules 10b-18 and 10b5-1) and says timing "depend[s] on market conditions, the share price, liquidity, and other capital allocation opportunities" [S3]. The announcement adds only the funding source: "cash balances derived from retained and future earnings," and that shares "will either be retained in treasury or canceled" [S15]. **Nowhere in the pool does the board or management explain why a repurchase was chosen over a dividend, what value test the repurchase must clear, or how it fits a capital-return framework.** The omission is not passive: the **Q2 2026 earnings call of 13 Aug 2026 — the first call after the programme was approved and after US$500.4m had already been spent — does not mention it at all.** The words "repurchase", "buyback" and even "capital" appear **zero times** in that transcript, and "repurchase"/"buyback" appear zero times across all twenty quarterly transcripts in the pool. The most recent time management discussed the capital position on a call was Q4 2025 (25 Feb 2026), before the programme existed, when it framed US$2.2bn as "excess capital in our operating entities" and said the intent was "to invest in growth from a position of strength" [S19][S20]. **Verdict: Amber.** | [S3][S15][S19][S20] |
| **Promoter participation in any buyback (tender/open-market)** | **No tender offer exists — purchases are open-market/privately-negotiated Class A only, so there is no tender for a controller to participate in, and Class B was untouched** (1,022,600,698 Class B shares at both 31 Dec 2025 and 30 Jun 2026) [S3]. **One item must be flagged rather than waved through.** The insider file records transactions typed "**Sale to Issuer**" — shares sold *to the company* — by the controller and other insiders: **23 Apr 2026** at US$14.44 (Vélez −45,690; Junqueira −8,264; Lago −24,348; Fragelli −11,991; ≈90,293 shares, ≈US$1.30m) and **23 Jul 2026** at US$13.39 (Vélez −45,690; Junqueira −8,048; Fragelli −13,496; ≈67,234 shares, ≈US$0.90m) [S17]. The April date **pre-dates** the 3 June programme, so it cannot be a repurchase under it; the July date falls **inside** the programme window but after the 30 June reporting date, so no filed data covers it. The identical quantity for Vélez on both dates (45,690 shares) at two different prices, the fixed quarterly cadence and the multi-executive single-price pattern all point to routine share-settlement of vesting awards — the equity note discloses 4,083,323 shares "withheld for employees' taxes" in the half, which "are canceled and cannot be reissued" [S3]. **The pool does not state which mechanism these Form 4 lines belong to.** Applying the conservative default (§4) to that specific residual uncertainty: recorded **Amber** with a follow-up, at **Low materiality** — 45,690 shares is 0.005% of Vélez's ~905.8m-share position, and the two dates together are ~0.2% of the programme's US$1.0bn [S18]. It is not a promoter tender and must not be written up as one. | [S17][S3][S18] |
| **Buyback timing vs promoter pledge / stake changes** | **No pledge regime applies and no pledge is disclosed** — a Cayman-incorporated NYSE foreign private issuer has no SEBI-style promoter-encumbrance filing, and no pledge of Vélez's or Rua California Ltd.'s shares appears in the beneficial-ownership table [S22]. On stake changes around the buyback: the controller's Class B block is unchanged, and open-market insider selling in the window sits **outside** the buying period, not inside it — Junqueira sold 300,000 shares at ~US$14.81–14.82 on 23 Mar 2026 (before the programme), the Lead Independent Director sold 21,000 at US$12.24 on 15 May 2026 (before the programme), and Junqueira and Fragelli sold 271,707 shares at ~US$15.80–15.81 on 14 Aug 2026 (after the reported buying) [S17]. The company's average purchase price (US$12.31) is **below** every one of those insider sale prices, which is the right way round for minority holders. **Verdict on timing: Green, on the evidence available.** | [S17][S22] |
| **The conduct point this test exists to catch, and it is real though small** | Because **only Class A shares are repurchased while Class B (20 votes per share) is untouched, every dollar of buyback mechanically raises the controller's voting percentage.** Arithmetic, shown in full: Class A fell 3,833,072,934 → 3,808,087,961 while Class B held at 1,022,600,698, so total votes fell 24,285,086,894 → 24,260,101,921 and the Class B share of votes rose **84.216% → 84.303%**. Vélez holds 88.3% of Class B, so **his voting power rose from ~74.36% to ~74.44%, +7.6 basis points.** If the remaining US$499.6m is spent at the same average price (~40.6m more shares), Class B reaches ~84.44% of votes and Vélez ~74.56% — **about +20bp across the whole programme.** This is a genuine, one-way transfer of control that no minority holder voted for, and it should be named. It is graded **Amber at Low materiality** because the size is 20 basis points on a stake that already carries absolute control (the CEO cannot be removed by public shareholders either before or after), so it changes nothing about who governs the company. | Share counts and classes from `Q2 FY26 Interim Report, Note 31 (Equity)` [S3]; 88.3% of Class B and 74.3–74.4% of votes from `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.C and Item 7.A` via [S22] |

## 5. Capital-Allocation Read

**Verdict: value-creative / disciplined — with the qualification that the record is short and the credit book has never been through a downturn.** On the numbers this engine can actually verify, capital has created per-share value rather than absolute size: profit retained rather than distributed has earned an incremental **29.2%** (Δ net income to parent ÷ Δ equity, FY2024 → LTM Jun-2026) against a reported return on equity that has climbed 18.2% → 31.6%, diluted earnings per share have gone from −US$0.08 (FY2022) to US$0.734 (LTM Jun-2026), and book value per share is up 72.8% in eighteen months to US$2.743.

**Best use of capital: organic reinvestment in the loan book** — US$33.7bn of gross-loan growth, roughly nine times cumulative operating cash flow, funded by deposits rather than by shareholders, at incremental returns in the high-twenties to high-thirties percent. Everything else in the capital-allocation table is a rounding error beside it. **Worst use of capital: nothing has been wasted, so the "worst" is an absence rather than an act** — acquisitions of US$131.9m over five years bought two useful regulatory licences and two products whose returns are **neither disclosed nor computable**, because the company reports a single segment; the buyback, though well priced, is a single half-year with no stated rationale; and there is no documented dividend policy telling a shareholder when, if ever, capital comes back.

**The single biggest capital-allocation signal is not the buyback — it is the arithmetic of the buyback sitting inside a falling capital ratio and a rising bad-loan ratio.** Non-performing loans have risen every year, 6.7% → 7.8% → 7.9% → 8.6% of loans, while the Tier 1 ratio has fallen 16.2% → 14.4% → 13.4%, and the company began returning capital in the middle of that trend, with US$28.8bn of undrawn credit-card limits sitting off the balance sheet as the exposure that draws hardest when customers are stressed. Today that combination is comfortably financed — Tier 1 capital in dollars rose through the buyback quarter, the repurchase was 25.9% of one half-year's profit and was paid from earnings not debt, and the loan-loss allowance stands at US$6,612.9m. **The falsification test is dated and simple: the Q3 2026 results, due November 2026, showing whether the non-performing ratio and the Tier 1 ratio move together or apart while repurchases continue.** If they diverge further, the same repurchase stops being surplus profit returned and becomes capital taken out of a thinning cushion — and this verdict moves from *value-creative* to *mixed* without a single new red flag appearing.

**Two things this report deliberately does not say.** It does not say the buyback was made below intrinsic value — this module runs before valuation and cannot know that. And it does not say the acquisitions created value — no return on any of them is disclosed or computable, and the doctrine forbids assuming one.

## management-governance / 03_incentives-and-compensation.md

_Source: `03_incentives-and-compensation.md`_

# Incentives & Compensation — NU

**Jurisdiction & regime detected (CLAUDE.md §27).** Nu Holdings Ltd. is a Cayman Islands exempted company listed on the NYSE and filing as a **foreign private issuer**. Its proxy-equivalent is therefore **not** a DEF 14A — it is **Item 6.B (Compensation), Item 6.C (Board Practices), Item 6.D (Employees) and Item 6.F (Clawback) of the Form 20-F**, plus the audited notes (Note 10 Share-based payments, Note 28 Related parties) and Exhibit 97.1 (Compensation Clawback Policy). Reporting standard is **IFRS as issued by the IASB**; reporting currency **US dollars**; fiscal year = **calendar year ended 31 December 2025**. India's Companies Act Sec 197 caps and the SEBI LODR Reg 17(6)(e) promoter-pay gates named in the checklist have **no Cayman/NYSE equivalent** — those prongs are answered Not Applicable with the reason, and the substantive tests behind them (pay vs profit, pay growth vs profit growth, controller pay) are run on the local numbers instead.

Cross-module inputs used: `01_management-and-track-record.md` (this module) and `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md`. `earnings/` outputs were not read for this agent's scope.

---

## 1. Compensation Structure

Reporting currency **US$**; period **FY2025 (year ended 31 December 2025)** unless stated.

**The binding fact first: Nu does not disclose any individual's pay.** "Under Cayman Islands law, we are not required to disclose compensation paid to our management team on an individual basis" [`FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.B — Compensation of Directors and Management Team, p.193`]. The only figure published is one aggregate line covering the whole board plus all key management personnel: **US$91.3 million for FY2025** [`FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.B — Executive Compensation, p.194`], confirmed in the audited notes as US$91,269 thousand (FY2024 US$96,007 thousand; FY2023 US$60,117 thousand) [`FY25 Form 20-F, Note 28(b) Management compensation, p.F-77`]. So the table below is filled at the level the filing actually supports, and the CEO and CFO rows say so.

| Executive | Base | Annual Bonus | Long-Term Incentive | Cash vs Equity Mix | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| **CEO — David Vélez Osorno** (Founder, Chairman & CEO) | Not disclosed individually | Not disclosed individually. He is not stated to be in the Brazil Profit Sharing Program | **No LTI grant disclosed since 2021.** His only ever performance award — the 2021 Contingent Share Award, "nearly 100% of Mr. Vélez's total compensation" — was terminated at his own request on 29 Nov 2022 for no consideration | Not disclosed. His economic exposure is his **906,212,615 shares (18.6% of share capital, ~US$13.0bn at US$14.30)**, not his pay | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B, p.193-194`; `FY24 20-F, Item 6.E — 2021 Contingent Share Award (CSA), p.288`; `FY25 20-F, Item 7.A, p.203`; `ciq_facts.json current_price 14.3, as-of 2026-08-29 (vendor)` |
| **CFO — Guilherme Lago** | Not disclosed individually | Not disclosed individually | Not disclosed individually | Not disclosed individually | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B, p.193` |

The company states it wants "the majority of compensation of our management team to be delivered in the form of share-based compensation" — so >50% equity by intent, unquantified | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B — Compensation Composition, p.195`; `FY25 20-F, Note 10, p.F-47` |
| **Non-employee directors** | No cash salary; a **fixed annual equity retainer** plus an additional amount for committee membership/chair | None | The retainer itself (equity); **no options granted in 2024 or 2025** | Mixed cash and equity, "primarily weighted towards equity"; no ratio set | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B — Board of Directors, p.196`; `FY25 20-F, Note 10, p.F-46` |

## 2. Performance Metrics

This is where the read gets thin, and the thinness is the finding. **Neither plan discloses a single named metric or a single weight.**

| Plan | Metric | Weight | Per-Share/Returns or Size-Based? | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| **Annual bonus — Brazil Profit Sharing Program** | "linked to the achievement of pre-established business goals through union negotiation." No goal is named, quantified, or published. Officers in Brazil are "subject to the same payout formulae and maximum payouts as the rest of our Brazilian employee population" | Not disclosed | **Cannot be classified** — the goals are pre-established but undisclosed. Nothing in the description points at revenue, deal count or headcount, so there is no evidence of a size metric; there is equally no evidence of a returns metric | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B — Compensation Composition, p.195` |
| **Long-term incentive — RSUs (2020 Omnibus Incentive Plan)** | **No performance condition attaches to the awards actually granted.** The plan permits the board to set "performance goals applicable to RSUs" but the filing does not state that this was done. Vesting is by time: 50.97% of outstanding grants on a 3-year schedule, 42.78% on 5 years, weighted-average 3.8 years | Not disclosed | **Neither** — time-vesting RSUs pay on tenure and on the share price. The payoff moves with per-share value because of the **vehicle**, not because of a metric. Not size-based | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B — Employee Share Plans, p.197`; `FY25 20-F, Note 10, p.F-47` |
| **RSU grant SIZING (how much you get, not whether it vests)** | Four stated inputs: "(i) individual performance; (ii) the performance of the business unit; (iii) our performance as a whole; and (iv) the importance of certain performance to our long-term goals" | Not disclosed | **Cannot be classified** — these are categories, not metrics. "Our performance as a whole" is not defined as revenue, profit, ROE or TSR | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B, p.195` |
| **Legacy — stock options (SOP)** | None. Time-vesting only (20% at year 1, then 48 equal monthly instalments) | n/a | Neither. **No options granted in 2024 or 2025**; the 21,819,196 outstanding are fully exercisable legacy grants at a weighted-average exercise price of US$1.80 | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B — SOP, p.199`; `FY25 20-F, Note 10, p.F-45/F-46` |
| **Terminated — 2021 Contingent Share Award (CEO)** | **The only fully specified metric Nu has ever published, and it was a pure per-share one:** 1% of fully diluted shares when the Class A VWAP held **≥ US$18.69** for 60 consecutive trading days, plus a further 1% at **≥ US$35.30**, both requiring five years' continued service | 100% of the CEO's variable pay while it existed | **Per-share / market-based.** Terminated 29 Nov 2022 at the CEO's own request | `FY21 20-F, Item 6.E — 2021 Contingent Share Awards, p.245`; `FY24 20-F, Item 6.E — CSA, p.288` |

**What the pay therefore rewards.** Two things: staying (time-vested RSUs over a 3.8-year average) and the share price (because the award is settled in shares). Nothing disclosed rewards revenue, absolute EBITDA, headcount, customer count, or deals done — so there is **no evidence of a size-based or empire-building metric anywhere in the pay structure**, which matters for a company that grew revenue from US$8.0bn to US$15.8bn in two years. But the converse is equally true: there is **no disclosed returns metric either** — no return on equity, no return on capital (ROIC — the profit earned per US$100 of capital put in), no earnings per share, no total shareholder return, and no hurdle of any kind on a single RSU that vested in 2025.

**Where the returns discipline actually sits.** Not in the pay plan — in the controller's own balance sheet. Vélez holds 3,088,117 Class A and 903,124,498 Class B shares, 906,212,615 of 4,860,599,241 shares outstanding = **18.6% of the economics**, worth roughly **US$13.0bn** at the 29 Aug 2026 close of US$14.30. That is about **142 times the entire US$91.3m aggregate pay pool** for the whole board and management team combined [`FY25 20-F, Item 7.A — Major Shareholders, p.203-204`; `ciq_facts.json current_price 14.3 / shares_outstanding_m 4,830.7 — CIQ Comps→Financial Data, as-of 2026-08-29, vendor export`]. Computation by this agent from those figures.

**The single most informative pay event in the record.** On 29 November 2022 Vélez unilaterally terminated the 2021 CSA and the board and compensation committee agreed, "on the basis that it has constituted a unilateral transfer of future value from Mr. Vélez to the Company – and, consequently, all shareholders." He "has not received any consideration for the termination." The stated reasons were (i) removing US$355.6m of future share-based expense and (ii) avoiding "potential dilution of the shareholders of the Company in an amount equivalent to up to 2% of the total number of ordinary shares in issue" [`FY24 20-F, Item 6.E — CSA, p.288`]. The award's grant-date fair value was **US$422.6m** [`FY21 20-F, Item 6.E, p.245`]; accounting acceleration cost US$355.6m in Q4 2022.

**Both sides of that fact, stated (§3, §8).** It is a real, dated, per-share-positive act by a controller who did not have to do it, and it is the strongest single alignment signal in the file. It is also true that the award was, and still is, **out of the money**: the first milestone required a US$18.69 60-day VWAP, and the stock closed at **US$14.30** on 29 Aug 2026 — roughly four years and nine months after grant, that milestone has still not been reached [`ciq_facts.json current_price 14.3, as-of 2026-08-29`]. So what he gave up was a contingent claim, not cash in hand. Both facts are the finding; neither cancels the other.

## 3. Pay vs Performance

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| CEO total pay (latest) | **Not disclosed.** No individual figure exists in any filing. The aggregate for the whole board plus all key management is US$91.3m (FY2025) | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B, p.193-194`; `Note 28(b), p.F-77` |
| Aggregate pay direction vs profit | Pay **fell 4.9%** (US$96.0m → US$91.3m) while net income **rose 45.6%** (US$1,972.0m → US$2,871.7m). Pay as a share of profit fell from 4.87% to **3.18%** | `Note 28(b), p.F-77`; `Statement of Income Data, p.155` |
| Pay growth vs 3-year profit growth | Aggregate pay CAGR FY2023→FY2025 = **+23.2%**; net income CAGR over the same two years = **+66.9%**. Pay growth is roughly one-third of profit growth | Computed from `Note 28(b)` and `Statement of Income Data` |
| Pay vs peers | **Not testable.** Nu says an "independent compensation consultant" reviews a Peer Group each year and publishes the selection criteria (fintech/software/internet, similar market cap and revenue, must file a proxy circular, revenue-growth preference) but **names no peer and publishes no positioning** — no percentile, no target quartile. The pool's own comp set is 10 LatAm banks and fintechs (Itaú, Bradesco, Banco do Brasil, Santander Brasil, BTG Pactual, Banorte, Cibest, PagSeguro, Inter & Co, Credicorp), none of which is the peer group Nu describes, and none of whose executive pay appears in the pool | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B — Peer Group, p.195`; `Company Comparable Analysis Nu Holdings Ltd .xls → Financial Data, as-of 2026-08-29 — CIQ vendor export` |
| Pay-for-performance alignment | **Directionally positive at the aggregate level, untestable at the person level.** Every ratio moves the right way (pay down, profit up, pay/profit down two years running), and the equity is delivered over a 3.8-year weighted average. But with no individual figure and no metric, the link is inferred from three ratios, not demonstrated from a pay plan | `Note 28(b)`; `Note 10, p.F-47` |
| Say-on-pay support (%) | **No such vote exists.** As a foreign private issuer Nu is exempt from the US say-on-pay rules, and as a Cayman exempted company controlled by one holder (74.4% of votes) no remuneration resolution is put to shareholders. The articles "provide no other right to put any proposals before annual general meetings or extraordinary general meetings" | `FY25 20-F, Item 10.B, p.~217`; `Item 6.C — Controlled Company Exception, p.143` |
| Share-based compensation expense | US$329.5m (FY2025), US$372.7m (FY2024), US$255.6m (FY2023) — **11.5% of FY2025 net income**, down from 18.9% | `Note 10, p.F-46`; `Statement of Income Data, p.155` |
| Net dilution outcome | Shares issued 4,765,937,154 (31-Dec-23) → 4,855,673,632 (31-Dec-25), **+1.9% over two years**, then **−0.51% to 4,830,688,659 by 30-Jun-26** as a US$1.0bn buyback (40,659,600 shares at an average US$12.31) outran vesting | `FY25 20-F, Equity note, p.F-85`; `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` (Q2 FY26 Interim Report, Note 31(e)) |

**The honest summary of this section.** The pay pool is small relative to what the business earns (3.18% of profit, 0.58% of revenue), it shrank in a year profit grew 46%, and the share count has stopped rising. Those are facts and they point one way. What is missing is the ability to check any of it at the level that matters — who got what, and for hitting what.

## 4. Incentive Alignment Read

**Verdict: mixed.**

The pay actually rewards two things — staying, and the share price. RSUs vest on time (weighted-average 3.8 years) with no performance condition attached, the annual bonus is a union-negotiated profit-sharing formula whose goals are never published, and the last time Nu attached a real metric to executive pay it was a pure per-share one (a US$18.69 and US$35.30 60-day VWAP) that the CEO handed back for nothing in November 2022, taking a claim on up to 2% of the fully diluted share count off the table [`FY24 20-F, Item 6.E, p.288`]. Nothing in the disclosed structure pays for revenue, absolute EBITDA, headcount or deals, which is the important negative in a business that doubled revenue in two years — **the empire-building channel is simply not wired into this pay plan** — but nothing pays for return on capital or earnings per share either, so the returns discipline is not in the contract; it is in the fact that the controller owns 18.6% of the economics, worth roughly 142 times the entire US$91.3m board-and-management pay pool [`FY25 20-F, Item 7.A, p.203`; `ciq_facts.json, as-of 2026-08-29`].

The single biggest incentive signal is that **the CEO's incentive is his shareholding, not his pay package — and Nu's disclosure makes it impossible to check that this is also true one layer down.** Aggregate pay fell 4.9% while profit rose 45.6% and now takes 3.18% of net income against 5.83% two years ago, equity burn is 0.77% a year against a 4.70% reserve, repricing is barred without a shareholder vote, and a Rule 10D-1 no-fault clawback with a three-year lookback is in force. Those are real and they are cited. Against them: no individual pay figure for anyone, no named metric, no weight, no named peer, no CEO-to-median ratio, no attrition rate, and no vote that any shareholder can cast on remuneration. That combination — good pay *conduct* on every number available, no ability to *audit* it at the level that matters — is what "mixed" means here, and it is why this score does not go higher.

*Note on the partial-data cap.* The MODULE_RULES cap "No proxy / compensation disclosure → Incentive alignment max 50" is **not** applied. Compensation disclosure exists and is substantive (Item 6.B plan terms, Note 10 award tables, Note 28 aggregate pay, Exhibit 97.1 clawback policy). What is absent is *individual* disclosure, a legal-regime feature of Cayman/FPI reporting rather than an absence of the disclosure the cap contemplates. The gap is instead charged directly against the "metric clarity and weights" and "minority-holder alignment" components below.
