# Ownership & Insider Behavior — NU

**Company:** Nu Holdings Ltd. (NYSE:NU) — Class A ordinary shares, USD, NYSE primary listing. Incorporated in the Cayman Islands; SEC foreign private issuer filing on Form 20-F; operations principally in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. Reporting standard IFRS, fiscal year ends 31 December.

**Jurisdiction note (CLAUDE.md §27, MODULE_RULES Jurisdiction-Aware Source Mapping).** There is no "promoter" concept, no SEBI shareholding-pattern filing and no SAST pledge-disclosure regime for a Cayman-incorporated NYSE issuer. The local equivalents used throughout are: the **Form 20-F Item 7.A beneficial-ownership table** (ownership), the **Capital IQ Public Ownership → Insider Trading export of Form 4 records** (insider transactions), **Schedules 13G** cited inside the 20-F (5% holders), and the **Memorandum and Articles of Association / Shareholder's Agreement** as summarised in Item 10.B (control structure). Every A3 and A15 band below is applied at its stated US/Cayman equivalent, and where a band names an Indian statute the regime substitution is stated on the row.

**Data sufficiency for this agent.** Full — the pool carries five consecutive 20-Fs (FY2021–FY2025), a complete beneficial-ownership table, a mechanically-parsed insider-transaction export that reconciles exactly to `ciq_facts.json`, and the full Articles/Shareholder's Agreement summary. **No partial-data cap applies.** Web sources were not available in this runtime (all network hosts denied) and were not needed: no ownership or insider fact below is web-sourced, and nothing below is memory-sourced.

---

**Total insider ownership.** The directors and management team named in the FY25 20-F hold **1,068,718,206 shares = 21.99% of shares outstanding** and **20,498,131,468 votes = 84.4% of total voting power** (46,117,508 Class A + all 1,022,600,698 Class B; arithmetic mine on the filing's counts). The vendor's independent count agrees: Capital IQ puts "Individuals/Insiders" at **1,101,421,622 shares = 22.80%** of shares outstanding as of Aug-2026, the ~33m difference being three quarters of vesting and one new director `[CIQ Public Ownership → Summary export, as of Aug-2026 — vendor export]`. **Roughly 22% of the economics, roughly 84% of the vote.** That gap is the single most important fact in this report and is dissected in §4.

**A3-06 — free float.** Public float **77.1%** of shares outstanding `[CIQ Public Company Profile export (NU), quote data as of 2026-08-28 — vendor export]`, comfortably above the ≥35–40% green band. But the float is economic, not political: Class A carries 3,837,998,543 of 24,290,012,503 total votes = **15.8% of the vote in aggregate**, and after removing insider-held Class A the public's voting share is roughly **15.6%**. No minimum-public-shareholding regime applies (that is a SEBI/SCRR 19A test); the NYSE distribution standards are met and no listing-standard deficiency is disclosed.

**A3-01 — controller holding trend.** Five consecutive annual observations from the company's own filings, and it is flat:

| Filing (period) | Vélez % of Class B | Vélez % of total voting power |
|---|---:|---:|
| FY2021 20-F (filed 2022-04-21) | 86.2% | 74.9% |
| FY2022 20-F (filed 2023-04-20) | 88.6% | 76.1% |
| FY2023 20-F (filed 2024-04-19) | 88.8% | 75.9% |
| FY2024 20-F (filed 2025-04-16) | 88.6% | 75.2% |
| FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-04-08) | **88.3%** | **74.3–74.4%** |

The controller has never sold a Class B share. The ~1.5 percentage points of voting power lost since FY2022 is arithmetic drift from Class A issuance under the equity plans, not disposal. Twelve quarters of shareholding-pattern data do not exist for this regime; five annual filed observations are the local equivalent and are what is reported.

**A3-05 — cheap insider equity (Amber).** No preferential allotment, warrant issue, discounted placement or option repricing to the controller is disclosed in any of the five 20-Fs. Class B cannot be granted as compensation — the plans issue Class A only `[FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.B]`. Two items keep this off Green. First, **Class B carries a standing pre-emptive right**: "if we issue Class A ordinary shares, we must first make an offer to each holder of Class B ordinary shares to issue to such holder **on the same economic terms** such number of Class B ordinary shares as would allow such holder to maintain its proportional ownership interest" `[FY25 Form 20-F, Item 10.B — Preemptive or Similar Rights]`. It is priced at market, so it is not cheap equity — but it is a permanent entitlement to top up **super-voting** stock that no Class A holder has. Second, options exercised in the window carry strikes of **US$0.29 and US$0.43** against a US$14–16 market price (Fragelli, 2,361,450 shares, 8 Apr 2026) `[CIQ Insider Trading export — vendor export]`; those are ordinary pre-listing startup grants for a business founded in 2013, disclosed, and are not a preferential issue — but they are the reason "insider ownership" and "insider conviction" are not the same thing here.

**Net insider activity: net selling on every measure that reflects a decision, and zero buying of any kind.**

- **Open market (the conviction signal): 0 buys, 4 sells, net −592,707 shares, ~US$8,996,436.** My tally of the four open-market disposals (300,000 + 21,000 + 50,000 + 221,707 = 592,707) ties **exactly** to the deterministic sidecar: `insider_open_market` = "trailing 12m (to 2026-08-18): net −592,707 (0 buys / 4 sells)" `[ciq_facts.json, source_ref: CIQ Public Ownership → Insider Trading — Open Market Acq/Disp only]`.
- **All disposals of every kind: 11 events, 750,234 shares, US$11,200,530.**
- **All acquisitions of every kind: 14 events, 4,765,246 shares — of which 2,403,796 are RSU grants and share awards at zero consideration and 2,361,450 are an option exercise at a US$0.29–0.43 strike. Not one share was bought at a market price.**
- **All-types net = +4,015,012 shares**, which again ties exactly to the sidecar (`insider_net_activity`: "net +4,015,012 (14 acq / 11 disp)"). **That positive number is compensation, not conviction** — it is the single most misreadable figure in this dataset and must never be quoted as insider accumulation.

**Distinguishing the three kinds of transaction, as required.**
1. **Open-market purchases: none.** Zero, by anyone, in the entire observed record — including through the 52-week low of US$11.20 and the 15-May-2026 print at US$12.24, at which the Lead Independent Director was a seller rather than a buyer `[CIQ Equity Listings export (NU), 52-week low US$11.20, as of 2026-08-28 — vendor export]`.
2. **Option exercises and RSU vesting** account for 100% of acquisitions and are excluded from the conviction read.
3. **10b5-1 status is not disclosed in the export.** The vendor filter explicitly excludes "Automatic" transactions, which is where 10b5-1 sales are usually classified — so the four open-market sales above are, on the export's own logic, more likely discretionary than plan-driven. That is an inference from the export's filter, not a filing fact, and is flagged for follow-up.

**The "sale to issuer" cluster — read carefully, because it is not a conviction sell.** Five insiders sold to the company on 23 Apr 2026 at a single uniform US$14.44 and three sold on 23 Jul 2026 at a single uniform US$13.39. Vélez's share count is **identical in both quarters (45,690)**. Two things follow. First, these predate the company's US$1,000m buyback, authorised only on **4 June 2026** for the twelve months to 3 June 2027 `[CIQ Key Developments export (NU), Buyback Transaction Announcements, 2026-06-04 — vendor export]`, so they are not buyback participation. Second, a uniform price across multiple insiders on one date, repeating quarterly at a fixed share count, is the signature of a **share surrender to the issuer to cover tax on vesting**, not a market decision. Corroborating arithmetic: Vélez's Class A balance rose from 2,724,260 (27-Apr) to 3,105,007 immediately before the 23-Jul sale — he acquired ~380,747 Class A in between, through vesting the export's filter hides. **Labelled inference, not a filing fact** — the Form 4 transaction code is not in the export. Treated as neutral, not as selling.

**Trade timing (feeding A15-04 and RF-MKT-001).** Every disclosed sale falls **after** an earnings release, never before one: 23-Mar-2026 (Q4'25 released 25-Feb-2026), 15-May-2026 (Q1'26 released 14-May-2026), 14-Aug-2026 (Q2'26 released 13-Aug-2026), and the two sale-to-issuer dates mid-quarter. **No insider sale in the record precedes a results announcement. RF-MKT-001 does not fire** — the pattern is the opposite of the one it tests. One residual worth naming rather than burying: the two largest open-market sales (US$4.3m combined, Junqueira and Fragelli) were executed the day after a strong Q2'26 print (net income US$1,060.2m vs US$636.8m a year earlier `[CIQ Key Developments export, Announcements of Earnings, 2026-08-13 — vendor export]`) at US$15.80–15.81, and the stock closed at **US$14.30 on 28 Aug 2026**, ~9.5% lower two weeks later `[CIQ Equity Listings export, NYSE:NU close 2026-08-28 — vendor export]`. That is legal, in-window, well-timed selling. It is not a red flag; it is also not a vote of confidence.

## 3. Pledging & Encumbrance

| Insider | Shares Pledged | % of Their Holding | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| David Vélez Osorno / Rua California Ltd. | **0 disclosed** | **0.0%** | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A Major Shareholders table and fn.(2)/(4), p.203` — no pledge footnote; the company states it believes each listed shareholder "possesses sole voting and investment power over all the Class A ordinary shares or Class B ordinary shares shown as beneficially owned" |
| Cristina Junqueira and her vehicles | **0 disclosed** | **0.0%** | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A fn.(3), pp.203–204` |
| All other directors and management team | **0 disclosed** | **0.0%** | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A table, pp.203–204` |

**No pledging disclosed.** Every "pledge" reference in the FY25 filing is something else and must not be confused with insider encumbrance: securities the **Group itself** pledges as exchange trading margin (US$297,274 thousand, versus US$350,193 thousand at 31 December 2024) `[FY25 Form 20-F, Note 12]`, receivables and securities pledged in repurchase-agreement operations `[FY25 Form 20-F, Notes 12 and 24]`, and Brazilian FGTS regulation permitting *workers* to pledge future withdrawals as loan collateral `[FY25 Form 20-F, Item 4.B — regulatory background]`.

**A3-02 tested against the graded thresholds, not a flat line.** Disclosed insider pledge = **0% of the control group's own 906,212,615-share holding** and **0% of total capital**. That is below the 25%-of-holding warning line, below the 50%-of-holding / 20%-of-capital declaration trigger, and there is no invocation. **Green. RF-OWN-001 does not fire; RF-OWN-002 does not fire** (no quarter-on-quarter increase — the balance is zero in all five annual filings). This is consistent with `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`, which independently computed 0% against the >50% hard-disqualifier line and answered **N**.

**Two honest qualifications, because a zero from a permissive regime is not the same as a certified zero.**
1. **The company's own policy permits pledging.** "While pledging Company securities is allowed, Nubankers should be aware of the associated risks… securities held in a margin account may be sold by a broker without the customer's consent if the customer fails to meet a margin call… Notwithstanding the above, Company securities may not be pledged during the 15-day period preceding the release of quarterly or annual earnings" `[FY25 Form 20-F, Exhibit 11.1 — Insider Trading Policy, "Pledging or margin accounts for Nubankers"]`. A best-practice policy prohibits pledging by executive officers and directors outright. This one allows it and only blacks out 15 days a year.
2. **There is no affirmative pledge-disclosure duty here.** Unlike SEBI's SAST Reg 31 regime, a Cayman/NYSE foreign private issuer has no standing obligation to report insider encumbrance quarter by quarter. So the correct statement is **"no pledge is disclosed anywhere in the filed record"**, not "it is proven that nothing is pledged". Confidence on the zero is 4, not 5. Follow-up recorded.

## 4. Control Structure

| Feature | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Dual-class / super-voting** | **Yes — 20:1.** Class B ordinary shares carry **20 votes per share**; Class A carries 1. Class B is 21.0% of shares but **84.2% of votes**. Rights are otherwise identical except that Class B additionally holds (a) conversion rights, (b) pre-emptive rights to maintain proportional ownership when Class A is issued, and (c) certain consent rights. **The only sunset is a threshold, not a clock**: Class B converts automatically to Class A only if, on a meeting record date, the aggregate voting power of Class B is **less than 10% of total voting power**. It is currently **84.2%** — the trigger is roughly two orders of magnitude away and, absent a founder sale, unreachable. There is no time-based sunset of any length, and Nu listed in December 2021. | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A, p.204`; `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 10.B — Memorandum and Articles of Association (conversion; Preemptive or Similar Rights)` |
| **Controlled-company status** | **Yes, and the exemptions are used.** "David Vélez controls a majority of the voting power of our shares. As a result, we are a 'controlled company' within the meaning of the NYSE listing standards… We rely and intend to continue to rely on some or all of these exemptions. **As a result, we do not have a stand-alone nominating and corporate governance committee, and our Compensation and People Committee is not required to consist entirely of independent directors.**" The company may also elect not to have a majority-independent board. | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.C — Controlled Company Exception`; `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 16G` |
| **Shareholder bloc with board rights** | **Yes — a Shareholder's Agreement dated 29 Nov 2021, last amended 11 Mar 2025, between the company and Vélez.** Board nomination on a sliding scale: **≥40% of votes → up to five nominees (or a majority of the board if enlarged); ≥25% → three nominees (or one-third); ≥5% → one nominee (or 10%)**. He is currently at 74.4%, so the top tier applies. He also has the right to designate his **pro-rata share of the Audit and Risk Committee and the Compensation and People Committee**. These rights are stated to be "additive to and not intended to limit in any way" his rights under the Articles and Cayman law. Plus access to books, records and operating data, and consultation rights with management, while ≥5%. | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.B — Shareholder's Agreement` |
| **Founder veto over corporate action** | **Yes, and it is broad.** While Vélez holds **≥10% of voting power**, the company agrees not to take, or permit subsidiaries to take, any of the following without his **prior written approval**: incurring debt above consolidated net equity; transactions with officers, directors or other affiliates; material changes to strategic direction or scope; adopting a shareholder rights plan; **paying or declaring any dividend or distribution**; any merger, consolidation, reorganisation or change of control; any liquidation, bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding; **authorising or issuing any share capital or convertible security**; acquiring or disposing of assets above 20% of net equity value; and **determining the annual compensation of any officer or director** (excluding himself). At 74.4% today, the 10% floor means this veto survives him selling roughly **87% of his stake**. | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.B — Shareholder's Agreement` |
| **Entrenchment that activates on loss of control** | **Two provisions that make the structure harder to unwind than it looks.** (a) **Classified board on a trigger:** "from and after the date on which the founding shareholder (together with his affiliates) no longer beneficially owns more than 50% of our outstanding voting power, **or the classifying date, the directors shall be divided into three classes**," each serving three-year staggered terms, with "the founding directors… allocated to the longest duration classes." Directors are elected annually **today**; the staggered board appears precisely when public holders would otherwise gain the power to use annual elections. (b) **Meeting requisition disappears on the same trigger:** a meeting may be requisitioned by holders of a majority of voting power while the founder controls a majority — "However, **if our founding shareholder controls less than a majority of the voting power of our shares, no shareholder shall have the power to requisition a meeting of shareholders.**" | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 10.B — Memorandum and Articles of Association (classifying date; requisition of general meetings)`; corroborated by `CIQ Takeover Defenses → Corporate Governance export (NU) — vendor export` (Classified Board: No; term 1 year; removal of directors only for cause: Yes; supermajority 66.67% to amend charter and bylaws) |
| **Controlling-owner objective alignment *(Filter 6)*** | **Tested. Filter 6 does NOT trip. RF-OWN-004 is not emitted.** See the test below. | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A`; `ciq_facts.json — segments_revenue`; `CIQ Public Ownership → Summary export — vendor export` |

**A3-03 — control-versus-cash-flow wedge (Red on the number, benign on the mechanism).** Vélez holds **18.6% of the economics and 74.4% of the votes: a wedge of 55.8 percentage points**, far past the registry's >20pp red band. But the mechanism matters for what the reader should do with it. There is **no pyramid**: one wholly-owned, named holding vehicle (Rua California Ltd., 100% his), one spousal holding of 1,500,000 Class B, no cross-holding, no circularity, no promoter investment company sitting between a family and the listed entity. **The entire wedge comes from the disclosed 20:1 dual-class structure**, which is A3-04's subject. Both rows are marked Red because both bands are genuinely tripped, and the cross-reference is stated on each so the synthesis prices the fact **once**, not twice.

**Unaligned-owner test (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 6) — worked, and negative.** Filter 6 asks whether the controlling owner's objective is long-term per-share value creation, and names three structures that are inherent conflicts:

- **(a) Government control — no.** "State Owned Shares" total **1,477,013 shares, 0.03%** of shares outstanding `[CIQ Public Ownership → Summary export — vendor export]`. No golden share, no state director, no directed-lending or social-policy mandate. The Executive Vice-Chairman is a former central-bank governor, which is a personal-history and conflict question for `07`, not state ownership.
- **(b) Listed subsidiary of a value-maximising parent — no.** Nu Holdings Ltd. **is** the top holding company; Rua California Ltd. is a personal holding vehicle with no operations that could receive steered economics, and the controller's only material asset is this stock `[FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A fn.(2)/(4); Item 4.C Organizational Structure]`.
- **(c) Sprawling unrelated conglomerate — no.** One reported segment: **Banking, US$6,991m = 100% of revenue** `[ciq_facts.json — segments_revenue, source CIQ Financials → Segments, FY2025]`. Geographically Brazil 91% / Mexico 7% / other 2%. The one pending acquisition is a Brazilian investment bank, Banco Porto Real de Investimentos S/A, squarely inside the core `[CIQ Key Developments export, M&A Transaction Announcements, 2026-07-20 — vendor export]`.

**So the conclusion is the opposite of a value trap, and should be stated plainly: the controller's US$13.0bn stake means his own wealth moves one-for-one with the Class A price, and he is not paid by anyone else.** The reason to buy is the same reason he holds. **No shareholder-friendliness cap, no governance-risk floor and no value-trap note flow from Filter 6, and none should be applied downstream.**

**What the reader is left holding, stated bluntly.** The risk here is not a misaligned owner; it is an **unaccountable** one. A Class A holder owns 22% of the economics alongside insiders and effectively none of the vote. The CEO cannot be removed, a dividend cannot be declared, shares cannot be issued and executive pay cannot be set without one man's consent; and the day he falls below 50% the board staggers itself and no shareholder can call a meeting. Nothing in the record suggests he has used any of it against minorities — but the protection against that is his judgement, not any right a Class A holder can exercise. That is a structural discount to price, not a red flag to escalate, and it is handed to `05_board-and-shareholder-rights` and `99` as the primary input to Shareholder friendliness.

Note for §27 hygiene: nothing here is graded down for being a foreign or non-English structure — the point is that the ultimate owners are identifiable, and they are. | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A fn.(2), (3), (4), pp.203–204` |

Both are present in the record: the 20-F cites **BlackRock's Schedule 13G filed 2024-11-08** and **Baillie Gifford's Schedule 13G filed 2025-04-30**, each with the sole voting and dispositive power detail. No takeover-code adjudication, open-offer trigger or stake-disclosure enforcement appears anywhere in the filed record. There is no 75% controller cap in this regime; the founder is at 74.4% of votes by design. | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 7.A fn.(5) and fn.(6), p.204`; `CIQ Insider Trading export, Trade Date vs Filed Date fields and footnote 3 — vendor export` |

## 5. Ownership / Insider Read

**Skin in the game is real and it was built, not granted.** Insiders own **21.99% of the company** — David Vélez alone holds 906,212,615 shares worth about **US$13.0bn** at the 28-Aug-2026 close of US$14.30, and his Class B stock is founder equity from a business he started in 2013 that **cannot be issued under either compensation plan**; his stake has not moved in five annual filings (88.6% → 88.3% of Class B). Against that, the incremental behaviour is one-directional: in the entire observed transaction record there were **zero open-market purchases by anyone** and four open-market sales of 592,707 shares for about **US$9.0m**, and the eye-catching "+4,015,012 net" figure is RSU grants and a US$0.29-strike option exercise, not accumulation — quote it as buying and you have inverted the signal. Nobody bought at the US$11.20 low; the Lead Independent Director sold 11.9% of her holding at US$12.24.

**The insider signal is therefore mild net selling with clean conduct.** Every sale landed after a results release, never before one; the quarterly uniform-price sales to the issuer look like tax withholding on vesting and are treated as neutral; there is **no pledge disclosed by any insider (0% of holding, 0% of capital)**, so RF-OWN-001, RF-OWN-002 and RF-OWN-003 all stay unfired, consistent with the disqualifier scan's independent 0% computation. The two things to keep watching are that the company's own policy **permits** insiders to pledge (banning it only 15 days before earnings, where best practice bans it outright), and that the largest sales, US$4.3m, went off one day after a strong quarter at US$15.80 with the stock 9.5% lower two weeks later.

**The biggest risk to a minority holder is not misalignment — it is powerlessness.** Filter 6 is tested and clean: no government, no parent creaming value off at another listing, one segment and 91% of revenue in one country, and a controller whose entire fortune is this share price — so this is **not** a value trap and must not be discounted as one. But the price of that alignment is a 20:1 dual-class with a sunset that requires Class B voting power to fall below 10% when it is 84.2% today, controlled-company exemptions actually taken (no stand-alone nominating committee, no requirement for a fully independent compensation committee), a founder veto over dividends, share issuance, M&A, affiliate transactions and executive pay that survives until he falls below **10%** of the vote, and — the provision that deserves the most attention — a board that **staggers itself into three classes and a shareholder body that loses the right to requisition a meeting at the precise moment the founder drops below 50%**. Class A holders own 22% of the economics alongside insiders and about 15.6% of the vote in total. On today's evidence the controller has used none of this against them; there is simply no mechanism by which they could stop him if that changed.

| Insider / promoter ownership | 23 | 25 | Insiders hold **21.99%** of shares outstanding (1,068,718,206 sh); the founder alone holds **18.6%** (906,212,615 sh, ~US$13.0bn), stable across five annual filings at 88.3–88.8% of Class B (04-001, 04-002, 04-003). ## management-governance / 05_board-and-shareholder-rights.md

_Source: `05_board-and-shareholder-rights.md`_

# Board & Shareholder Rights — NU

**Company:** Nu Holdings Ltd. (NYSE: NU) · Cayman Islands exempted company · NYSE-listed **foreign private issuer** · reporting in **US$** under **IFRS Accounting Standards** · fiscal year = calendar year.
**Jurisdiction note (CLAUDE.md §27):** the proxy-equivalent here is **Form 20-F Items 6, 7 and 16G plus the AGM Form 6-K**, not a DEF 14A. Nu files no DEF 14A, and that is a regime fact, not a data gap. Where a US or Indian rule (NYSE 303A, SEBI LODR) is named below, it is named because Nu's own filing names it or because the checklist band does — the local rule that actually binds is stated each time.
**As-of date:** 2026-09-06. **Primary filing:** FY25 Form 20-F, filed 8 April 2026.

---

## 1. Board Composition

| Feature | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Board size | **9 directors** as of 8 Apr 2026 (8 in the FY24 20-F; 9 at 31 Dec 2023; 8 at 31 Dec 2022). Articles cap the board at the number a majority of directors sets, "being up to nine directors on the date of adoption" | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.A, p.187`; `FY24 Form 20-F (16 Apr 2025), Item 6.A`; `FY23 Form 20-F (19 Apr 2024), Item 6.A, p.271`; `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 10.B, p.218` |
| Independent directors (%) — vs the applicable floor | **7 of 9 = 77.8%** independent by the company's own designation. Applicable floor: **none**. Nu is a **"controlled company"** and expressly elects not to comply with the NYSE 303A.01 majority-independent-board requirement, and separately follows Cayman home-country practice in lieu of it. Prior year: **7 of 8 = 87.5%**. **Trend: deteriorating** — David Alexandre Marcus carried the "* Independent Director" designation in the FY24 20-F and does **not** carry it in the FY25 20-F | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.A, p.187` (asterisk footnote); `FY24 Form 20-F, Item 6.A`; `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.C — Controlled Company Exception, p.201`; `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 16G, p.243` |
| Chair / CEO split? Chair non-executive, non-promoter? Designated (not rotating)? | **No split.** David Vélez Osorno is **Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer** simultaneously, and controls **74.3–74.4% of voting power**. The chair is therefore executive AND the controller. Counterweight: a **designated Lead Independent Director** (Anita Mary Sands, since Oct 2022) — a real, named, non-rotating role, but the 20-F discloses **no charter, powers or agenda-setting rights** for it | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.A, p.187`; `Item 6.C, p.201`; `Item 7.A, p.203` |
| Woman director / independent woman director | **2 of 9 = 22.2%** (Sands, Reses) — both independent, neither related to the controller. **No statutory diversity floor** applies to a Cayman FPI; 22.2% sits below the UK UKLR 6.6.6 40% target and below the ~30%+ large-cap norm | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.A, p.187` |
| Meeting count, longest gap, ID present in every quorum (A1-14) | **Not disclosed** — no meeting count, no attendance, no gap data anywhere in the 20-F, and none is required of an FPI. Structurally: the Articles set board quorum at "a **simple majority of the directors then in office**", with **no requirement that any independent director be present**, and the chairman has **no casting vote** | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 10.B — Proceedings of the Board of Directors, p.218` |
| Audit / Comp (NRC) / Nominating committee independence | **Audit and Risk Committee: 3 of 3 independent (100%)**, chaired by a designated audit-committee financial expert. **Compensation and People Committee: 3 of 4 independent (75%)** — Marcus is on it and is no longer designated independent; the charter expressly relies on "certain exemptions… for foreign private issuers and controlled companies". **There is no nominating or corporate-governance committee at all** — Nu takes the NYSE 303A.04 exemption, so director nominees are not selected by independent directors | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 6.C, pp.200–201`; `Item 16G, p.243`; `Capital IQ → Committees export (NU), as-of Aug-2026 — vendor export` |

**The one sentence that frames everything below.** Nu's board is more independent than it has to be — nobody forced 7 of 9, and the audit committee is genuinely good — but the *rights* architecture underneath it hands every decision that matters to one man, and the board has no power the controller has not chosen to leave it.

Board-wide median including the founder = 5.4y. **Attendance is disclosed for nobody**, in any year, in any filing in the pool.

**A vendor-conflict resolution (recorded, not buried).** The `Capital IQ → Board Members export` lists **Roberto de Oliveira Campos Neto** as a current *internal director* titled "Executive Vice-Chairman". The primary filing does not: the FY25 20-F places him in the **Management Team**, not the board, and the AGM nominee slate does not include him. **The filing wins (§4).** He is a KMP, not a director — which matters here, because if he were a director the independent share would fall from 77.8% to 70% and there would be two executives on a nine-person board. 07 reached the same resolution on the same primaries.

## 1B. Board Process & Renewal (A1-08 … A1-17)

| Test | Finding | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Skills matrix — per-director mapping, gaps (A1-08) | **No skills/competence matrix is disclosed.** Competencies are traceable from the bios and no core competency is unmapped: accounting/finance → Calderón (ex-PwC audit partner, four CFO seats); banking/regulation → Sands (UBS, Citi, RBC, CIBC), Moreno (IDB); payments/fintech → Marcus (PayPal, Meta), Reses (Square/Block, Lead Bank); technology/scale → Pham (Uber, Coupang), Piacentini (Amazon); venture/capital → Leone. What is absent is the **mapping document and any statement of gaps** | **Amber** | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.A, pp.188–190` |
| ID resignations, 3 years — reasons held up? (A1-09) | **One unexplained departure.** **Daniel Krepel Goldberg** was an independent director from April 2021 and became a **permanent observer of the Audit and Risk Committee in December 2023**. He appears in the FY23 20-F board table and then **vanishes** — no mention in the FY24 or FY25 20-F, none in the CIQ Key Developments export, no stated reason anywhere in the pool. The board went 9 (Dec 2023) → 8 (Apr 2025) → 9 (Apr 2026). One unexplained mid-term exit is below the "≥2 in 24 months" red band, but a director elevated into audit oversight in December and gone within roughly fifteen months, with no word said, is exactly the thing the item exists to catch | **Amber** | `FY23 20-F, Item 6.A, pp.271–272`; `FY24 20-F, Item 6.A`; `FY25 20-F, Item 6.A, p.187`; `CIQ Key Developments export — vendor export` |
| Reappointments / removals — evaluation-based? against dissent? (A1-10) | All nine directors stood for re-election at the **6 Aug 2026 AGM** and all nine were re-elected on a single slate resolution carrying **96.23% of votes cast**. **No performance evaluation is disclosed behind any reappointment**, and no director-by-director vote is disclosed — a slate vote cannot express a view on an individual. No dissenting director has been removed. The founder can remove and replace **his five designees at any time, with or without cause, by notice** | **Amber** | `SEC Form 6-K, AGM results, Ex-99.1, filed 2026-08-07 — read via EDGAR web 2026-09-06`; `FY25 20-F, Item 10.B, p.218` |
| Board evaluation — method + outcomes, or recycled boilerplate? (A1-11) | The company's governance guidelines record that **board performance reviews take place**, and that the board oversees director orientation and continuing education. **Neither the methodology nor any outcome or action is disclosed**, in the 20-F or elsewhere in the pool. No external facilitation is claimed | **Amber** | `CIQ → Takeover Defenses → Corporate Governance export (NU), as-of Aug-2026 — vendor export (sourced to the company's governance guidelines)`; `FY25 20-F, Item 6.C, pp.200–201` |
| Diversity & refreshment — median tenure, additions (A1-12) | **2 of 9 women (22.2%)**, both independent, neither promoter kin. **Median ID tenure 5.3 years**, comfortably inside the <9y green band. Additions are genuinely staggered: Pham (Sep 2022), Marcus (Mar 2023), Piacentini (Apr 2026) — three new voices in four years. No statutory floor applies. The honest caveat: 22.2% women is low against the 40% UK target and the ~30% large-cap norm | **Green** (band met; the 22.2% level noted) | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.A, p.187`; tenure arithmetic mine from the appointment dates in Item 6.A |
| Succession planning (A1-13) | Succession is **owned by a committee** — the Compensation and People Committee charter includes "reviewing our management succession planning" and "reviewing our leadership development process". The governance guidelines assert a **CEO succession plan exists**. It was also **executed, visibly and well, one level down**: the CFO handover (Lago → Rob Livingston, ex-CFO Visa North America) was announced ~6 weeks ahead, with a named successor, a stated transition to 31 Aug 2026, and the outgoing CFO retained as an adviser. What is not disclosed is any CEO bench, and the founder-CEO is 44 — the real succession problem here is not his age, it is that **his votes, not his job title, are what cannot be succeeded** | **Amber** | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.C, p.201`; `CIQ Corporate Governance export — vendor export`; `CIQ Key Developments export, Jun–Jul 2026 — vendor export` |
| Permanent / age-exempt seats — shareholder renewal within 5y (A1-15) | **No permanent seat, and no age limit.** Every director holds a **one-year term** and every one of the nine was put to shareholders on 6 Aug 2026, so the letter of the test is met. The substance is different: the Articles let the founder **designate up to five of nine directors** (a majority) for so long as he holds ≥40% of voting power, and **remove and replace them himself by notice**. Five seats are therefore renewed by shareholders only in form. There is **no retirement age** | **Amber** | `FY25 20-F, Item 10.B, p.218`; `Item 6.A — Shareholder's Agreement, p.193`; `AGM 6-K, 2026-08-07` |
| ID appointment/removal minority gate (A1-16) | **The gate does not exist — and its absence is chosen, not imposed.** Directors are elected by **ordinary resolution** (simple majority of votes cast) in a poll where the founder holds ~74.3% of the votes; there is **no cumulative voting**, **no advance-notice nomination right**, and the Articles provide **"no other right to put any proposals before annual general meetings"**. Vacancies "may be filled by the remaining Director(s)" without shareholders, "notwithstanding that the remaining Director(s) may constitute fewer than is required for a quorum". No LODR Reg 25(2A)-style majority-of-minority requirement exists in the Cayman/NYSE regime — but nothing in that regime required the designation and removal rights either. Recorded Amber on the checklist band (no local requirement can be *breached*); the substance is carried to §4 and A10-03, where it belongs | **Amber** | `FY25 20-F, Item 10.B, pp.214, 218`; `CIQ Corporate Governance export — vendor export (vacancy article text, Art. 21.2/21.5)` |
| IDs-only meeting held; D&O cover (A1-17) | **A documented conflict between two of the company's own disclosures.** The 20-F states Nu follows home-country practice **in lieu of NYSE 303A.03**, the rule requiring independent directors to have regularly scheduled meetings with only independent directors present. The company's own governance guidelines say non-employee directors "will meet in executive sessions… **no less than two times a year**", and that where non-employee directors include non-independent directors, the independent directors will also meet at least twice a year. **No affirmative disclosure that any such meeting was actually held exists in the pool.** On D&O: a policy is in force — but the 20-F describes it verbatim as covering defence costs and losses "**at a minimal limit**", which is an unusual thing for a company to say about its own directors' cover | **Amber** | `FY25 20-F, Item 16G, p.243`; `CIQ Corporate Governance export — vendor export (Executive Sessions of Non-Executive Directors)`; `FY25 20-F, Item 6.B — Directors' and Officers' Insurance, p.194` |

### Matched-basis check on every ratio quoted (CLAUDE.md §15)

| Ratio quoted | Numerator + its basis | Denominator + its basis | Matched-basis version | Basis mismatch? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Director-linked balance vs the balance sheet | **US$926k — period-end balance at 31-Dec-2025** (a stock, not a peak and not an approved cap; the note reports the closing "Assets (Liabilities)" position, and the comparative and the interim confirm it is a point-in-time series: 1,795 → 926 → 265) | **Total liabilities US$63,572,315k at 31-Dec-2025** — period-end (scope: all liabilities per the consolidated balance sheet) | **0.0015% of total liabilities** — stock over stock, same date, same statement | **No** |
| Director-linked balance vs equity | US$926k — period-end 31-Dec-2025 | **Total equity US$11,321,562k at 31-Dec-2025** — period-end | **0.008% of total equity** | **No** |
| Key-management compensation vs cost base | **US$91,269k — cumulative flow for FY2025** (twelve months) | **Total expenses US$12,032,723k — cumulative flow for FY2025** (as computed upstream in `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`) | **0.76% of FY2025 total expenses** — flow over flow, same twelve months | **No** |
| *Deliberately not quoted:* "RPT as % of revenue" | — | — | **Avoided on purpose.** Nu has two defensible revenue bases in this pool — the 20-F Note-34 base of US$12,083.8m and the Capital IQ bank-template "Total Revenue" of US$6,991.2m, which nets interest expense and provisions. A ratio whose denominator can differ by 1.7× depending on which document you open is not a measurement; the absolute figures and the two matched pairs above carry the finding instead | — | **Avoided** |

**Monitoring threshold, stated so it can be measured again.** Do **not** monitor "RPT as a share of revenue". Monitor the **absolute period-end related-party balance in Note 28(a) at each reporting date** — 1,795 (Dec-24) → 926 (Dec-25) → 265 (Jun-26), all on the identical period-end basis. **Trigger: any Note 28(a) balance above US$10 million, or the appearance of any related-party ASSET (a receivable, loan or guarantee to a related party) where today there is only a small liability.** That is testable on exactly the same line, in the same note, at the next reporting date.

**Counterparty facts (the disclosure that is missing).** The related counterparty is **not a financial entity** and is **not named**. Nu discloses only "a company where one of its Directors serves as CEO". Nu holds **no equity interest** in it that any filing discloses, there is **no approved cap** and **no utilisation figure**, and the arrangement's arm's-length character is **not asserted** in the note (unlike the credit-card/loan paragraph, which is expressly stated to be on third-party terms). Two of Nu's nine directors are sitting CEOs — **David Marcus (Lightspark)** and **Jacqueline Reses (Lead Bank)** — and `07` concludes Marcus is the near-certain counterparty. **That identification is an inference, not from filings.** It matters for one reason and one only: if it is Marcus, the counterparty is the same director whose independence designation the company dropped in the FY25 20-F while leaving him on the committee that sets executive pay.

**The minority-protection read.** The gate exists and is the right one on paper: since **March 2024** a written related-party policy requires certain RPTs to be approved by the board **or a designated committee, including the Audit and Risk Committee**, and "reviewing related-party transactions" is an express duty in that committee's charter — a committee that is **100% independent** and chaired by a genuine financial expert. What does **not** exist is any **majority-of-minority** vote, any **independent-directors-only** vote requirement, or any disclosure of **who approved this particular arrangement, when, or with what dissent**. There is also a structural oddity worth naming: the Shareholder's Agreement gives Vélez a veto over the company "entering into transactions with our officers, directors or other affiliates" — with the words "**(excluding our founding shareholder)**" in the text. He cannot veto his own related-party deals through that clause; his own would run through the board / audit-committee policy instead.

**Cross-reference.** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` computed related-party sales ÷ revenue ≈ 0.0% and related-party purchases/expenses ÷ total expenses = 0.76%, against the >25% hard-disqualifier threshold — **not tripped, by more than an order of magnitude twice over**. `RF-RPT-001/002/003 considered and NOT fired`: US$265k at the latest balance-sheet date is below every materiality band in the registry, and no loan, advance or guarantee to a related party is disclosed. **Is economic value leaking to the controller? On the disclosed evidence, no — Nu is one of the cleanest RPT files this module will see.** The leakage risk here is not through transactions. It is through control rights, which is §4.

The Shareholder's Agreement bars the company from "adopting a shareholders' rights plan" without Vélez's prior written approval while he holds ≥10% of voting power. **Blank-check preferred shares are authorised**, issuable by the board alone with any rights it fixes — the 20-F says in terms that this "may be used as an anti-takeover device without further action on the part of our shareholders" | `CIQ Takeover Defenses export — vendor export`; `FY25 20-F, Item 6.A, p.193`; `Item 10.B, pp.210, 220` |
| Classified / staggered board | **Dormant — and it arms itself precisely when control weakens** | The board is **not** classified today; every director serves a **one-year** term. But the Articles provide that **from the date Vélez ceases to own more than 50% of voting power** ("the classifying date"), the board **shall** divide into three classes on three-year staggered terms — and **"the directors nominated by our founding shareholder shall be allocated to the longest duration classes"**. A takeover defence that switches on at the exact moment the controller's block falls below a majority, with his own nominees given the longest-dated seats | `FY25 20-F, Item 6.A, p.187`; `Item 10.B — Staggered Board, p.220` |
| Dual-class / unequal voting | **Yes — 20:1, with an effectively unreachable sunset** | Class B = **20 votes**; Class A = **1 vote**. Vélez holds 88.3% of Class B, **74.3–74.4% of total voting power**, on Class A+B economics of roughly 18.6% of shares outstanding — a control-versus-economics wedge of about **56 percentage points**. Sunset: Class B converts automatically **only if aggregate Class B voting power falls below 10% of total voting power** — with a 20:1 ratio that requires the Class B share count to collapse to roughly 0.5% of the register. **There is no time-based sunset.** No cumulative voting | `FY25 20-F, Item 7.A, pp.203–204`; `Item 10.B — Voting Rights / Conversion Rights, p.210`; wedge arithmetic mine |

Removal: "with or without cause by ordinary resolution", and the founder may remove **his** designees by notice alone. *(The `CIQ Takeover Defenses` export reports "Removal of Directors Only for Cause — Yes"; the filing says the opposite and the filing wins, §4. ## 4A. Shareholder Voting & Dilution

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| AGM votes against | **AGM of 6 August 2026 — two resolutions only.** Proposal 1 (approve and ratify the FY2025 audited financials and the Form 20-F): **99.88% of votes cast in favour**. Proposal 2 (re-elect all nine directors, as one slate): **96.23% of votes cast in favour**. **I verified this against the primary document myself** — the 6-K exhibit filed 2026-08-07 — rather than take the sibling agent's figure on trust; it checks out verbatim. **No vote counts, no against/abstain numbers, and no per-director breakdown are disclosed.** There was **no say-on-pay resolution and no auditor-ratification resolution** — neither is required of an FPI, so shareholders had no vote on pay or on the auditor at all | `SEC Form 6-K, AGM results, Ex-99.1, filed 2026-08-07 — read via EDGAR web 2026-09-06 (primary filing, web-retrieved)`; `CIQ Key Developments export (AGM agenda) — vendor export` |
| Proxy-advisor recommendations (ISS / Glass Lewis / IiAS) | **Not available in the pool**, and none located. Insufficient Data | — |
| Institutional opposition | **Not separately disclosed and not derivable from the filing.** The two largest disclosed institutions, BlackRock (266.2m Class A, 6.9% of Class A, **1.1% of votes**) and Baillie Gifford (265.2m Class A, 6.9%, **1.1% of votes**), together command 2.2% of the vote against the founder's ~74.4%. **What can be derived, and should be:** see the arithmetic below | `FY25 20-F, Item 7.A, p.203` |
| Dilution history | **Low and now reversing.** Shares outstanding 4,824.4m (Mar-25) → 4,855.7m (Dec-25) → 4,861.7m (Mar-26) → **4,830.7m (Jun-26)** — roughly +0.65% a year of RSU creep, then a reduction after the **US$1.0bn buyback** authorised 4 June 2026 (12-month programme to 3 June 2027). **No equity raise since the December 2021 IPO** (US$2,541.7m); only a shelf registration. No preferential allotment, no warrants, no promoter-priced issue | `CIQ Financials → Historical Capitalization export — vendor export`; `CIQ Key Developments export — vendor export`; `Transaction Summary → Public Offerings export — vendor export` |

**Deriving what the 96.23% actually says about minority holders (inference, not from filings — bases labelled).**
A headline of 96.23% "for" in a company where one man holds ~74.4% of the votes is close to uninformative until the founder's block is stripped out. Two bounds, both built from primary numbers:

- **Floor case (uses only primary inputs).** Share counts at 1 March 2026 (20-F Item 7.A): 3,837,998,543 Class A × 1 vote + 1,022,600,698 Class B × 20 votes = **24,290,012,503 total votes**. If every vote entitled had been cast, votes against = 3.77% × 24.29bn ≈ **916m**, and non-founder votes = 25.6% × 24.29bn ≈ **6,218m** → **≈14.7% of non-founder votes cast against the slate**.
- **Upper case (adds one secondary input, labelled).** Press summaries of the same 6-K report a quorum of ~23bn shares, 94.30% of shares entitled to vote; **the 6-K exhibit I read does not state the quorum**, so this input is secondary and unverified. On 94.30% turnout with the founder voting his whole block in favour: against ≈ 3.77% × 22.91bn ≈ **864m**, non-founder votes present ≈ 4,834m → **≈17.9%**.

**So roughly 15–18% of non-founder votes cast were against re-electing this board — four to five times the headline number.** Three basis caveats travel with that: the share counts are a **1 March 2026** snapshot against an **August 2026** meeting (RSU vesting grows Class A, which nudges the founder's share down slightly and the estimate up); "votes cast" may exclude abstentions, which would raise the implied against-share further; and it assumes the founder voted his entire block in favour, which for a slate containing himself is near-certain but is not disclosed.

**RF-SHR-001 (high votes against a key resolution) — considered and NOT fired.** The headline 3.77% against is far below the 20% significant-dissent line, and the derived non-founder dissent of 15–18% is below it too, on my own inference rather than a disclosed number. Firing a red flag on a figure I derived, against a threshold it does not reach, would be inventing a finding. **It is recorded as an Amber with a live follow-up**: if Nu ever discloses per-resolution vote counts, or if the next AGM's headline slips below ~95%, the implied non-founder dissent crosses 20% and this becomes a red flag.
**RF-SHR-002 (controversial preferential allotment / warrants / dilution) — considered and NOT fired.** No allotment, warrant or discounted issue to the controller has occurred; the structural asymmetry is recorded as Amber at A10-04 below.

## 5. Minority-Shareholder Protection Read

The board itself is better than it needed to be — 7 of 9 independent when the controlled-company exemption required none, a **100%-independent audit committee chaired by a real financial expert**, a genuinely trivial related-party file (US$265 thousand at 30 June 2026), no pledging, no leakage, and a CFO succession executed the way it should be — so this is not a story about a captured or lazy board, and the honest verdict on stewardship conduct is that nothing here has been abused. But a board's quality is capped by its authority, and this one has almost none that the founder has not chosen to leave it: **20:1 voting with a sunset that will effectively never trigger, a contractual right for the founder to designate five of nine directors and remove them by notice, a standing veto over dividends, share issues, mergers, officer pay and any rights plan, no shareholder right to nominate a director or put a single proposal to a meeting, no right to requisition a meeting at all once his stake falls below half, a staggered board that arms itself at that exact moment with his nominees given the longest terms, and Class B-only anti-dilution rights so every future share issue dilutes the minority and not him.** Two specific things sharpen it from structure into conduct: the company **quietly dropped David Marcus's independence designation between the FY24 and FY25 20-F while leaving him on the committee that sets executive pay, and explained nothing**; and an independent director elevated to audit-committee observer in December 2023 (Daniel Goldberg) simply disappeared from the board with no reason ever given.

**Conclusion: weak / entrenched.** Not because value is being taken — on the disclosed evidence it is not — but because nothing in the architecture would stop it, and the one number that hints at how minority holders actually feel (roughly **15–18% of non-founder votes cast against the board slate**, derived, versus a headline 96.23%) is the only vote they get to cast, on a slate they cannot amend, for a board five of whose seats are not theirs to fill.

*On §24 Filter 6 / RF-OWN-004:* it does **not** apply here. Vélez is a founder-controller whose own economics are per-share, not a government, not a value-maximising parent of a listed subsidiary, and not an unrelated conglomerate — so the mandatory "no better than weak/entrenched" lock is not engaged by that route. **`04_ownership-and-insider-behavior` has not run and is not available to this agent** (same layer); if it reaches a different read on control alignment, the synthesis reconciles it. I reach "weak / entrenched" on the rights evidence above, independently.

**Shareholder friendliness /100 (the module-level score this agent feeds): 50.** Not capped for partial data — board, committee, RPT, charter and AGM disclosure are all present and primary; the gaps (attendance, meeting counts, evaluation outcomes, per-resolution vote counts) are regime-permitted omissions, recorded as Amber, not as a missing-input cap.

**Red-flag count from this agent: 0 fired.** Four were explicitly considered and not fired, each with its reason recorded in the row: **RF-SHR-001** (dissent below 20% on both the disclosed and the derived basis), **RF-SHR-002** (no allotment event), **RF-RPT-001/002/003** (below every materiality band), **RF-OWN-004** (a founder-controller is not a structurally unaligned owner under §24 Filter 6 — that filter names government control, listed subsidiaries of value-maximising parents, and unrelated conglomerates). The Red findings in this report — combined chair/CEO, no independent chair, true-independence concerns, overboarding, dual class, no requisition right — have **no canonical ID in the Red-Flag Registry**, and I have not invented one. The entrenchment here is structural, disclosed and lawful, which is exactly why it needs to be stated in the verdict rather than laundered through a flag count.

# Candor & Disclosure Quality — NU

**Ticker:** NU (Nu Holdings Ltd.) · **Line read:** NYSE:NU Class A ordinary shares, USD · **Date:** 2026-09-06 · **Reporting:** IFRS, fiscal year ends 31 December · **Data pool:** `data/NU/` (citation label; every read resolved inside the frozen extraction generation `f9081efa…09f2be`).

**Jurisdiction note (CLAUDE.md §27).** NU is a Cayman-incorporated **US foreign private issuer**. There is no DEF 14A, no 10-Q and no 8-K. The annual filing is the **Form 20-F**; quarterly results are furnished as preliminary interim reports and interim condensed financial statements; management commentary sits in the quarterly earnings calls. The absence of a US domestic form is not missing data.

**Data adequacy for this agent — no partial-data cap applies.** The pool contains **20 verbatim S&P Global Market Intelligence earnings-call transcripts** (Q4 2021 through Q2 2026), so tone, owning-the-miss and Q&A behaviour are assessed from management's actual words, not from a paraphrase. Both cross-module inputs were available and used: `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` and `earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md`, plus `01_management-and-track-record.md` and `business-model/03_segment-map.md`.

**Web use.** None.

---

## 1. Owning the Misses

The misses come from `01_management-and-track-record.md`, Section 4. NU publishes **no revenue, EPS, EBITDA or capex guidance at all**, so the testable promise set is small — four scoreable items, one open, one not assessable. What follows judges how each was communicated.

| Miss (from 01) | How It Was Communicated | Owned or Obscured? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **IFRS effective tax rate came in at 14.2% in Q2'26, below the 15–20% range guided three months earlier** (a miss in the direction that flatters earnings) | The guide was given **unprompted and directly** on 2026-05-14: *"Now I want to be direct about our effective tax rate, or ETR, because we know it may be a focus… For modeling purposes, we expect our IFRS ETR for the remainder of 2026 to converge towards the 15% to 20% range. Our managerial ETR, **which we believe is the more economically meaningful comparison**, should converge towards the 30% to 35% range."* Then, on the quarter it was tested, **the word "tax" appears zero times in the entire Q2'26 call** — prepared remarks and Q&A. Not restated, not withdrawn, not explained; and no analyst asked | **Obscured — by omission, on the one line that mattered most.** `earnings/04` measured that **96.7% of the 12.6% Q2'26 net-income beat came from the tax line** while pre-tax landed +0.5% versus consensus. The guide the company beat (efficiency ratio) was explicitly reiterated on the same call; the guide it missed was silently dropped | Guide: `Q1 2026 earnings-call transcript, May-14-2026, prepared remarks — Guilherme Marques do Lago, CFO`. Silence: `Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, Aug-13-2026` (full-text search: "tax" = 0 occurrences). Outcome and beat decomposition: `earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md, §6–7`; `Q2'26 interim condensed consolidated financial statements, statements of income, three months ended 06/30/2026` |
| **Risk-adjusted net interest margin fell for six quarters** (~11% mid-2024 → 9.5% Q4'24 → **8.2% Q1'25**), against the Q3'23 claim that higher delinquency would be *"more than offset by additional revenues"* | Disclosed and decomposed **in prepared remarks, before any analyst asked**: *"This dynamic weighed on our risk-adjusted NIM, which declined to 8.2%. Of the 130-basis-point reduction, roughly 3/4 stemmed from seasonal effects on CLA with the remaining impact primarily linked to short-term NIM pressures in Mexico and Colombia."* When an analyst pressed harder in Q&A (*"it has been slipping a little bit… for several quarters now… the biggest surprise for me this quarter was the higher cost of risk"*), the CFO pointed to a named slide, repeated the 3/4–1/4 split, benchmarked the Q1'25 cost-of-risk move against Q1'23 and Q1'24, and gave a forward view by country | **Owned.** The number was volunteered, the decline was quantified in basis points, and the causes were split with weights. The attribution was management-asserted rather than audited, and it took until Q2'26 (12.4%) to recover — but nothing was buried | `Q1 2025 earnings-call transcript, May-13-2025, prepared remarks and Q&A`; recovery: `Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, Aug-13-2026, Q&A` |
| **Q1'26 missed consensus on both lines** (revenue −1.8%, GAAP EPS −5.2%) while the headline efficiency ratio hit a record low 17.6% | The CEO flagged the flattering number **in his own opening remarks** — *"a record low efficiency ratio below 18%, a result that reflects both structural progress and **some timing benefits** that Lago will unpack shortly"* — and the CFO then quantified it: *"Roughly 1/3 reflects structural efficiency gains that are durable… the remaining 2/3 reflect timing items that will normalize in the next quarters, including real estate and marketing phasing. **So the 17.6% efficiency ratio should not be extrapolated as our run rate.**"* One quarter later he confirmed the reversal: *"As we discussed last quarter, the 17.6% reported in Q1 was not a run rate. Roughly 2/3 of that improvement reflected temporary timing effects, which reversed as expected this quarter"* | **Owned — and this is the strongest single candor signal in the file.** Management talked down its own record number, in advance, with a weighted split, and then reported the reversal as promised. Talking down a good number is the behaviour most companies never produce | `Q1 2026 earnings-call transcript, May-14-2026, prepared remarks`; `Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript, Aug-13-2026, prepared remarks` |
| **Q4'25 missed on profit** (EPS −1.6%, net income −4.0% vs consensus) on a quarter whose reported tax rate fell | Asked directly (*"there is one line here that I think investors are a little bit more puzzled this quarter. That is the tax rate"*), the CFO **itemised three one-offs, two of which were negatives management had not led with**: a **+US$58m** deferred-tax-asset remeasurement (*"the portion that I attribute as a nonrecurring one-off event"*), a **−US$25m** Prosofipo expense and a **−US$22m** return-to-office provision. He also volunteered that the same Brazilian law change is *"in the medium term… a headwind for our effective tax rate"* | **Owned.** Numbers given, recurring separated from non-recurring by name, and a forward negative disclosed unprompted | `Q4 2025 earnings-call transcript, Feb-25-2026, Q&A — Guilherme Marques do Lago, CFO` |
| **Cost to serve reached the exact ceiling management twice publicly committed to hold** — US$0.70 per active customer per month (Q1'25) → **US$1.00 (Q1'26 and Q2'26)**, +14% year on year FX-neutral | The commitment was a headline: *"maintaining a low cost to serve, which we aim to keep at or below the $1 level for the foreseeable future"* (Q4'23) and *"we remain committed to keeping our cost at or below $1 per active customer for the foreseeable future. Once again, we achieved this goal with a cost to serve per active customer of $0.80"* (Q4'24). From the **Q4'25 call onward the commitment is never restated and no consolidated number is spoken**; the metric survives only as an appendix chart (slide 28) in the deck | **Neither owned nor hidden — quietly retired.** The number is still published with an unchanged definition, so this is not a dropped KPI. But a stated commitment reached its limit and management stopped mentioning it in the same quarter, rather than saying "we are now at the line and here is why". The mitigating fact, which must travel with the finding: ARPAC rose faster over the same six quarters (US$11.6 → US$17.1, +22% YoY FX-neutral), so the operating leverage claim itself still holds | Commitments: `Q4 2023 earnings-call transcript, Feb-22-2024, prepared remarks`; `Q4 2024 earnings-call transcript, Feb-20-2025, prepared remarks`. Levels and definition: `Q2'26 Earnings Presentation, Aug-13-2026, Appendix slide 28 and Notes 2–3`. Silence: `Q4 2025`, `Q1 2026`, `Q2 2026` transcripts |
| **Senior departures never announced** — President & COO Youssef Lahrech and CTO Vitor Guarino Olivier both vanished from the management table and the calls with no statement or successor (finding owned by `01`) | No announcement anywhere in the pool: no press release, no 6-K, no transcript reference, no 20-F narrative | **Obscured (by silence).** Referenced here, not re-adjudicated — `01` owns it and grades it Amber | `01_management-and-track-record.md, §2`; `FY24 Form 20-F (filed 2025-04-16), Item 6.A` vs `FY25 Form 20-F (filed 2026-04-08), Item 6.A` |

**A factual correction to two upstream reports, recorded because it changes who is accountable for the guidance.** Both `earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md` and `01_management-and-track-record.md` attribute the Q1'26 tax-rate guide and the risk-adjusted-NIM comment to **"Rob Livingston, CFO"**. The verbatim transcript's Call Participants list for the Q1 2026 call (May-14-2026) names **Guilherme Marques do Lago as Chief Financial Officer**; "Livingston" appears zero times in that transcript. Livingston first appears as CFO on the **Q2 2026** call (Aug-13-2026), consistent with his 2026-07-13 start date. The substance of both guides is unaffected; the point that matters for candor is that **the outgoing CFO set the tax guide and the incoming CFO ran the call on which it was missed and not mentioned.**

## 2. Non-GAAP / Adjustment Aggressiveness

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Recurring "one-off" addbacks** | **Present, and it is the whole of the profit adjustment.** NU's only non-IFRS profit measure, **Adjusted Net Income**, is IFRS net income plus **share-based compensation and its tax effects** — a real, cash-equivalent cost that appears in **every period on record** (US$212.6m FY2023, US$272.4m FY2024, US$271.8m FY2025, US$216.8m H1'26 in the cash-flow statement; the reconciliation add-back is larger at US$359.0m in FY2025 because it also carries payroll and social-security taxes on vested awards). A second item behaves the same way: the Brazilian **CSLL rate-change deferred-tax remeasurement**, described by the CFO as *"the portion that I attribute as a nonrecurring one-off event"* (+US$58.5m FY2025), reappeared the very next reporting period (+US$28.4m H1'26) | `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md, §4–5`; `FY25 Form 20-F, Non-IFRS Financial Measures and Reconciliations`; `Q4 2025 earnings-call transcript, Feb-25-2026, Q&A` |
| **GAAP-to-adjusted gap (magnitude / trend)** | **+US$203.7m on FY2025 reported net income to parent of US$2,868.9m = +7.1%**, and **shrinking**: +16.1% (FY2023) → +11.9% (FY2024) → **+7.1% (FY2025)**. It does not touch revenue, credit losses, funding costs or tax. There is no adjusted EBITDA, no adjusted EBIT and no adjusted EPS | `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md, §4 and §7`; `FY25 Form 20-F, Non-IFRS Financial Measures` |
| **Does adjusted framing flatter reality?** | **On the profit measure, no — the company headlines the conservative figure.** The Q2'26 deck and every recent call lead with **IFRS net income** (US$1.1bn), not Adjusted Net Income, and the phrase "Adjusted Net Income" was spoken **zero times** on all six calls from Q1'25 to Q2'26. **On the framework, the footprint has widened materially and this is the finding.** From the **Q4'25 results (Feb-25-2026)** the company introduced a **Managerial P&L** and every metric it now communicates sits on it: *"All financial metrics discussed and presented today reflect our managerial P&L framework."* The deck describes it as *"supplemental, non-audited, non-IFRS"*, built from *"reclassifications and tax-equivalency adjustments"*. So the gross revenue, gross profit, margin and efficiency-ratio figures management speaks about are no longer IFRS quantities — even though net income, cash flow, equity and regulatory capital are preserved and a full IFRS bridge is published. A third, smaller item: a **"core efficiency ratio" of 16.6%**, excluding return-to-office, international-expansion and AI-infrastructure spend, was introduced on the Q1'26 call — the quarter with the record-low headline ratio — and **never used again** | `Q4 2025 earnings-call transcript, Feb-25-2026, prepared remarks`; `Q1 2026` and `Q2 2026 earnings-call transcripts, opening disclaimer`; `Q2'26 Earnings Presentation, Aug-13-2026, "Managerial P&L · Framework, reclassifications & tax-equivalency" and "Definitions & rationale · Adjusted Net Income"`; `Q1 2026 earnings-call transcript, May-14-2026, prepared remarks` |

**Cross-check against `earnings/06`, including where it and I differ.** `earnings/06` and I agree on the profit measure: one reconciled non-IFRS metric, recurring share-based-compensation add-back triggered, gap +7.1% and falling, no impairment, no restructuring, no change of useful life, no accounting-policy change, no restatement. **We differ on scope.** `earnings/06` §4 records that *"NU publishes one non-IFRS profit measure, Adjusted Net Income… plus a family of FX-Neutral growth measures"* and does not capture the **Managerial P&L framework** introduced at Q4'25, which now governs every metric management communicates and carries its own tax-equivalency adjustments. That is a material addition to the non-IFRS footprint and is routed to the module synthesis as a cross-module reconciliation item, not as a disagreement about any number.

**Three mitigations, stated so the finding is not read as worse than it is.** (i) A standalone **Managerial P&L reconciliation report** with the full IFRS bridge and methodology is published, and the bridge is reproduced in the deck appendix. (ii) **Historical data was restated back to Q1 2021** on the new basis, so the five-year series remains comparable to itself. (iii) The framework is *"net-income neutral"* — it cannot manufacture profit. The cost it did impose is real and management named it themselves: *"We are aware that consensus estimates across the sell side reflect the mix of IFRS and managerial frameworks, and we encourage everyone to use the reconciliation report as a reference point for aligning models."* The very next print (Q1'26) missed both revenue and EPS against that mixed-basis consensus.

---

## 3. Disclosure Transparency

On the things it chooses to show, NU is specific and quantified — cohort ARPAC curves out to month 90, a basis-point bridge for early delinquency (seasonality −37bp, deliberate risk expansion +24bp in Q2'26), coverage of 90-plus balances at 244%, and per-country deposits, customers and regulatory capital ratios. What it does not show is **profit**: the group reports **one operating segment** and discloses **no country margin, no product margin and no country net income**, and roughly a fifth to a quarter of what it earns (US$3,691.0m of FY2025 interest and fee income, 23.4%) sits outside the geographic revenue split entirely `[FY25 Form 20-F, Note 34; business-model/03_segment-map.md, §1–3]`. It also issues no revenue, EPS, EBITDA or capex guidance of any kind `[earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md, §2]`.

**Two disclosures got LESS transparent, and both are warnings.** First, the **geographic breakdown narrowed**: the FY2023 20-F named Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, the Cayman Islands, the United States, Germany and Argentina separately; from the FY2024 20-F onward everything except Brazil and Mexico is collapsed into "Other countries" — a bucket that is only 2.0% of revenue but **13.9% of group non-current assets** and that now conceals Colombia, an operating bank with 5m+ customers and US$3.3bn of deposits, plus the new US entity `[FY23 Form 20-F (filed 2024-04-19), Segment information note; FY25 Form 20-F, Note 34(b); business-model/03_segment-map.md, §3]`. Second, **cost to serve moved from a spoken "pillar of our strategy" with a stated ceiling to an unspoken appendix chart in the same quarter the metric reached that ceiling** (US$1.00, Q1'26 and Q2'26, from US$0.70 in Q1'25) `[Q4 2023 and Q4 2024 transcripts; Q2'26 Earnings Presentation, Appendix slide 28]`.

---

## 4. Tone in Bad Times

The worst recent periods are **Q1'25** (risk-adjusted NIM trough of 8.2%) and **Q1'26** (a double miss — revenue −1.8%, GAAP EPS −5.2% against consensus). In both, the tone was **candid rather than promotional on the specific bad number**: the 8.2% NIM and its 130-basis-point decline were volunteered in prepared remarks with a 3/4–1/4 causal split before any question was asked, and the flattering 17.6% efficiency ratio was actively talked down by management itself — *"should not be extrapolated as our run rate"* — a call that was then proved right one quarter later. Q&A is answered directly and with numbers rather than deflected: on the hardest question of the last two years (Q4'25, the tax rate) the CFO itemised three one-offs including two negatives and volunteered that the same law change becomes *"a headwind"* later, and in Q2'26 the new CFO corrected an analyst who put words in his mouth — *"I would correct one thing you said… you said that 12% is a floor. I didn't say that it was a floor… I don't want to overcommit there."*

The countervailing feature of the tone is **framing, not falsehood**: the CEO opens every call with the same growth formula (*"13 years later, that hypothesis continues to play out exactly as we envisioned"*), attributes a record profit to *"customer obsession translated into an earnings-generating formula"*, and the Q1'26 script called a quarter that missed both consensus lines *"another clean expression of that model"*. The numbers management named as the sequential drivers of that record quarter — revenue +8% sequentially, risk-adjusted NIM up almost 3 points — are corroborated by the filings, so this is promotional packaging around accurate operating detail, not commentary contradicting the numbers.

---

## 5. Candor Read

**Verdict: mixed — leaning candid, held back by one specific and repeatable pattern.** On the evidence that matters most, management does tell the truth when the number is bad: it volunteered an 8.2% risk-adjusted margin with a weighted decomposition before being asked, it talked down its own record-low 17.6% efficiency ratio as *"not a run rate"* and was proved right, it itemised two negative one-offs alongside one positive when only the positive was being asked about, and its CFO publicly refused to be pinned to a floor he had not given. That behaviour is uncommon and it is the strongest evidence for trusting this management in a bad quarter.

What holds the verdict at mixed is that the **selectivity runs one way**. The guide the company was beating — the ~20% full-year efficiency ratio — was explicitly reiterated on the Q2'26 call. The guide it had just missed **to the flattering side** — the 15–20% IFRS effective tax rate — was not mentioned once on that call, in a quarter where `earnings/04` shows **96.7% of a 12.6% net-income beat came from the tax line** while pre-tax profit landed within 0.5% of consensus, and where the deferred tax asset that generates the benefit has reached **27.5% of parent equity**. The same pattern appears in the cost-to-serve commitment, retired without comment in the quarter the metric hit the US$1.00 ceiling management had twice promised to hold, and in the geographic disclosure that narrowed from seven named countries to three buckets. Weighed against the trust read, and not set aside, are two items routed from upstream: `01`'s finding that the **President & COO and the CTO both left with no announcement, no reason and no successor**, and `01`'s confirmation that `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` routed **no unresolved adverse integrity signal** (so `RF-MGT-005` is not emitted here either) — the first weighs against, the second does not clear the first.

**The single biggest candor signal:** management is candid about what the operating business is doing and silent about the line that is actually producing the earnings surprise.

**Standalone red-flag tags (CLAUDE.md §13).**

`RF-DISC-002 (recurring "one-off" / aggressive non-GAAP add-backs)` — triggered at **Medium** severity: share-based compensation, a cost incurred in every period on record (US$212.6m / US$272.4m / US$271.8m / US$216.8m H1'26), is added back to Adjusted Net Income every year; and the CSLL deferred-tax remeasurement the CFO called *"a nonrecurring one-off event"* (+US$58.5m FY2025) recurred the next period (+US$28.4m H1'26). Severity is Medium, not High, because the add-back is +7.1% of reported profit and falling, and the company headlines the IFRS figure.

`RF-DISC-001 (commentary contradicting the numbers)` — **tested and NOT triggered.** The sequential drivers management named for the record Q2'26 quarter (revenue +8% sequentially, risk-adjusted NIM +~3 points, cost of credit contributing 115bp) are corroborated by the filings and the deck. The defect found is omission of the tax line, not an assertion the numbers contradict, so the tag is not emitted.

`RF-REG-002 (delayed results / material-disclosure timeliness)` — **tested and NOT triggered.** Results have been published 44 days after each of Q3'25, Q1'26 and Q2'26 and 56 days after Q4'25; the FY2025 Form 20-F was filed 2026-04-08, 98 days after the 31-December year-end and inside the four-month foreign-private-issuer deadline (prior years 2025-04-16, 2024-04-19, 2023-04-20, 2022-04-21). Timeliness (A7-01) is owned by `12_regulatory-legal-and-compliance`; the unannounced senior departures are a disclosure-**completeness** matter owned by `01`, not a timeliness breach.

(CNPJ 18.236.120/0001-58, opened 4 June 2013), which is a **disclosed, consolidated, still-active subsidiary** of the listco and the registered proprietor of its core brands. **A1-05 — Director & KMP reputation (verdict line).** **AMBER.** Twenty-five named people were swept and graded: **22 Clean, 3 Minor concerns, 0 Material concerns, 0 Disqualifying.** No controller, CEO, CFO or board chair carries any adverse record, so the A1-05 red band — "any controller / CEO / CFO / chair graded Material concerns or Disqualifying" — is **not** met and the Non-Negotiable Gate is not engaged from this agent's side. It is not Green either, because the green band requires *every* person Clean and three are not: two of the three Minor grades are **exposure floors carrying no personal record** (Calderón via Grupo Casas Bahia; Leone via Sequoia Capital), and one is a genuine own-record item on a KMP (Campos Neto's ethics proceeding and revolving-door move). The single most decision-relevant fact is that the exposure sits on the **chair of the Audit and Risk Committee**, i.e. the board's principal gatekeeping seat.

## 2. Per-Person Dossiers

**Output-budget note.** Full axis tables are given for every **Tier A** person and for the two people carrying a flag. The remaining nineteen swept people — all Clean, all Tier B/C — are carried as **completed compact rows in §1**, not as scope-boundary items: a compact row is a finished sweep with its grade, its coverage and its Sweep Log rows intact, and any hit would have promoted that person straight back to a full dossier. Six full person subsections are used of the 40-subsection ceiling (see §5).
