I confirm that negative from my own read of Note 24: the only guarantee beneficiary named is a wholly-owned regulated subsidiary. **Cross-reference A5-03 <-> A7a-06; the exposure is counted once, in `10`.**

**The one honest gap in this section.** Nu is a **bank**. It issues credit cards and loans to its own directors and executives - the note says so - and it has **never quantified them**, in any of five years, despite Form 20-F Item 7.B asking specifically for "amounts outstanding on loans" to key management. The company's answer is a materiality judgement it has not shown its working for. Given the individuals involved are compensated in the tens of millions and the group's loan book is US$11.3bn, a genuinely material director loan book is implausible - but "implausible" is an inference, not a disclosure. **Recorded Amber under A5-05, with the exact document that would settle it named in Section 14.**

**The controlling shareholder's own vehicle is a share-holding company, not a trading one.** David Velez Osorno holds 901,624,498 Class B shares of record through **Rua California Ltd.**, "a company controlled by David Velez Osorno, who holds 100% of its shares" [`FY25 20-F, Item 7.A, p.~197`]. Rua California appears in the CIQ corporate tree only as a **minority investor in NU**, with no operating business, no industry classification and no disclosed transaction with the group [`CIQ Corporate Structure Tree (NU), retrieved 2026-08-29 - tier-5 vendor export`]. **Identification of the Rodamoinho counterparty (labelled inference).** A web sweep on 2026-09-06 establishes that **Grupo Rodamoinho was founded in 2014 by Larissa de Macedo Machado ("Anitta")**, whose company runs concert and event production. Anitta joined NU's board in 2021 and left in 2022 - which matches the note's "a former member of the Company's Board of Directors, who has not been a member of the Board since September 2022." Two matching facts, so the identification is **probable, labelled as inference, not a disclosure**. It changes nothing in the numbers: the arrangement was under US$1.7m combined with Reprograma, was disclosed with its nature, its date and the reason the relationship ended, and has been nil for three straight years.

## 4. Round-Tripping Cross-Year Name Match (A5-04)

**The test was BUILT, not eyeballed.** I assembled ONE list of every named counterparty across ALL five years read (FY2021 Note 24, FY2022 Note 25, FY2023 Note 27, FY2024 Note 28, FY2025 Note 28, H1-2026 interim Note 28), then matched those names against every disclosed customer and supplier name in the pool - the Capital IQ Customers and Suppliers exports and `relationships.json` (11 disclosed relationship rows) - and against the 34-entity corporate tree. The match was run **across years, not within a single year**.

**Universe assembled (every name, all sources, all years):**
- *From the RPT notes:* Rodamoinho Produtora de Eventos Ltda.; Reprograma; "the Company's Board Members" (class); the unnamed director-CEO company (= Lightspark Group, Inc.); the class "executive directors, board members, key employees and close family members."
- *From the disclosed customer side (1 row):* Circle Internet Group, Inc. (NYSE:CRCL) - customer of Nu Pagamentos.
- *From the disclosed supplier side (10 rows):* Amazon Web Services, Inc.; Computershare Trust Company, N.A.; Edenred SE; MasterCard International Incorporated (x3 rows, three group entities); Mercedes-Benz Grand Prix Limited; Numis Corporation Limited; U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC); Wise Group plc.
- *From the corporate tree:* the 34 majority-held group entities (all consolidated).

| Name | Years as customer | Years as vendor | Both roles? | Sales approx. purchases (circular)? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circle Internet Group, Inc. | 2025 (Circle S-1) | never | **No** | n/a | **No match - single role** | CIQ Customers export, scope "recently disclosed customers only (last two years)" |
| Amazon Web Services, Inc. | never | 2026 (20-F) | No | n/a | No match | CIQ Suppliers export |
| MasterCard International Incorporated | never | 2026 (20-F), 3 group entities | No | n/a | No match - licensor only | CIQ Suppliers export |
| Edenred SE | never | disclosed | No | n/a | No match | CIQ Suppliers export |
| Wise Group plc | never | disclosed | No | n/a | No match | CIQ Suppliers export |

NU received cash; NU has disclosed **no** payment, purchase or sale to this counterparty in any year | **No match - one-directional** | `FY24/FY25 20-F, Note 28(a)`; `H1 2026 Interim, Note 28(a)` |

**Result: ZERO both-roles matches across five years and every disclosed counterparty in the pool.** No name appears as both a customer and a vendor; no matched or mirrored amounts exist because no counterparty has two legs at all; there is no funds-flow circle. **No Amber-investigate lead was generated, so nothing needed escalating to Red.** The DHFL / Gensol pattern - money leaving as a purchase and returning as a sale - requires two legs, and this ledger has none.

**Coverage limit, stated honestly.** The customer/supplier universe comes from a **tier-5 Capital IQ vendor export** whose own scope note reads "Recently disclosed customers only (within the last two years)... Include Customers for: Current subsidiaries." It is **not** a complete vendor ledger and I do not present it as one; it is the disclosed-relationship universe. `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` records `intragroup_row_share_pct` = **0.0** across those 11 rows, i.e. **no disclosed trading with the group's own entities**. The cross-year test is therefore run over every name the filings and the disclosed-relationship export contain - which is what is obtainable - and its answer is unambiguous within that scope. Nothing in the corpus suggests a suppressed second leg.

## 5. Approval & Disclosure Hygiene (A5-05, A5-06, A5-07, A5-08)

| ID | Test | Raw finding | Band | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A5-05** | Arm's-length substantiation | The only substantiation offered anywhere is the sentence: transactions with directors, officers, key employees and family "are conducted on **similar terms as those offered to unrelated third parties under similar circumstances** and do not involve more than the normal risk of collectability." **No benchmarking methodology is disclosed. No audit-committee approval is documented for any specific transaction. No pricing evidence is given for the Note 28(a) arrangement at all** - the boilerplate does not even attach to it | **Bare assertion, not methodology** | **Amber** (would be Red on a material RPT; the amounts here are 0.0059% of revenue, which caps the severity, not the finding) | `FY25 20-F, Note 28, p.F-77` |
| **A5-06** | Minority dissent on RPT resolutions | **No RPT resolution has been put to shareholders in any year.** The FPI regime does not require one, and NU's dual-class structure (Class B shares held by Rua California Ltd. carrying the controlling vote) means a minority vote would not bind in any case. **Dissent percentage: not applicable - no vote exists to measure** | n/a - no vote in this regime | **Not Applicable (no vote required or held)** - recorded, not skipped | `FY25 20-F, Item 7.B`; `Item 10.B (Memorandum and Articles)`; `Item 7.A` |
| **A5-07** | Pre-approval, only-independent voting, omnibus discipline, slab-slicing | A policy **exists and was strengthened**: "In March 2024, we updated our related party transaction policy, which requires certain related party transactions to be approved by our board of directors or a designated committee thereof, **including our Audit and Risk Committee**." What is **not** disclosed: the monetary thresholds that trigger approval; the word "certain"; whether approval is **pre-facto or ratifying**; whether only **independent** members vote; whether any omnibus approval exists; and whether any transaction was actually approved in FY2025 | Policy present, **operation undisclosed** | **Amber** | `FY25 20-F, Item 7.B, p.206` |
| **A5-08** | Counterparty transparency | Rodamoinho and Reprograma **were** named. The FY2024/FY2025/H1-2026 counterparty is **not** named - described only by class, "a company where one of its Directors serves as CEO." The director-loan class is named as a class and **not quantified**. IAS 24 requires the nature of the relationship and the amounts, both of which are given, and does **not** require the name | Relationship + amount disclosed; name withheld | **Amber (disclosure-quality, not omission)** | `FY25 20-F, Note 28(a) fn.(i)` |

**Slab-slicing test - performed, with the sums shown.** The test is to SUM same-counterparty transactions per year and compare the TOTAL, not each slice, against the approval threshold.

| Counterparty | FY2021 | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | H1-2026 | Summed total per year vs any threshold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Rodamoinho + Reprograma (combined, as the notes present them) | 1,685 | 1,112 | 0 | - | - | - | Only ONE line exists per year; there are no slices to sum |
| Unnamed director-CEO company (Lightspark) | - | - | - | 1,795 | 926 | 265 | **Single balance, single arrangement, single counterparty.** Nothing is split across multiple line items, multiple entities, or multiple dates |
| Board Members (Series G-1 share purchase) | 1,600 as printed | - | - | - | - | - | One transaction, one date (2021-06-30) |

**Result: no slicing detected.** In every year the note carries **one** outside related-party line. There is no counterparty appearing more than once in a year, no cluster of similar amounts, and nothing sitting just under a threshold - and in any case **no numeric approval threshold is disclosed to sit just under**. The absence of a disclosed threshold is itself the A5-07 Amber: you cannot demonstrate that a transaction cleared a bar the company has not published.

**The candid summary of this section.** NU's related-party *substance* is close to nil and its related-party *process disclosure* is thin. Those are different findings and I keep them apart. Nothing here says value is leaking. What it says is that if value **were** leaking through a small-to-medium related-party arrangement, the reader could not detect it from these filings alone: there is no named counterparty, no pricing methodology, no threshold, no approval record, and no vote. That is the honest shape of the risk - **a low observed exposure combined with a modest detection capability**, which is why the disclosure-hygiene component below carries the largest single share of the risk score.

## 8. Group-Structure Map (A11-01)

| Metric | Value | Band | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Layers, listco -> deepest entity | **3 on the vendor tree; at least 4 once the audited filing's own control labels are honoured** (see below) | <=2 Green; >3 Red | **Amber** | CIQ Corporate Structure Tree, retrieved 2026-08-29 (tier-5); `FY25 20-F, Note 3, p.F-19` |
| Total group entities (subs + associates + JVs) | **34** subsidiaries / operating units; **0 associates**; **0 joint ventures**; **0 equity-method entities** | Proportionate Green; >100 Red | **Green** | CIQ Corporate Structure Tree - Aggregates: 34 subsidiary/operating units, 34 majority holdings, **0 minority holdings, 0 unknown holdings** |
| Offshore entities without evident purpose | **7 named, purpose not stated in any filing** - Nu Cayman Ltd, and Nu 1-A / 1-B / 2-A / 2-B / 3-A / 3-B LLC (all US) | 0 Green | **Amber** | CIQ Corporate Structure Tree |
| Entities that only move money | **0 identified.** Every entity with a disclosed activity has an operating or regulated function | 0 Green | **Green** | `FY25 20-F, Note 3`; CIQ tree |
| Entities named in the AUDITED filing | **6 of 34** - Note 3 lists only "the most relevant entities" | - | **Amber (see below)** | `FY25 20-F, Note 3, p.F-19` |
| Regional split | 23 Latin America & Caribbean; 11 United States & Canada; **0 Europe, 0 Asia-Pacific, 0 Africa/Middle East** | No tax-haven chain | **Green** | CIQ tree Aggregates |

**Depth, worked rather than asserted.** The longest chain the vendor tree shows is **Nu Holdings Ltd. -> Nu Pagamentos S.A. -> Nu Investimentos S.A. -> Verios Gestao de Recursos S.A.** = three layers below the listco. But the audited filing contradicts the vendor on parentage: **Note 3 labels Nu Pagamentos, Nu Financeira, Nu Investimentos, Nu Mexico Financiera and Nu Colombia Financiera all "Indirect"**, and only **Nu United States LLC "Direct"** [`FY25 20-F, Note 3, p.F-19`]. "Indirect" means at least one intermediate holding company sits between the listco and Nu Pagamentos that the vendor tree renders as a direct child - most plausibly **Nu Participacoes Financeiras** or **Nu Cayman Ltd**, both of which appear in the tree as direct subsidiaries with no stated activity. Honouring the audited label (CLAUDE.md §4 - the filing beats the vendor), the true depth to Verios is **at least 4**. I report both readings and grade on the audited one: **Amber, above the >3 Red line on depth but well inside every other band.**

**What each layer is FOR, one line each.**
- **Layer 0 - Nu Holdings Ltd. (Cayman Islands):** the NYSE-listed holding company and the IPO vehicle. A Cayman topco is the standard listing structure for a Latin American technology issuer listing in New York; it is disclosed, it is the registrant, and it holds no operations.
- **Layer 1 - country and function holdcos** (Nu Participacoes Financeiras, Nu Participacoes S.A., Nu Cayman Ltd, Nu BN Tecnologia, Nu United States LLC, Nu MX LLC): intermediate holding companies that group the Brazilian, Mexican, Colombian and US stacks. Purpose is inferable from geography; **not one of them has a stated purpose in any filing.**
- **Layer 2 - the regulated operating banks:** Nu Pagamentos (payment institution, BACEN), Nu Financeira (credit, BACEN), Nu Mexico Financiera (SFP, BANXICO/CNBV), Nu Colombia Financiera (SFC), Akala (Mexico). These are where the business, the customers and the balance sheet actually are.
- **Layer 3 - product and technology subsidiaries:** Nu Investimentos (brokerage), Nu Asset Management, Nu Corretora de Seguros (insurance broking), Nu Crypto, Nu DTVM, NuCommerce, Nu Pay for Business, plus the acquired technology teams (Cognitect, Olivia AI, Juntos Global, Chico AI, Plataformatec, Spin Pay).
- **Layer 4 - Verios Gestao de Recursos S.A.**, held under Nu Investimentos: an acquired asset manager, LTM revenue **US$0.59m**, total debt **US$0.00m**. This is the deepest point in the group, and it is a rounding error.
- **The seven unexplained entities.** **Nu Cayman Ltd** and the six identically-named **Nu 1-A / 1-B / 2-A / 2-B / 3-A / 3-B LLC** (all United States) have **no stated activity, no revenue, no assets and no purpose in any filing in the pool**. Six sequentially numbered paired LLCs in the same jurisdiction is the naming convention of **securitisation or warehouse-financing vehicles** (an A/B pair per series is the classic issuer/depositor split) - but that is my inference from the naming pattern, **not from filings**, and I label it as such. They are majority-held per the vendor tree and therefore consolidated; none appears in Note 3, none carries disclosed debt, and none is named in the borrowings note. **This is the single genuine structural opacity in the group**, and it is what the A11-01 Amber is for.

**Proportionality.** Thirty-four entities for a group operating three regulated banking licences across three countries, plus a brokerage, an asset manager, an insurance broker, a crypto arm and six acquired technology teams, is **proportionate** - roughly one entity per licence, product line or acquisition. It is a fraction of the IL&FS 348 that the Red band exists to catch, and there is **no associate held just below a consolidation threshold**: the tree reports **zero minority holdings and zero unknown holdings**, meaning nothing is parked at 49%.

**One extraction limit, declared.** The 20-F's index references **"Exhibit 8.1 - List of Subsidiaries"** [`FY25 20-F, Item 4.C and exhibit index, item 8.1`], but the exhibit's own content is not present in the extracted pool text. The 34-entity count therefore rests on the **tier-5 CIQ corporate tree** cross-checked against **Note 3's six named entities** and the entities named in Notes 24, 25 and 28. That is a coverage note, not a gap in the company's disclosure: the exhibit exists and was filed.

## 9. Cash & Funding Topology (A11-02, A11-03)

**Matched-basis rule (CLAUDE.md §15) applied to every row.** Both sides' bases are named. Where a matched version cannot be built, the mismatch is labelled inline and no headline number is taken from it.

| Question | Raw value | Basis (both sides) | Matched ratio | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Where does consolidated cash sit (parent vs subs)? | Consolidated cash and cash equivalents **US$15,003,643k** at 31-Dec-2025 (US$9,185,742k at 31-Dec-2024). **The parent-only split is NOT disclosed** - IFRS consolidated statements carry no parent-only column, and a foreign private issuer filing IFRS 20-F files no Schedule I condensed parent financials | n/a - one side is undisclosed | **Cannot be computed** - recorded as undisclosed, never as zero | **Amber - not assessable from the filings** | `FY25 20-F, Consolidated Balance Sheet, Note 11` |
| Share held with a related finance company or treasury vehicle | **Nil. There is no affiliated finance company, no promoter-controlled treasury vehicle and no related NBFC anywhere in the group.** Group cash sits in the group's own **regulated** banks and at central banks | n/a | **0.00%** | **Green** | `FY25 20-F, Note 3, Note 11`; CIQ tree (34 entities, all group-owned) |
| Subsidiary cash pledged as collateral | **US$899,809k** at 31-Dec-2025 (US$201,494k at 31-Dec-2024) "held by the subsidiaries as guarantee pledged to the margin loan" | **Both sides period-end 31-Dec-2025**: pledged balance over total cash and cash equivalents | **6.00% of consolidated cash** (899,809 / 15,003,643). Matched - a period-end over a period-end | **Amber (memo)** - rose 4.5x YoY alongside the margin loan (US$201,493k -> US$1,868,626k). Not a related-party issue; routes to balance-sheet survival | `FY25 20-F, Note 11(i)`; `Note 24(iii)` |
| Parent borrowing while subs hold the cash? | **No.** The margin loan facility was entered **through Nu Financeira**, an operating subsidiary, secured on government securities - not at the Cayman parent. The DFC facility sits at **Nu Colombia**. Debt sits **with the operating entities that use it** | Structural, not a ratio | n/a | **Green** | `FY25 20-F, Item 5.B; Note 24` |
| ICDs to group entities - amount, rate, tenor | **Intercompany loans exist between entities with different functional currencies** and are **eliminated on consolidation**; only the FX translation difference reaches the income statement. **Amounts, rates and tenors are not disclosed** because consolidation removes them. **No ICD to any entity outside the consolidation exists** | n/a | n/a | **Green** on external leakage; **not assessable** on internal terms | `FY21 20-F, Note 24`; `FY22 20-F, Note 25`; `FY23 20-F, Note 27`; `FY25 20-F, Note 28` |
| Evergreen / rolled-over ICDs? | **None identifiable.** No related-party loan balance appears in any of the five RPT notes. The only outside related-party balance is the Lightspark **liability**, which is **falling** (1,795 -> 926 -> 265), i.e. being extinguished, not rolled | Sequential period-end balances, like for like | **-85% over 18 months** (265 / 1,795) | **Green** | `FY24/FY25 20-F, Note 28(a)`; `H1 2026 Interim, Note 28(a)` |

**Related FINANCIAL counterparty: none exists, so the required facts are recorded as nil rather than omitted.** The checklist asks that where cash sits with a related financial entity, five things be recorded - the company's own equity interest in it, its regulatory supervision, the approved cap, its utilisation, and the independent-director / auditor review status. **NU has no related financial counterparty.** The nearest structural analogue is that group cash sits inside **NU's own wholly-owned regulated subsidiaries**, and for those the equivalent facts are: **equity interest 100%**; **regulatory supervision** BACEN (Brazil), BANXICO and CNBV (Mexico), SFC (Colombia) [`FY25 20-F, Note 3, p.F-19`]; **no approved cap or utilisation applies** because these are consolidated subsidiaries, not counterparties; **auditor review** - all consolidated and audited within the group audit by the group auditor. That is the complete set, given the structure.

**The real cash-topology fact, and it is a genuine one.** Note 3 states, verbatim: the regulated Brazilian, Mexican and Colombian subsidiaries are subject to "some regulatory requirements that **restrict the ability of the Group to access and transfer assets freely to or from these entities** within the Group and to settle liabilities of the other entities of the Group" [`FY25 20-F, Note 3, p.F-19`]. The 20-F reinforces it as a named risk factor: "**Our holding company structure makes us dependent on the operations of our subsidiaries**" [`FY25 20-F, Item 3.D`], and Item 8.A adds that Brazilian *sociedades anonimas* must distribute a mandatory minimum dividend (25% of prior-year net income after the 5% legal reserve, absent a bylaw figure) while Colombian and Mexican subsidiaries "may also face restrictions."

**Read that correctly - it is a liquidity-location fact, not a leakage fact.** Cash trapped behind a **prudential regulator** is trapped by the Central Bank of Brazil, not by a controller. It restricts the parent's ability to fund buybacks or dividends; it does **not** create a channel through which minority value reaches the promoter. **A11-02 Amber** for the undisclosed parent/subsidiary cash split - which I record as undisclosed, never as safe - and **not** for the classic Red pattern of cash concentrated in *opaque* subsidiaries while the parent borrows. Here the cash sits in **named, regulated, audited** banks, and the parent does not borrow.

**A11-03 Green.** No inter-corporate deposit to any entity outside the consolidation exists in any of the five years read.

(director-CEO, not controller) | **Adjacent, not overlapping** - blockchain payments infrastructure (Lightning Network, UMA), which NU *integrates* rather than competes with | **None - the flow runs the other way.** Lightspark paid NU an integration incentive. **The finding here is an absence, and it is the most important absence in this report.** The listed-vs-private sibling pattern - the listco carrying the costs while the family's private companies keep the upside - **requires a private company in an overlapping business**. NU's controller does not have one. David Velez holds his entire economic interest in a **single-purpose share-holding vehicle**, which means his upside is the share price and nothing else. There is no promoter-owned lender, no promoter-owned fintech, no promoter-owned processor, no promoter-owned real-estate arm renting to the bank. **The channel does not exist**, which is a structurally stronger answer than "the channel exists and is currently small."

### 10A. Predecessor / lineage entity (A11-04, A11-05) - step 14A

`07`'s Section 3B lineage read identifies **Nu Pagamentos S.A. - Instituicao de Pagamento** as NU's originating operating entity (the business began there in 2013 before the 2021 Cayman holdco reorganisation and NYSE listing). The three questions, answered with numbers:

1. **Is it still LIVE?** **Yes** - and it is **inside the consolidated group**, 100% held, named in Note 3 as the group's principal payment institution, regulated by BACEN. LTM total revenue **US$2,896.12m**, total debt **US$11,659.45m** [CIQ tree, LFQ 2026-06-30].
2. **Is it still trading on the same brands / in the same market?** **Yes - and that is the correct place for it to be.** Nu Pagamentos is the registered proprietor of **NUBANK (USPTO serial 86386363)** and **NU BANK (serial 86963402)**. The predecessor **is** the brand owner, and it sits inside the consolidation.
3. **Does the listco transact with it, or with anyone who controls it?** All transactions with it are **intra-group and eliminated on consolidation**. It is controlled by Nu Holdings Ltd. and by no one else.

**Conclusion: there is no phoenix, no shell, and no external predecessor.** The usual danger pattern - a predecessor still operating *alongside* the listco, on shared brands, owned by the controller - is **absent**, because the predecessor was folded **into** the group rather than left outside it. Nothing flows between the listco and an outside lineage entity, and I show what was checked: Note 3's consolidation list, the corporate tree, the USPTO proprietor field, and all five RPT notes. **A17-04 stays Green and its licence economics under A5-02 are nil, because no licence to an outside party exists.**

## 11. Subsidiary Transparency & Governance (A11-05, A11-06)

**Regime note first.** **SEBI LODR Reg 24(1), 24(5) and 24(6) do not apply to NU** - it is a Cayman-incorporated SEC foreign private issuer, not an Indian listed company. There is no Indian-style "material subsidiary" regime, no requirement to place a listco independent director on a subsidiary board, and no secretarial audit. The equivalent tests in this regime are: whether material subsidiaries' financials are visible and audited; whether the structure is stable; and whether the local prudential regulators supervise the entities where the assets sit.

| ID | Test | Raw finding | Band | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A11-05** | Material subs' financials visible & audited; structure stable | **Visible in aggregate, not individually.** All 34 entities are fully consolidated into audited IFRS statements covered by one group audit opinion. Note 3 names **6** entities with control basis, principal activity, functional currency, country and **percentage interest for 2025 / 2024 / 2023**. **Stand-alone subsidiary financial statements are not published in the 20-F.** Structure is **stable**: the same six entities appear at **100%** in all three disclosed years, with **no change** | Individual sub P&Ls not published, which is normal in an IFRS 20-F; ownership stable at 100% | **Green on stability; Amber on individual visibility** | `FY25 20-F, Note 3, p.F-19` |
| **A11-05** | Restructuring churn / associates held below consolidation thresholds | **No churn.** No disposal, demerger, hive-off or reorganisation disclosed in FY2023-FY2025. **Zero associates and zero joint ventures** - the corporate tree records **34 majority holdings, 0 minority holdings, 0 unknown holdings**, so nothing is parked at 49% to stay off the consolidation. One new entity **gained** in Nov-2024: an investment fund (FIDC), which was **consolidated** on obtaining control | 0 associates below threshold = Green | **Green** | CIQ Corporate Structure Tree - Aggregates, 2026-08-29; `FY25 20-F, Note 3` (consolidated investment funds); `FY25 20-F, fair-value note (FIDC control obtained Nov-2024)` |
| **A11-06** | Independent-director oversight of subsidiary boards | **Reg 24(1) not applicable.** No subsidiary board composition is disclosed. The functional substitute is prudential supervision: **Nu Pagamentos, Nu Financeira and Nu Investimentos are regulated by BACEN; Nu Mexico Financiera by BANXICO and CNBV; Nu Colombia by the SFC** - each with its own fit-and-proper, governance and reporting obligations | Regime-appropriate; specific board composition undisclosed | **Green (regime N/A) with an Amber note on subsidiary board transparency** | `FY25 20-F, Note 3, p.F-19` |
| **A11-06** | Special resolution before sub dilution <50% or >20% asset sale | **Reg 24(5)-(6) not applicable** in the Cayman/SEC regime. No dilution below 50% and no disposal of >20% of any material subsidiary's assets occurred in FY2023-FY2025 - percentage interests are unchanged at 100% across all three disclosed years, so **the test has nothing to bite on** | n/a | **Not Applicable (regime) - and no triggering event occurred** | `FY25 20-F, Note 3, p.F-19` |

**The honest summary.** Subsidiary governance is **supervised by three central banks and one securities regulator rather than by published subsidiary board lists**. That is a genuinely different, and in some respects stronger, control than an independent director on a subsidiary board - a prudential regulator inspects capital, liquidity and related-party lending directly. What a reader **cannot** do from these filings is see any individual subsidiary's profit, its intra-group pricing, or who sits on its board. Recorded Amber on visibility; not scored as leakage, because no mechanism to move value outside the consolidation has been found.

**The one caveat I will not smooth over.** The **six numbered US LLCs (Nu 1-A through 3-B)** carry no disclosed purpose, no disclosed assets and no disclosed debt, and appear in **no note of the 20-F**. The vendor tree records them as majority-held, which means they are consolidated - and if they are consolidated, A11-07 is satisfied by definition. But their absence from every audited note means I am relying on a **tier-5 vendor export** for the fact that six US entities with a securitisation-style naming convention are inside the consolidation. That is a thinner basis than I would like for the single structure in this group that could, in principle, hold off-balance-sheet debt. It is named in Section 14 as a follow-up, and it is why the group-structure component of the score is not zero.

## 14. Read

**Roughly US$0.9m of value sits between Nu Holdings and any outside related party, and it is owed TO the company, not by it.** The entire five-year related-party record outside remuneration amounts to a US$1.7m combined services bill in 2021-22 (a director's events company and the founder's family's coding-education project, both named, both ended), a pre-IPO share purchase by board members, and a Q2-2024 partnership under which a start-up whose CEO sits on NU's board **paid** the company an integration incentive that has since run down from US$1,795k to US$265k. Including all key-management compensation, related-party intensity is **0.58% of FY2025 revenue and 3.21% of profit** [`FY25 20-F, Note 28`; denominators from `earnings/01`]; excluding it, **0.0059% of revenue**. The single largest channel is the unnamed Lightspark arrangement, and its direction of value favours the minority shareholder.

**The group structure would not hide much, but it is not fully lit.** Thirty-four entities, **zero associates and zero joint ventures**, no entity parked at 49% below a consolidation line, no unconsolidated SPE, and the one securitisation-shaped fund (a FIDC) consolidated the moment control was obtained. Against that: depth runs to **at least four layers** once Note 3's own "Indirect" control labels are honoured against the vendor tree; the audited filing names only **6 of 34** entities; and **seven entities have no stated purpose in any filing** - Nu Cayman Ltd and six sequentially paired US LLCs (Nu 1-A through 3-B) whose naming convention is that of financing vehicles, a reading I label as my inference and not a disclosure. Consolidated cash of **US$15.0bn** sits inside the group's own **regulated** banks - BACEN, BANXICO/CNBV, SFC - with **6.00% pledged as margin-loan collateral** (US$899.8m over US$15,003.6m, both 31-Dec-2025, a matched period-end ratio). It is trapped by prudential regulators, not by a controller, and the parent/subsidiary split of that cash is not disclosed at all.

**What actually caps this read is detection capability, not exposure.** NU offers a **bare "similar terms" assertion** with no benchmarking methodology, **never quantifies** the credit cards and loans it issues to its own directors and executives despite Item 7.B asking for exactly that, publishes **no approval threshold** and **no record of any specific approval**, and **declines to name** its only current related counterparty when it named the previous two. None of that is a violation in this regime, and none of it is evidence of leakage. It does mean that a mid-sized related-party arrangement could exist without a reader being able to price it - and the honest conclusion is a **low measured leakage risk with a moderate blind spot**, not a clean bill.

**The one disclosure that would settle the biggest open question:** **the quantified balance of credit cards and loans outstanding to NU's directors, executive officers, key employees and their close family members at 31 December 2025** - the figure Form 20-F Item 7.B already asks for and NU has never given. It is the only unquantified related-party number in the whole file, it sits at a **lender** where such lending is the natural leakage channel, and one line in the next 20-F closes it. (Second, and separable: the identity of the **Banco Porto Real** selling shareholders, and the content of **Exhibit 8.1**, which would resolve the six unexplained US LLCs.)

# Contingent Liabilities & Commitments — NU

**Company:** Nu Holdings Ltd. (NYSE: NU) — Cayman Islands holding company, operating banks and financing companies in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.
**Reporting regime:** SEC foreign private issuer → **Form 20-F** is the audited annual filing (the local equivalent of a 10-K); IFRS Accounting Standards; presentation currency **US dollars**; fiscal year ends **31 December**. There is no Indian-style "Contingent Liabilities and Commitments" schedule and no CARO annexure — the equivalent disclosures are **Note 25 "Provisions and contingent liabilities"**, **Item 8.A "Legal Proceedings"**, the borrowings note's **Guarantees** paragraph, and the market-risk section. All note figures below are **US$ thousands as printed**, restated to US$ millions where I compare them to equity.

**Cross-module inputs.** `balance-sheet-survival/05_off-balance-sheet-and-contingencies.md` does not exist in this run root (`analyses/NU_2026-09-06/balance-sheet-survival/` contains only `00_solvency-data-triage.md`) — **balance-sheet-survival cross-module input not available; proceeding on this module's own read of the data pool.** No figure below is taken from, or recomputed against, that module. Denominators come from the 20-F balance sheet and `earnings/01_historical-financials.md`.

**Sector overlay.** This is a bank/financial group (MODULE_RULES sector overlay: banks/NBFCs). Undrawn credit-card limits are the business itself, not a governance contingency — they are shown once, labelled, and left to the survival module.

| Memo — **credit commitments (unused credit-card limits)** | 28,841.327 | Net worth = US$11,321.562m | 254.7% | Not graded here — this is the lending business, revocable, and inside the ECL model | Memo only | FY2025 20-F, Credit Risk — Other exposures |
| Memo — **unquantified claim bound**: Colombia GMF class action, gross claim across 52 defendants | ~2,500 | Net worth = US$11,321.562m | ~22.1% **(a bound, not an exposure)** | See §4 | See §4 | FY2025 20-F, Item 8.A Legal Proceedings |

**RF-FIN-003 (CL above 5% of net worth) does NOT fire.** Every *measured* contingent liability sums to US$39.824m = 0.352% of net worth. The ~22.1% figure is the **gross claim against 52 defendants jointly**, which the company says it cannot apportion; firing a threshold designed for a company's own exposure off an unapportioned gross claim would mix two different bases (§15). It is reported as a bound, and RF-CL-001 is fired separately on the disclosure defect in §4.

**(b) Contingencies — possible losses, disclosed only, not provided**

| Item | Dec-2022 | Dec-2023 | Dec-2024 | Dec-2025 | Jun-2026 | Movement explained? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Civil (possible) | 7,128 | 14,212 | 2,613 | 4,372 | 4,784 | **No** — no movement table exists for possible losses in any year | Amber | FY2023/FY2024/FY2025 20-F Note 24/26/25(c); H1-26 Interim Note 25(c) |
| Labor (possible) | 1,814 | 12,333 | 17,738 | 4,532 | 4,891 | **No** — fell 74% in FY2025 with no explanation | **Amber (movement honesty)** | same |
| Tax (possible) | — | — | — | — | — | **No line exists** in any year | **Not separately disclosed** (not "Nil") | same |
| **Total possible** | **8,942** | **26,545** | **20,351** | **8,904** | **9,675** | — | Amber | same |

**The flat-total trap, in the mirror.** The headline "contingent liability" number (possible losses) **fell 56% in FY2025**, from US$20.351m to US$8.904m. Read alone, that is an improving trend. It is not. Two things moved the other way inside it: (i) the underlying consumer-litigation book migrated from *possible* into *probable* and was provided — the civil provision rose from US$2.096m (Dec-2022) to US$30.739m (Jun-2026), 14.7×, against customer growth of 75.6%, and the PROCON/small-claims caseload rose from 8,714 to 32,703 active proceedings (litigation intensity per million customers roughly doubled, from ~117 to ~250); (ii) the single largest claim the company faces — the Colombia GMF class action (§4) — is classified *possible* and appears **nowhere** in that US$8.904m. **Never grade this company's contingency trend from the possible-loss total.**

**Vanished / unexplained items.** Labor possible losses dropped from US$17.738m to US$4.532m (−74%) and civil possible losses from US$14.212m to US$2.613m in the prior year (−82%), each with no reversal, payment or narrative — because IAS 37 does not require a movement table for possible losses and Nu does not volunteer one. Recorded as a movement-honesty Amber, not accepted silently.

**Crystallization test (A7a-13) — RF-CL-003 does NOT fire.** Payments out of provisions ran US$22.226m (2023), US$15.719m (2024), US$23.738m (2025), US$14.147m (H1-2026). That is recurring cash crystallization, and FY2025 payments (US$23.738m) **exceeded the opening provision balance (US$22.551m)** — the stock of provision is under one year of outflow. But the pattern is a fast-turning consumer-claims book where each year's claims are booked as *probable* and provided **before** they are paid, not items that sat in "possible" and then landed. The one genuine crystallization of a disputed item — the PIS/COFINS tax matter, US$15.747m — was fully provided from 2021 and settled against a judicial deposit in May 2023. Provisions were not understated. Verdict: **Amber on coverage depth, Green on candor.**

**Read.** Both tax items are Green on size — a combined probable tax provision of 0.045% of net worth, against a Green band of <5%, and both named historical disputes were provided before they crystallized. Two disclosure gaps sit under that: the note never splits direct from indirect tax, and it never states whether any tax claim is classified *possible* — the possible-loss paragraph names only civil and labor. Absence of a line is not evidence of absence.

## 4. Litigation & Claims Not Acknowledged as Debt (A7a-05)

| Claim | Counterparty | Amount | Interim rulings so far | Provided? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| **Colombia GMF ("4x1000") class action** — alleged failure to automate the Financial Movements Tax exemption required by Art. 65, Law 2277 of 2022 by the 14-Dec-2024 deadline; seeks restitution of all GMF withheld since 13-Dec-2024 plus interest | Class of Colombian account holders vs **52 financial institutions**, including Nu Colombia Compañía de Financiamiento | **COP 9.3 trillion ≈ US$2.5bn** total claim (company's own translation, as of 16-Jan-2026) — the 20-F states Nu's proportionate share "is not possible to quantify" | 20-F (filed 08-Apr-2026): "Nu Colombia has filed a motion for dismissal, and the case is currently in its initial stages awaiting a court resolution." **Public court reporting says the action was ADMITTED by a Bogotá judge (Sergio Iván Mesa Macías), file 110013103007-2025-00368-00, notified 25-Aug-2025** — i.e. before the 20-F was filed | **No** — classified *possible*, unprovided, and **absent from the Note 25(c) possible-loss total of US$8.904m** | **Red** — RF-CL-001 | FY2025 20-F, Item 8.A Legal Proceedings; Forbes Colombia / abceconomia.co, May-2026 (web, dated, **unverified against the primary docket**) |
| 123 Milhas chargeback class action (IDC, Sept-2023) | Instituto de Defesa Coletiva vs Nubank and other banks | ~**R$7.5m** amounts involved; Nu chose to fully reimburse customers | Defence filed; administrative claim-review phase closed 31-Jan-2026; mediation opened. Company: "No material risk has been identified" | No provision stated; impact limited to non-recovery of amounts already absorbed | Green (immaterial: R$7.5m ≈ US$1.3m at ~R$5.6/US$, <0.02% of net worth) | FY2025 20-F, Item 8.A |
| Consumer proceedings — PROCONs and small-claims courts | ~**32,703 active proceedings** at 31-Dec-2025 (27,830 at Dec-2024; 24,226 at Dec-2023; 8,714 at Dec-2022) | Not individually quantified; drives the civil provision | Ongoing, continuous | Yes — via the civil provision (US$22.044m at Dec-2025; US$30.739m at Jun-2026) | Amber — provided, but the caseload is compounding faster than the customer base | FY2025 20-F, Item 3.D; Note 25 |

**Why this is the module's central finding.** The GMF claim is the largest single legal item Nu faces by an order of magnitude, it is classified *possible*, it is unprovided, and it is disclosed **only in Item 8.A** — it does not appear in Note 25(c), which is where a reader looking for the company's possible-loss universe would look, and which totals US$8.904m. The 20-F's own explanation for not sizing it is reasonable and is stated (52 defendants, apportionment requires transaction-level data Nu does not hold), so this is not concealment. It is a **placement and completeness defect**: IAS 37.86 asks for the estimate of the financial effect, or a statement that it cannot be made, in the contingency disclosure — and the statement that it cannot be made lives in a different item of the filing. Compounding it, the FY2025 20-F's litigation narrative ends with *"For further information, see note 23 to our audited consolidated financial statements"* — the contingency note is **note 25**, not note 23. A reader following the filing's own signpost lands in the wrong place.

**Posture (web, coverage-limited).** The public reporting that the class action was admitted on 25-Aug-2025 is a *dated, unverified* web source; admission ("admisión de la demanda") is a procedural gate, not a merits ruling, and a dismissal motion or appeal can still be live. But the 20-F, filed nearly eight months later, tells the reader the case is "in its initial stages awaiting a court resolution" without saying the action cleared admission. This is the IndiaMART pattern in a different dress: **the number stayed at zero while the procedural posture moved.** I have not read the primary docket — see the Sweep Log.

## 9. Provided vs Only-Disclosed (A7a-14)

| Dispute / claim | Classified as | Appeal record says | Provision held | Candor verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Civil / consumer claims (credit card, NuAccount, fees and charges, moral and material damages) | **Probable** | ~32,703 active PROCON/small-claims proceedings; recurring adverse outcomes are the norm in this forum | **US$22.044m (Dec-2025), US$30.739m (Jun-2026)** — provided, and provisions rose ahead of the caseload | **Green** — management provides rather than parks; the provision grew 14.7× since Dec-2022 rather than being held flat | FY2025 20-F, Note 25(a); H1-26 Interim, Note 25(a) |
| Labor claims | Probable / possible split disclosed | — | US$3.795m provided; US$4.532m possible | Green | FY2025 20-F, Note 25 |
| PIS/COFINS (closed) | Was **probable** from 2021 | Nu withdrew the suit in 2019; deposit released to the tax authority May-2023 | Was fully provided (US$15.747m) before crystallizing | **Green** — the model case for provisioning ahead of a loss | FY2023 20-F, Note 24(a) |
| **Colombia GMF class action** | **Possible** | Filed Dec-2024; motion to dismiss filed; **public reporting says the action was admitted 25-Aug-2025**, which the 20-F does not state | **Nil**, and excluded from the possible-loss total | **Red on placement, not on the label** — "possible" is defensible for an early-stage, unapportioned claim with no merits ruling; what is not defensible is that the note's possible-loss universe (US$8.904m) omits it entirely and the filing's cross-reference points to the wrong note | FY2025 20-F, Item 8.A; web (dated, unverified) |

**RF-CL-002 does NOT fire.** That flag is for large probable losses carried as "possible" through **serial appeal losses**. There is no record of Nu losing the GMF matter at any level; there is no adverse merits ruling anywhere in the pool; and the one dispute that did go against the company (PIS/COFINS) was provided in full years before it settled. Judged against the actual record rather than management's assertion, the probable/possible labels hold. The H1-2026 interim actually **improved** the disclosure: it now spells out the probable/possible/remote policy in the note and describes what the possible civil claims consist of — a candor improvement worth recording.

**Internal-consistency failure — judicial deposits.** The same fact is reported three different ways:

| Source (all describing the same balance, same purpose — the Nu Investimentos withholding-tax deposit) | 31-Dec-2024 | 31-Dec-2025 |
|---|---:|---:|
| FY2024 20-F (filed 16-Apr-2025), Note 26(d) | **US$5,711k** | — |
| FY2025 20-F (filed 08-Apr-2026), **Note 25(d)** | **US$31,143k** (restated comparative) | **US$92,738k** |
| FY2025 20-F, **Item 8.A** (same document) | **US$5.7m** | **US$6.6m** |
| H1-2026 Interim Report (14-Aug-2026), Note 25(d) | — | **US$6,614k** (comparative) |

The audited FY2025 note reports a judicial-deposit balance roughly **14× its own filing's Item 8 figure for the same date**, and restates the prior-year comparative **5.5×** without a word of explanation; the interim filed four months later reverts to the Item 8 basis. One of these is wrong and none of them says which. This is a Red on disclosure honesty in the contingency note — **RF-DISC-001** (management commentary contradicts the numbers) — and it is exactly the kind of defect that erodes trust in the rest of a note that is otherwise small and well-behaved.

## 11. Read

**The measured off-P&L exposure is trivially small and honestly provided: US$39.824m of provisions plus disclosed possible losses against net worth of US$11,321.562m — 0.352%, against a Green band of under 5% — and the one tax dispute that ever crystallized (PIS/COFINS, US$15.747m) was fully provided from 2021 and paid from a judicial deposit in May 2023.** But do not read the trend off that total: the possible-loss line fell 56% in FY2025 (US$20.351m → US$8.904m) while the thing underneath it got worse — the civil provision is up 14.7× since Dec-2022 (US$2.096m → US$30.739m at Jun-2026) against customer growth of 75.6%, and active PROCON and small-claims proceedings went from 8,714 to 32,703, so consumer-litigation intensity per customer has roughly doubled; the number shrank because claims migrated from *possible* into *provided*, which is the honest direction but not the reassuring story the total tells.

**The single worst item is the Colombian GMF class action: a COP 9.3 trillion (~US$2.5bn) restitution claim against 52 financial institutions including Nu Colombia, classified "possible", unprovided, and disclosed only in Item 8.A — it does not appear in Note 25(c)'s US$8.904m possible-loss total, and the filing's own signpost sends the reader to "note 23" when the contingency note is note 25.** Nu's stated reason for not sizing its share (apportionment needs transaction-level data across 52 defendants) is reasonable and is on the record, so this is a placement-and-completeness failure rather than concealment — but public court reporting says a Bogotá judge **admitted** the action on 25-Aug-2025, nearly eight months before the 20-F that still calls it "in its initial stages awaiting a court resolution." That posture change is not in the filing, and I could not read the docket to confirm it (see the Sweep Log).

**On provisioning candor, management provides rather than parks:** probable losses are booked ahead of payment, the probable/possible/remote policy is now spelled out in the H1-2026 note, and there is no dispute anywhere in the record that lost at multiple levels while being carried unprovided — so RF-CL-002 does not fire. Against that, one thing in the audited note simply does not add up: judicial deposits are reported as **US$92,738k at 31-Dec-2025 in Note 25(d)**, as **US$6.6m for the same date in Item 8.A of the same 20-F**, and as **US$6,614k in the H1-2026 interim's comparative** — with the FY2024 comparative silently restated from US$5,711k to US$31,143k. A 14× internal contradiction inside an audited contingency note, unexplained and uncorrected, is a candor problem out of all proportion to the dollars involved.

**What a rational minority holder should watch next, in order:** (1) whether the FY2026 20-F moves the GMF matter into Note 25 with a quantified or explicitly-unquantifiable statement, and whether it discloses the admission and any ruling on Nu Colombia's dismissal motion; (2) the civil provision run-rate — it added US$21.762m and paid out US$14.147m in H1-2026 alone, so the full-year provision is tracking toward roughly double FY2025, and payments have already exceeded the opening balance once; (3) whether the judicial-deposit figure is corrected or explained, since which of the three published numbers is right determines whether a US$86m asset exists; and (4) the derivative notional, which more than doubled to US$5.25bn in a year against a still-small net mark of +US$14.779m — plain instruments today, worth re-reading each year.

# Accounting Forensics — NU

**Scope and boundary.** This report answers one question: do Nu Holdings Ltd.'s financial statements show the measurable patterns that precede accounting blow-ups? It does not re-derive the earnings-quality baseline (`earnings/06_earnings-quality` owns CFO/profit conversion, accruals and non-GAAP aggressiveness — its figures are consumed here, not recomputed), does not judge the auditor (`08`), does not size related-party transactions (`09`) or contingent liabilities (`10`), does not run the company-level enforcement sweep (`12` — this report owns only A8-20, the regulator-inspection-versus-reported-numbers divergence check), and produces no valuation or rating.

**Reporting regime (CLAUDE.md §27).** Nu Holdings Ltd. is a Cayman-incorporated, NYSE-listed foreign private issuer operating in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. It reports under **IFRS Accounting Standards** in **US dollars**, fiscal year ending **31 December**. The audited annual filing is a **Form 20-F**; the quarterly disclosure is an unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statement furnished on Form 6-K. There is no 10-K, no 10-Q, and no DEF 14A, and their absence is not a data gap. All figures below are **US$ millions, reported (IFRS)** unless a cell says otherwise; source figures are stated in the filings in US$ thousands and are converted here by dividing by 1,000, with no other adjustment.

**Cross-module inputs.** `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` and `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` are present in this run root and are consumed. **`balance-sheet-survival/01_capital-structure-and-leverage.md` cross-module input not available — proceeding on this module's own read of the data pool** (only `balance-sheet-survival/00_solvency-data-triage.md` exists in `analyses/NU_2026-09-06/balance-sheet-survival/`; `NOSTRA_CONTINUATION_RUN_ROOT` is set to this run root, so no prior run was searched). The A14-01 and A14-02 debt-stack figures below are therefore built directly from the borrowings note and the statement of financial position, and are labelled as such.

## 2. Beneish M-Score (A8-14) — NOT COMPUTED (sector exclusion)

**The Beneish M-score is Not Applicable (sector — financials overlay applies) and no composite is reported.** The M-score is a manipulation-probability model built on eight ratios drawn from an industrial company's income statement and classified balance sheet. Four of the eight — GMI (gross-margin deterioration), AQI (asset-quality softening, which needs a current-asset subtotal), SGAI (overhead versus sales) and DSRI (receivables outrunning sales) — have **no valid denominator or no valid meaning** in a bank's IFRS accounts, for the reasons set out in the sector gate. Computing the remaining four and presenting a partial composite would be a faked number, which this report will not produce.

*A note on what this does and does not mean.* An M-score that was not run is a **stated gap in one test**, not a clean bill and not a finding of manipulation. It is also not the same gap it would be for an industrial: the model's whole diagnostic content for this issuer would sit in TATA (accruals versus assets), and TATA's economic content — reported profit that operating cash did not confirm — is measured directly and more honestly in Section 6 from the company's own cash-flow statement, and by `earnings/06`.

**No pre-computed web M-score has been substituted.** No web M-score was used, quoted, or sought as a stand-in; per the self-check, a web score may only ever be labelled corroboration of a computation performed here, and no computation was performed here.

## 3. Dechow F-Score & Accrual Battery (A8-17, A8-18) — NOT COMPUTED (sector exclusion)

**The Dechow F-score is Not Applicable (sector — financials overlay applies) and no composite is reported.** Of its seven inputs, `ΔINV` is structurally zero (no inventory), `ΔREC` measures deliberate loan origination rather than uncollected sales, `RSST` requires a working-capital accrual that an unclassified bank balance sheet does not define, and `SOFT` (soft assets = the share of the balance sheet resting on estimates rather than on cash or hard assets) would read **~81% for this issuer purely because a bank's assets ARE financial claims** — total assets 74,893.9 less net PP&E 27.6 less cash 15,003.6 = 59,862.7, i.e. 79.9% at Dec-31-2025 and 83.6% at Jun-30-2026 — which would trip the model's ">65% and rising" red band on every solvent bank on earth. That is a definitional artefact, not a finding, and it is exactly why the overlay exists.

| Test | Value | Green band | Red band | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Dechow F-score (1.00 = average company) | **Not computed** | <1.00 | ≥1.85 (substantial; ≥2.45 high) | **Not Applicable (sector)** | Overlay; model inputs invalid for a lender |
| RSST accruals / average assets | **Not computed** | ≤3% | ≥10% | **Not Applicable (sector)** | No working-capital accrual is defined on an unclassified balance sheet |
| Soft assets % of total assets | 79.9% (Dec-25); 83.6% (Jun-26) — **shown for transparency, NOT graded** | <50% | >65% and rising | **Not Applicable (sector)** — a structural artefact of banking, not an estimate-heavy balance sheet | FY2025 Form 20-F, F-9; Q2'26 interim, F-3 |
| Δ receivables / average assets | Not graded — the "receivable" is the loan book | <2% | ≥5% with no acquisition explaining it | **Not Applicable (sector)** | Notes 13, 14 |
| Δ inventory / average assets | Structurally 0 (no inventory) | <2% | ≥5% | **Not Applicable (sector)** | F-9 |
| A8-18 — issuance in a flagged year | **No flagged year exists** (no F-score, no TATA). Substantive facts recorded anyway: **no equity was issued in FY2025 or H1'26**; debt raised US$2,823.5m in FY2025 at the regulated Brazilian subsidiaries; and in H1'26 the company **returned** US$500.4m through its first-ever buyback | none while flagged; self-funded | issued while F ≥1.85 or TATA ≥0.031 (RF-ACC-004) | **Not Applicable (sector)** — and the underlying pattern the item exists to catch (books dressed for a raise) is absent on the facts | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 24(a); Q2'26 interim, Statements of Cash Flows and Note 31 |

**RF-ACC-004 does not fire**, and could not, since no flagged year exists to fire it in.

## 4. Cash Authenticity (A8-19)

**The yield test is invalid for this issuer and is not run.** Per the A8-19 band itself: *"NOT valid for banks/NBFCs/insurers (interest income IS the business — sector overlay applies; test cash existence via regulator returns/confirmations instead)."* Nu Holdings' interest income of US$13,434.7m in FY2025 is overwhelmingly earned on the loan and securities books; dividing it by average cash would produce an ~110% "yield" that means nothing, and the other-income note does not itemise a deposit-only interest line that could be scope-matched out of it. So the item rests on the two prongs that do work for a bank — **where the cash sits and who independently confirmed it** — plus the disclosed remuneration rates.

| Test | Value | Band | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Interest income ÷ average cash & deposits (implied yield) | **Not computable — sector-invalid and mixed interest line.** Interest income is the business's revenue, not a return on idle cash, and Note 6 does not itemise deposit-only interest | — | **Not Applicable (sector)** | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 6 |
| Period risk-free rate (instrument, source, date) | Brazil Selic policy rate **15.00% p.a.**, held by COPOM at its Jan-2026 meeting after the 2025 tightening cycle; the FY2025 cash is remunerated against the closely-tracking CDI interbank rate | — | Context only — the yield test above is not run | Web: Agência Brasil, "Brazil's Central Bank keeps benchmark interest rate at 15% per annum", Jan-2026 (dated, unverified) — see Sweep Log |
| Gap | **Not computable** (see above) | Green within ~150bp; Red implied <50% of risk-free on a material pile | **Not Applicable (sector)** | — |
| **Where the cash actually sits** (the prong that replaces the yield test) | Of US$15,003.6m at Dec-31-2025: **US$8,640.2m (57.6%) is on deposit AT the central banks** of Brazil, Mexico and Colombia; US$3,611.5m is overnight reverse repurchase agreements collateralised by government bonds; US$2,099.0m is bank balances; US$652.9m is short-term investments. **None is "held in trust" by a third party.** Compulsory and other deposits at central banks of a further US$9,537.8m sit separately on the balance sheet | Red: "held in trust" / third-party custody | **Green** | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 11; Consolidated Statements of Financial Position, F-9; Note 15 |
| Remuneration disclosed and at market | Brazilian central-bank deposits remunerated at **100.0% of the CDI rate**, daily maturity, at both Dec-31-2025 and Dec-31-2024; Mexican reverse repos at **8.3% p.a.** (10.3% in 2024); USD short-term investments at **3.6% p.a.** Colombian and Mexican central-bank deposits are unremunerated, which is the reserve-requirement regime, disclosed as such | Red: a material pile earning nothing with no explanation (the Satyam pattern) | **Green** | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 11 |
| Auditor obtained independent confirmations / opinion on cash | KPMG Auditores Independentes Ltda. (PCAOB ID 1124), auditor since 2018, issued an **unqualified opinion on the FY2023–FY2025 consolidated financial statements AND a separate unqualified opinion that internal control over financial reporting was effective at Dec-31-2025** (COSO 2013). The audit was conducted under PCAOB standards. **The single Critical Audit Matter is the measurement of expected credit losses — not the existence of cash.** Cash was not identified as an area of especially challenging or complex judgment | Red: confirmations not independently obtained; a cash-related CAM or scope limitation | **Green** | FY2025 Form 20-F, Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, F-3 to F-5 |
| Regulator-return corroboration (the bank-specific existence test) | The Brazilian prudential conglomerate's regulatory capital, risk-weighted assets and capital ratios are computed on BACEN's own definitions and filed with BACEN; the same balances underpin the Mexican SOFIPO and Colombian capital ratios disclosed in Note 33. Regulated subsidiaries are subject to BACEN/CNBV/SFC restrictions on transferring assets out, which the filing discloses | Red: no independent regulator sight of the balances | **Green** | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 33 (Capital management), F-96/F-97; Note 3, F-20 |

**Verdict: A8-19 Green on the substitute prongs, with the formal yield test recorded Not Applicable (sector).** Neither the Satyam pattern (a large cash pile earning no interest, unconfirmed) nor the Wirecard pattern (cash "in trust" with a third party the auditor never independently confirmed) is present: the majority of the balance is held at central banks, remuneration is disclosed instrument by instrument, and both the financial statements and internal control over financial reporting carry unqualified PCAOB opinions.

## 5. Revenue Quality (A8-15)

The generic tests are adapted to a lender and the adaptation is stated on each line. "Unbilled revenue and contract assets" do not exist here; the closest economic analogue is **interest accrued under the effective-interest method but not yet received in cash**, which is capitalised into the receivable — so that is the ratio computed, and it is labelled as a substitute rather than presented as the template metric.

|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Revenue growth vs cash-taxes-paid growth | Revenue +43.4%; cash tax paid 1,262.5 | Revenue **+37.0%** (11,517.1 → 15,774.7); cash tax paid **+30.0%** (1,262.5 → 1,641.7). Cash tax paid equals **42.4% of pre-tax profit** in FY2025 and rose further to US$2,108.1m over the twelve months to Jun-30-2026 | Red: revenue grows, cash taxes flat | **Green** — cash taxes track revenue closely; fabricated profit does not pay this much tax. This is the Satyam test run in the affirmative | FY2025 Form 20-F, F-6 and Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows; consumed via `earnings/06`, Sections 1 and 3 |
| Collections proxy — cash interest received vs interest income accrued | Cash interest received 5,820.9; collection ratio **68.9%** | Cash interest received **8,440.0** (+45.0%) against interest income of 13,434.7 (+39.5%); collection ratio **70.2%**, and **72.0% in H1'26** — improving for four straight years from 62.5% in FY2023 | Red: collections flat while revenue grows | **Green** — cash collected is growing *faster* than accrued revenue, the opposite of the paper-revenue pattern | Consumed from `earnings/06`, Sections 2 and 3, built from FY2025 Form 20-F Statements of Cash Flows and Note 6 and the Q2'26 interim |
| Accrued-but-uncollected interest, % of revenue *(substitute for unbilled revenue + contract assets — labelled)* | ~22.7% (FY2025: accrued ~12,022.8 less cash received 8,440.0 = ~3,582.8 on revenue 15,774.7) | H1'26: accrued 8,302.8 less cash received 5,976.3 = **2,326.5 = 22.2% of H1 revenue of 10,481.2** | Green <10%; Red >25% or mark-to-model | **Amber** — above the 10% green line and below the 25% red line, **stable rather than rising**, and structural: interest on an instalment loan accrues before it is due, which is how lending works. It is not marked to model — it is contractual interest on amortised-cost assets. Held Amber, not cleared, because gross card receivables overdue at any age rose 11.0% → 12.5% over the same six months | Consumed from `earnings/06`, Sections 3 and 8, built from Q2'26 interim Notes 6 and 7 |
| Order book: contractually binding or MOU-paper? | **N/A — a consumer lender has no order book.** There is no backlog, no MOU-based demand claim, and no mark-to-market revenue recognition. Revenue is contractual interest, interchange and fees on executed transactions; fair-value lines were 6.7% of Q2'26 revenue and shrinking | Red: non-binding MOUs presented as demand | **Not Applicable (business model)** — the Enron mark-to-market and Gensol pre-order patterns have no foothold here | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 6; consumed from `earnings/06`, Section 8 |
| Customer concentration sanity check | — | **No single customer represented 10% or more of revenue** in FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025 | — | Green | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 34(b) |

**Verdict: A8-15 Green overall, with the accrued-interest line held Amber.** Revenue growth of 37.0% is corroborated independently by cash taxes paid (+30.0%) and by cash interest collected (+45.0%) — two things a company cannot fabricate. **RF-ACC-003 does not fire.**

| A8-09 — provisioning adequacy *(the overlay's own priority item)* | Expected-credit-loss allowance ÷ gross credit assets: **15.36% (Dec-24) → 15.37% (Dec-25) → 16.86% (Jun-26)**, i.e. **+149bp in six months** while the book grew 20.6%. ECL charge in the P&L: 2,285.2 (FY2023) → 3,169.0 (FY2024) → 4,204.9 (FY2025). Legal provisions rose 22.6 → 30.9 with additions of 35.8 against reversals of 7.4. Other-receivables ECL was built from US$1.9m to **US$26.3m** in H1'26. **No reserve release flattered earnings in any period examined** | coverage stable vs history and peers | releases funding reported earnings | Building faster than the book | **Green** | `earnings/06`, Sections 3 and 8 (from Q2'26 interim Notes 7, 13, 14 and the Q2'26 deck); FY2025 Form 20-F, F-6, Note 25; Q2'26 interim, Note 16 |

The H1'26 gap to statutory is **30.7 percentage points.** Cash tax paid was 42.4% of pre-tax profit in FY2025 and the current-tax charge was 50.9% of pre-tax profit in the TTM — it is the **deferred** credit that pulls the reported rate down. Cash tax paid ÷ accounting tax charge: **1.65× (FY2025), 6.93× (H1'26)** | near statutory or fully explained | persistently far below, unexplained (the Satyam test) | **Falling fast, in the opposite direction to the statutory rate** | **Amber** — see the reasoning below | FY2025 Form 20-F, F-6/F-7 and Note 30; Q2'26 interim, Statements of Income and Note 30; `earnings/06`, Sections 8 and 10 |

**Why A8-10 is Amber and not Red — the band's own wording decides it.** The red band is "persistently far below statutory **with no credible explanation** — the Satyam test", and the Satyam pattern is fabricated profits that pay no tax. Neither half holds here. First, an explanation exists and is itemised in the audited Note 30 reconciliation, line by line: profits taxed at lower rates in other group entities (US$280.8m in H1'26 against US$56.9m a year earlier), interest-on-capital deductions (US$108.8m against US$38.8m), a CSLL rate-change remeasurement (+US$28.4m), and a bucket of foreign tax credits, non-taxable sovereign-bond interest and tax incentives (US$253.6m against US$99.0m). Second, and decisively for a forensic read, **this company pays a great deal of cash tax**: US$1,641.7m in FY2025 and US$2,108.1m over the twelve months to Jun-30-2026 — 2.7 times the tax charged to the income statement. Fabricated profits do not do that.

**Why it is not Green either, and what would move it.** The gap to statutory is very large and widened by ~14 percentage points in a single half-year; its persistence rests on a **management assertion** — the CFO's "a recurring structural feature of how we operate" — rather than on anything audited as permanent; the deferred credit that produces it is **self-reversing by construction**, arriving only while the provision build outruns tax-deductible write-offs, which is only true while the loan book grows fast (in H1'25 the reverse happened and the line was a net expense); and upstream `04` measured **96.7% of the 12.6% Q2'26 net-income beat as coming from this one line** while pre-tax landed within 0.5% of estimate. The resulting deferred tax asset is US$3,649.1m, **27.5% of equity attributable to the parent**, with recovery on the loss-carryforward slice capped by Brazilian law at 30% of taxable profit a year. That is a durability and recoverability risk sitting in the largest single accounting judgment in these accounts — which is a reason to watch it hard, not evidence of misstatement. **Follow-up:** if the FY2026 effective tax rate stays below ~15% while the loan-book growth rate falls, or if the deferred tax asset passes ~30% of parent equity, this item moves to Red and `RF-ACC-001` should be reconsidered.

## 10. Regulator-Found Divergence (A8-20) — swept per frameworks/GOVERNANCE_DATABASES.md

For a bank this is the most decision-relevant item on the list. The Yes Bank pattern is a supervisor's inspection finding that the reported bad-loan and provisioning numbers were materially understated, disclosed only afterwards. Brazil has no mandatory "divergence disclosure" regime equivalent to the RBI's, so the test is run on the available equivalents: any BACEN, CNBV or SFC supervisory finding or sanction that restated reported numbers; any SEC enforcement action or Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Release; and any lender- or regulator-directed forensic audit. Every lookup is logged, including the nil results.

| Check | Finding | Red band | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Regulator inspection divergence vs reported numbers | **None found.** No BACEN, BANXICO/CNBV or SFC finding restating Nu's reported provisions, credit quality or capital appears in the filings or in the sweep. The prudential conglomerate's regulator-defined capital is disclosed in full and is above every minimum: **regulatory capital US$5,159.4m against a minimum required of US$3,269.9m, an excess margin of US$1,889.6m; CET1 13.0%, Tier 1 14.4%, CAR 16.6%** at Dec-31-2025 (14.7% / 16.2% / 18.1% at Dec-31-2024). Nu Mexico Financiera 15.4% against a 10.5% minimum (19.2% prior year); Nu Colombia 16.9% against 10.5% (22.6% prior year). The Nu Pagamentos-led conglomerate transitioned to BACEN supervisory segment **S2 in July 2025** — a step *up* in supervisory intensity, not a sanction — and from January 2025 operates under the full (post-phase-in) capital requirements | any divergence above the local threshold (India banks: added GNPAs >5% of reported, or provisioning gap >10% of pre-provision profit) | **Green**, with the coverage note that Brazilian supervisory correspondence is not public, so this is a "nothing found across the swept sources" finding, not a proof of absence | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 33, F-96/F-97; Item 4B (regulatory framework); Sweep Log rows 1–4 |
| Lender- or regulator-directed forensic audit | **None found.** No forensic audit, special audit or investigation ordered by any lender, regulator or court is disclosed in the FY2025 20-F, the Q2'26 interim, or the sweep. Provisions and contingent liabilities total **US$30.9m (0.27% of total equity)** across tax, civil and labour risks, with "possible" contingencies of a further US$8.9m — all ordinary-course consumer-credit litigation, none regulatory in nature. No SEC enforcement action, AAER, comment-letter dispute or short-seller accounting allegation surfaced | any (RF-ACC-005) | **Green** | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 25, F-75/F-76; Sweep Log rows 2 and 3 |
| Auditor-side corroboration (read only for what A8-20 needs; auditor calibre belongs to `08`) | KPMG issued an unqualified opinion on the financial statements **and** a separate unqualified opinion that internal control over financial reporting was effective at Dec-31-2025. No material weakness or significant deficiency is reported. The sole Critical Audit Matter is the ECL measurement — precisely the estimate a supervisor would challenge — and the audit response included credit-risk specialists testing PD, EAD and LGD against historical data and comparing the significant-increase-in-credit-risk definition **to applicable industry and regulatory practices** | a divergence the auditor flagged but the company did not disclose | **Green** | FY2025 Form 20-F, Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, F-3 to F-5 |

**`RF-ACC-005` does not fire.**

## 11. Leverage & Advances Hygiene (A14-01, A14-02)

**Basis note (§15).** `balance-sheet-survival/01` is absent, so the debt stack is built here from Note 24 (borrowings and financing), Note 21 (repurchase agreements) and the lease-liability line. Two definitions are used and labelled every time. **"Debt" here means borrowings and financing + repurchase agreements + lease liabilities.** It deliberately EXCLUDES customer deposits (US$45,328.4m at Jun-30-26) and payables to network (US$15,541.7m) — for a bank those are the funding base and the product, not leverage in the governance sense, and treating them as debt would make every deposit-taking institution on earth look insolvent.

| Test | Raw value (basis labelled per §15) | Green band | Red band | Trend | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| A14-01 — net debt / EBITDA (governance lens) | **Net debt/EBITDA is not computable and is meaningless for a financial** — there is no EBITDA line (`ciq_facts.json` `ltm_ebitda_m` = unknown, `net_debt_ebitda_x` = unknown). What is computed instead: **strict-basis net cash of US$7,744.6m at Jun-30-2026** (total debt 5,807.0 = borrowings 4,682.3 + repos 1,058.3 + leases 66.4, less cash and cash equivalents 13,551.6), against **US$9,792.4m strict-basis net cash at Dec-31-2025** and **US$7,120.6m at Dec-31-2024**. Total debt ÷ total equity: 0.27× → 0.46× → 0.44×. Reconciliation to the vendor read: `ciq_facts.json` reports `net_debt_m` −9,274.2 (i.e. net cash) on total debt of 5,896.7 — **CIQ vendor basis, which nets a wider set of liquid investments**; my filing-built total debt of 5,807.0 differs from the vendor's 5,896.7 by US$89.7m, and the vendor's implied cash of 15,170.9 exceeds the filed cash-and-equivalents of 13,551.6, so the two are not interchangeable and the filing figure is the one used (§4/§5). **Governance lens:** the borrowing sits at the regulated operating subsidiaries and funds the loan book — financial bills issued by Nu Financeira (US$2,529.6m) and a margin loan facility at Nu Financeira **collateralised by government securities and sovereign bonds** (US$1,868.6m). **No debt is pledged against controller shares, funds a buyout, or funds a private venture.** The company was in compliance with all financial covenants (the DFC facility for Nu Colombia) at Dec-31-2025 | net cash or <0.5× (§24 Filter 3: net cash = strategic asset) | >3×, or leverage rising to fund promoter objectives | Net cash throughout; debt/equity roughly flat 2025→2026 after a 2025 step-up | **Green** | FY2025 Form 20-F, Notes 21 and 24 (incl. covenants and guarantees), F-9/F-10; Q2'26 interim, Statements of Financial Position; `ciq_facts.json` |
| A14-02 — loans & advances % of total assets | Read on the governance meaning of the item — **advances outside the ordinary lending business**, not the credit book itself (which IS the business). Other receivables, net: **US$1,413.4m (2.83% of assets, Dec-24) → US$1,000.7m (1.34%, Dec-25) → US$849.9m (1.03%, Jun-26)** — falling in absolute terms and as a share for two consecutive periods. Composition disclosed: **credit-card receivables acquired from merchant acquirers, due from card issuers (mainly banks and other financial institutions)**, plus, in 2024, receivables under the Mastercard incentive agreement — arm's-length counterparties, not connected parties. Entire exposure classified **Stage 1 Strong (PD<5%) with no stage transfers in FY2024 or FY2025**, and the ECL against it was nonetheless built from US$1.9m to US$26.3m in H1'26 (conservative, not a release). Related-party balances are a **single US$0.9m other-liability item** (a commercial incentive received from a company where a director is CEO); credit cards and loans to executives, board members and key employees are stated to be on the same terms as unrelated third parties, and are routed to `09` for quantification | <2%, ordinary-course | >5%, rising, or advanced to parties that never repay | Falling | **Green** | FY2025 Form 20-F, Note 16, Note 28, F-9; Q2'26 interim, Note 16 |

## 12. Forensics Read

**The batteries did not run, and that is a sector fact, not a hiding place: for a deposit-funded lender the Beneish M-score and the Dechow F-score measure banking rather than manipulation** — soft assets alone would read 83.6% and trip a red band on every solvent bank in the world — so what stands in their place is the set of tests that do work, and those come back clean on the things that cannot be faked. Revenue grew 37.0% in FY2025 while cash taxes actually paid grew 30.0% to US$1,641.7m and cash interest collected grew 45.0% to US$8,440.0m; the credit-loss allowance was built faster than the book in every period examined (coverage 15.37% → 16.86% in six months, over-90-day coverage 266% → 277%, no release anywhere); goodwill is 3.1% of equity and static; the consolidation perimeter, the accounting policies, the fiscal year-end and the segment presentation have not moved in three years; there has been no restatement; and both the financial statements and internal control over financial reporting carry unqualified PCAOB opinions from an auditor of nine years' standing, whose sole Critical Audit Matter is the credit-loss estimate rather than the existence of cash. **The cash is real:** 57.6% of the US$15,003.6m balance sits on deposit at the central banks of Brazil, Mexico and Colombia, remunerated at 100% of CDI in Brazil with the rate disclosed in the note, none of it "held in trust" by a third party — neither the Satyam nor the Wirecard pattern has a foothold.

**The single worst measured signal is the effective tax rate, and it rhymes with a pattern of earnings that migrate below the operating line rather than with fraud.** The reported rate has fallen 33.04% → 29.45% → 25.77% → 11.78% in H1'26 against a Brazilian statutory rate that *rose* to 42.5% — a 30.7-percentage-point gap — and upstream `04` measured 96.7% of the Q2'26 net-income beat as coming from that one line while pre-tax profit landed within 0.5% of estimate. It is graded **Amber, not Red**, for two reasons stated rather than assumed: the gap is itemised in an audited Note 30 reconciliation, and this company paid US$2,108.1m of cash tax over the last twelve months — 2.7 times the tax charged to the income statement. Fabricated profits do not pay that. What is genuinely at risk is **durability and recoverability**: the deferred credit is self-reversing by construction, arriving only while the provision build outruns tax-deductible write-offs (i.e. only while the loan book grows fast — in H1'25 the line was a net expense), and it has built a US$3,649.1m deferred tax asset now worth 27.5% of parent equity, with recovery on the loss-carryforward slice capped by Brazilian law at 30% of taxable profit a year.

**What a rational minority holder should conclude about the books.** They are not being manipulated on any measure this report could compute, and the balance sheet is conservative where it counts — net cash of US$7,744.6m (strict basis), total debt at 0.44× equity, borrowing that sits at the regulated subsidiaries and is collateralised by government securities rather than by controller shares, non-core advances at 1.03% of assets and falling, and capital ratios above every regulatory minimum in all three countries with no supervisory finding surfacing in the sweep. But roughly 40% of the last twelve months' reported profit is a non-cash tax timing benefit tied to a growth rate and a corporate structure, and a holder should read the reported earnings-per-share as containing that, watch the FY2026 effective tax rate and the loan-book growth rate together, and treat a rate that stays below ~15% while growth decelerates as the point at which this item stops being Amber.
