# Regulatory, Legal & Compliance — NU

**Ticker:** NU (Nu Holdings Ltd.) · **Date:** 2026-09-06 · **Data pool:** `data/NU/` (citation label; all reads resolved through the frozen extract generation `f9081efa…09f2be`)

**Regime (from `00_governance-data-triage.md`, §5A).** Cayman Islands incorporation; US SEC **foreign private issuer** (Form 20-F annual, Form 6-K interim/material events); **NYSE: NU** Class A ordinary shares is the tradable line this report reads. A second line exists — a **BDR Level I programme on B3 (Brazil)**, depositary Banco Bradesco S.A. Operating regulators: **BCB / CMN** and **CVM** (Brazil), **CNBV / Banxico / Condusef** (Mexico), **SFC** (Colombia), plus **SEC / NYSE / PCAOB** at the listed level. Sector overlay: banks / NBFCs.

**Sweep status — the triage cap does NOT bind.** `00` recorded that every network host was denied from its runtime and pre-applied the Score Cap row *"Legal-database sweep did not run → Legal & regulatory risk floor 40; Confidence max 70."* **That cap does not apply to this report.** The company-level sweep RAN from this agent's runtime on 2026-09-06 across BCB sanctioning decisions, CVM, CNBV/SFC, US federal courts, SEC EDGAR, NYSE Regulation, rating-agency and rating-action sources, consumer-regulator sources and dated adverse media — every query logged below. What still did NOT run is named in the Sweep Log and in §9: no paid court-docket terminal (Brazilian TJ/JusBrasil dockets were not searched case-by-case), no certified consolidated sanctions-list query, no public Cayman company register, and the primary BCB decision PDF for the one enforcement hit returned unextractable binary on direct fetch. Those are stated coverage limits inside a sweep that ran — not a filings-only read.

**Disqualifier deference.** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md`, row 6 (Active regulatory enforcement action on financial reporting) = **N**, verbatim: *"No enforcement or investigation touching financial reporting by the SEC, the Brazilian Central Bank (BCB), the CVM, Mexico's CNBV, or any other regulator is disclosed."* That lock is not re-adjudicated here. This report owns the spectrum below it — and it finds one thing the disqualifier scan could not, because the scan reads the filings and this agent reads the regulator's own register.

**Regime translation first (Hard Rule — never flag a structure the regime dictates).** The "quarterly exchange fine file" the A9-06 band contemplates is a **SEBI-LODR instrument**. There is no NYSE equivalent: the NYSE does not publish a quarterly per-issuer fine register. Its equivalent surfaces are (a) the **NYSE Regulation Noncompliant Issuers list** (Below Compliance and Late Filer) and (b) any Section 802.01/802.02 deficiency notice, which a listed company must itself announce. Both were checked.

| Vigil mechanism / whistleblower policy exists | **Yes.** A **Code of Conduct** and a **Global Whistleblower Policy** apply to *"all of our employees, interns, as well as our officers and directors, including our Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and other executive and senior financial officers."* The Policy is stated to *"(i) provide guidelines regarding the whistleblower channel, under the Integrity Program; (ii) encourage the prompt reporting of any suspected violation; (iii) undertake to investigate any good faith report of violations; and (iv) inform our employees, directors, independent directors, apprentices, interns, officers and interested parties about their right to report."* | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 16B — Code of Ethics, p.240` |
| Independent channel | **Yes.** The Ethics Program includes *"an independent Whistleblower Channel"*, covering *"anti-bribery and corruption risks, conflict of interest, related parties, insider trading as well as any violations from Nu's Code of Conduct."* Nu México separately *"maintains a mandatory internal whistleblower system set forth in its Code of Conduct"* | `FY25 Form 20-F, Compliance, Ethics and Anti-Money Laundering section`; `Item 4 — Mexico regulatory` |
| Ombudsperson | **Structurally required, but no ombudsperson is named.** BCB rules require Brazilian institutions to *"create an ombudsman"* and to *"maintain a whistleblower hotline for anonymous reporting of potential illicit activities, with semiannual reports to the board"*; Mexican banks face an equivalent CNBV obligation. The 20-F describes the obligation and the function but **names no individual** — consistent with `00`'s finding that no Chief Compliance Officer and no head of internal audit is named anywhere in the pool | `FY25 Form 20-F, Item 4 — Brazilian regulatory framework; Mexican regulatory framework`; `00_governance-data-triage.md §5E.1 rows 26–27` |
| **Complaint statistics disclosed (received / resolved / pending)** | **No.** No count of whistleblower reports received, substantiated, resolved or pending appears anywhere in the FY25 20-F, in any of the five 20-Fs FY2021–FY2025, or in any interim filing. Searched | Pool grep across `Nu_Holdings_Ltd_-_Form_20-F` FY2021–FY2025, 2026-09-06 — 0 hits for report counts |
| Fraud-alleging complaints and their outcomes | **None disclosed, and none found externally.** No fraud-alleging whistleblower complaint against Nu Holdings surfaced in the sweep | Sweep Log rows 13–15; `07_people-integrity-dossiers.md` §24 Filter-1 buzz sweep, 0 results |

**A9-03 Amber.** The green band requires *mechanism + ombudsperson + complaint statistics disclosed*. Two of three are met: the mechanism is documented and its scope is specific, and the ombudsman function is regulator-mandated and described. **The statistics are simply not there** — and a whistleblower channel whose throughput nobody outside the company can see is a machine you cannot test. That is not a red-band condition (no mechanism absent, no unresolved fraud complaint), so it is Amber, not Red.

**A9-09 Amber.** The red band is *"repeated pollution-board closures, consumer-fraud orders, or product bans"* — **none of those exists**: not one consumer-fraud order, TAC, or penalty has been issued against Nu by any consumer authority in any of the three countries. What does exist is a **large and growing consumer-dispute volume with two live regulator information demands sitting on top of it**, and a civil provision that added US$21.8m in six months. That is above the green band ("none material") and below the red band, which is exactly what Amber is for. The honest read: this is what mass-market consumer banking at 131m customers looks like, and the number to watch is the civil-provision trajectory, not the headline case count.

The single matter that is NOT in the filings is an R$12,500 administrative fine from 2021, and it does not reach any materiality threshold, so it does not fire RF-CMP-001 and does not trigger the undisclosed-matter Score Cap row. **The reconciliation was run both ways** — filings-to-sweep and sweep-to-filings.

## 9. Read

The public record does not contradict this company's filings — it very nearly matches them, which after a real sweep is a finding rather than an absence. Across BCB, CVM, CNBV, SFC, SEC, NYSE and the US federal courts the only thing the regulators know that the filings do not mention is a **R$12,500 Banco Central administrative fine against Nu Pagamentos, decided on 22 October 2021** — five orders of magnitude below any materiality line, and immaterial enough that its non-disclosure is a completeness note rather than a disclosure-integrity breach, though it is enough to stop A9-01 being Green inside the five-year window. Everything the sweep found that is genuinely material, the company had already disclosed first, including the US$2.5 billion Colombian GMF class action it could have buried and instead explained. The compliance machinery is real where it can be tested — five annual filings on time with the margin widening each year, nineteen unbroken quarters of results, no NYSE deficiency notice, two rating upgrades and an AAA.br affirmation with no non-cooperation tag and no withdrawal, and a lender roster headed by the US DFC and the World Bank's IFC — and untested where it cannot: **no whistleblower complaint statistics are disclosed anywhere, and nobody has ever publicly accused this company of anything, so how it treats a critic is unknown.** The single worst legal fact is not a case at all but a trajectory: **32,703 active consumer proceedings and a civil provision that grew 39% in six months to US$30.7m**, with SENACON and Procon-SP information demands sitting on top of it — small money against US$13.3bn of equity, and the exact line that stops being small if consumer-conduct scrutiny in Brazil hardens.

**Verdict: clean record, machinery real — with the caveat that the messenger-response half of the machine has never been switched on.** Nothing here belongs in front of the synthesis as a cap. The triage-anticipated "sweep did not run" floor of 40 does **not** apply, because the sweep ran; what should travel forward instead is the narrower set of things that genuinely could not be checked — Brazilian court dockets case-by-case, a certified sanctions query, the Cayman register, and the conduct alleged in the one BCB fine, whose primary decision document is unreadable.
